As $I_1(y,k)\subset I_2(y,k)$ directly from the definition \eqref{defineij}, it follows by definition \eqref{definei3} that $x\in I_2(y,k)$. By definition \eqref{defineij}, there is $y'\in Y_{k-1}\cap B(y,2D^k)$ with $x\in I_3(y',k-1)$. By induction, $x\in B(y', 4D^{k-1})$. By the triangle inequality applied to the points $x,y',y$ and $D>4$, we conclude $x\in B(y,4D^k)$. This shows the second inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic} and completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Induction setup
nodes.statement: We prove these statements simultaneously by induction on the ordered set of pairs $(y,k)$. Let $-S\le k\le S$.
nodes.statement_short: Simultaneous induction over $(y,k)$

nodes.name: Disjointness j=1
nodes.statement: We first consider \eqref{disji} for $j=1$. If $k=-S$, disjointedness of the sets $I_1(y,-S)$ follows by definition of $I_1$ and $Y_k$. If $k>-S$, assume $x$ is in $I_1(y_m,k)$ for $m=1,2$. Then, for $m=1,2$, there is $z_m\in Y_{k-1}\cap B(y_m,D^k)$ with $x\in I_3(z_m,k-1)$. Using \eqref{disji} inductively for $j=3$, we conclude $z_1=z_2$. This implies that the balls $B(y_1, D^k)$ and $B(y_2, D^k)$ intersect. By construction of $Y_k$, this implies $y_1=y_2$. This proves \eqref{disji} for $j=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness for $j=1$

nodes.name: Disjointness j=3
nodes.statement: We next consider \eqref{disji} for $j=3$. Assume $x$ is in $I_3(y_m,k)$ for $m=1,2$ and $y_m\in Y_k$. If $x$ is in $X_k$, then by definition \eqref{definei3}, $x\in I_1(y_m,k)$ for $m=1,2$. As we have already shown \eqref{disji} for $j=1$, we conclude $y_1=y_2$. This completes the proof in case $x\in X_k$, and we may assume $x$ is not in $X_k$. By definition \eqref{definei3}, $x$ is not in $I_3(z,k)$ for any $z$ with $z<y_1$ or $z<y_2$. Hence, neither $y_1<y_2$ nor $y_2<y_1$, and by totality of the order of $Y_k$, we have $y_1=y_2$. This completes the proof of \eqref{disji} for $j=3$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness for $j=3$

nodes.name: Covering j=2
nodes.statement: We show \eqref{unioni} for $j=2$. In case $k=-S$, this follows from \Cref{cover-big-ball}. Assume $k>-S$. Let $x$ be a point of $B(o, 4D^S-2D^k)$. By induction, there is $y'\in Y_{k-1}$ such that $x\in I_3(y',k-1)$. Using the inductive statement \eqref{squeezedyadic}, we obtain $x\in B(y',4D^{k-1})$. As $D>4$, by applying the triangle inequality with the points, $o$, $x$, and $y'$, we obtain that $y'\in B(o, 4D^S-D^k)$. By \Cref{cover-big-ball}, $y'$ is in $B(y,2D^k)$ for some $y\in Y_k$. It follows that $x\in I_2(y,k)$. This proves \eqref{unioni} for $j=2$.
nodes.statement_short: Covering for $j=2$ via the cover big ball lemma

nodes.name: Covering j=3
nodes.statement: We show \eqref{unioni} for $j=3$. Let $x\in B(o, 4D^S-2D^k)$. In case $x\in X_k$, then by definition of $X_k$ we have $x\in I_1(y,k)$ for some $y\in Y_k$ and thus $x\in I_3(y,k)$. We may thus assume $x\not\in X_k$. As we have already seen \eqref{unioni} for $j=2$, there is $y\in Y_k$ such that $x\in I_2(y,k)$. We may assume this $y$ is minimal with respect to the order in $Y_k$. Then $x\in I_3(y,k)$. This proves \eqref{unioni} for $j=3$.
nodes.statement_short: Covering for $j=3$ via a minimal centre

nodes.name: First inclusion
nodes.statement: Next, we show the first inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic}. Let $x\in B(y,\frac 12 D^k)$. As $I_1(y,k)\subset I_3(y,k)$, it suffices to show $x\in I_1(y,k)$. If $k=-S$, this follows immediately from the assumption on $x$ and the definition of $I_1$. Assume $k>-S$. By the inductive statement \eqref{unioni} and $D>4$, there is a $y'\in Y_{k-1}$ such that $x\in I_3(y',k-1)$. By the inductive statement \eqref{squeezedyadic}, we conclude $x\in B(y',4D^{k-1})$. By the triangle inequality with points $x$, $y$, $y'$, and $D\geq8$, we have $y'\in B(y,D^k)$. It follows by definition \eqref{defineij} that $I_3(y',k-1)\subset I_1(y,k)$, and thus $x\in I_3(y,k)$. This proves the first inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic}.
nodes.statement_short: Inner ball inclusion $B(y,\frac12D^k)\subset I_3(y,k)$

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Let $x\in B(y,\frac 12 D^k)$. As $I_1(y,k)\subset I_3(y,k)$, it suffices to show $x\in I_1(y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $x\in I_1(y,k)$

nodes.name: Base scale
nodes.statement: If $k=-S$, this follows immediately from the assumption on $x$ and the definition of $I_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Bottom scale case

nodes.name: Higher scale
nodes.statement: Assume $k>-S$. By the inductive statement \eqref{unioni} and $D>4$, there is a $y'\in Y_{k-1}$ such that $x\in I_3(y',k-1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Higher scale: find a previous-scale cube containing $x$

nodes.name: Centre location
nodes.statement: By the inductive statement \eqref{squeezedyadic}, we conclude $x\in B(y',4D^{k-1})$. By the triangle inequality with points $x$, $y$, $y'$, and $D\geq8$, we have $y'\in B(y,D^k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Locate its centre near $y$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: It follows by definition \eqref{defineij} that $I_3(y',k-1)\subset I_1(y,k)$, and thus $x\in I_3(y,k)$. This proves the first inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic}.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $x\in I_1(y,k)\subset I_3(y,k)$

nodes.name: Second inclusion
nodes.statement: We show the second inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic}. Let $x\in I_3(y,k)$. As $I_1(y,k)\subset I_2(y,k)$ directly from the definition \eqref{defineij}, it follows by definition \eqref{definei3} that $x\in I_2(y,k)$. By definition \eqref{defineij}, there is $y'\in Y_{k-1}\cap B(y,2D^k)$ with $x\in I_3(y',k-1)$. By induction, $x\in B(y', 4D^{k-1})$. By the triangle inequality applied to the points $x,y',y$ and $D>4$, we conclude $x\in B(y,4D^k)$. This shows the second inclusion in \eqref{squeezedyadic} and completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Outer ball inclusion by induction and the triangle inequality

nodes.name: cover by cubes
nodes.statement_short: Each cube $I_3(y,k)$ is covered by the cubes of any lower scale $l$.
nodes.statement: Let $-S\le l\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$. We have \begin{equation} I_3(y,k)\subset \bigcup_{y'\in Y_l} I_3(y',l)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: cover-by-cubes

nodes.name: Covering by lower-scale cubes
nodes.statement: I_3(y,k)\subset \bigcup_{y'\in Y_l} I_3(y',l)\, .
nodes.label: 3coverdyadic

nodes.name: Proof of the cover by cubes lemma
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k-l$ using the recursive definitions of $I_3$ and $I_j$.
nodes.statement: Let $-S\le l\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$. If $l=k$, the inclusion \eqref{3coverdyadic} is true from the definition of set union. We may then assume inductively that $k>l$ and the statement of the lemma is true if $k$ is replaced by $k-1$. Let $x\in I_3(y,k)$. By definition \eqref{definei3}, $x\in I_j(y,k)$ for some $j\in \{1,2\}$. By \eqref{defineij}, $x\in I_3(w,k-1)$ for some $w\in Y_{k-1}$. We conclude \eqref{3coverdyadic} by induction.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement_short: Base case $l=k$

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: We may then assume inductively that $k>l$ and the statement of the lemma is true if $k$ is replaced by $k-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive hypothesis for $k-1$

nodes.name: Unfold definitions
nodes.statement:
Let $x\in I_3(y,k)$.
    By definition \eqref{definei3}, $x\in I_j(y,k)$
    for some $j\in \{1,2\}$. By \eqref{defineij},
    $x\in I_3(w,k-1)$ for some $w\in Y_{k-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definitions to find a cube of scale $k-1$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We conclude \eqref{3coverdyadic} by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the hypothesis

nodes.name: dyadic property
nodes.statement_short: Intersecting cubes are nested: the lower-scale cube is contained in the higher-scale one.
assumptions: Let $-S\le l\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$ and $y'\in Y_l$ with $I_3(y',l)\cap I_3(y,k)\neq \emptyset$
nodes.statement: Let $-S\le l\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$ and $y'\in Y_l$ with $I_3(y',l)\cap I_3(y,k)\neq \emptyset$. Then \begin{equation} I_3(y',l)\subset I_3(y,k). \end{equation}
nodes.label: dyadic-property

nodes.name: Nesting of intersecting cubes
nodes.statement: I_3(y',l)\subset I_3(y,k).
nodes.label: 3dyadicproperty

nodes.name: Proof of the dyadic property lemma
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$: same scale by disjointness; otherwise pass through a scale-$(k-1)$ cube and split on whether $x\in X_k$.
nodes.statement:
Let $l,k,y,y'$ be as in the lemma. Pick $x\in I_3(y',l)\cap I_3(y,k)$. Assume first $l=k$. By \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we conclude $y'=y$, and thus \eqref{3dyadicproperty}. Now assume $l<k$. By induction, we may assume that the statement of the lemma is proven for $k-1$ in place of $k$. By \Cref{cover-by-cubes}, there is a $y''\in Y_{k-1}$ such that $x\in I_3(y'',k-1)$. By induction, we have $I_3(y',l)\subset I_3(y'',k-1)$. It remains to prove  egin{equation} I_3(y'',k-1)\subset I_3(y,k). \end{equation} We make a case distinction and assume first $x\in X_k$. By Definition \eqref{definei3}, we have $x\in I_1(y,k)$. By Definition \eqref{defineij}, there is a $v\in Y_{k-1}\cap B(y,D^k)$ with $x\in I_3(v,k-1)$. By \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we have $v=y''$. By Definition \eqref{defineij}, we then have $I_3(y'',k-1)\subset I_1(y,k)$. Then \eqref{wyclaim} follows by Definition \eqref{definei3} in the given case. Assume now the case $x
otin X_k$. By \eqref{definei3}, we have $x\in I_2(y,k)$. Moreover, for any $u<y$ in $Y_k$, we have $x
ot\in I_3(u,k)$. Let $u<y$. By transitivity of the order in $Y_k$, we conclude $x
ot \in I_2(u,k)$. By \eqref{defineij} and the disjointedness property of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we have $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_2(u,k)= \emptyset$. Similarly, $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_1(u,k)= \emptyset$. Hence $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_3(u,k)=\emptyset$. As $u<y$ was arbitrary, we conclude with \eqref{definei3} the claim in the given case. This completes the proof of \eqref{wyclaim}, and thus also \eqref{3dyadicproperty}.

nodes.name: Fix point
nodes.statement: Let $l,k,y,y'$ be as in the lemma. Pick $x\in I_3(y',l)\cap I_3(y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a common point $x$

nodes.name: Same scale
nodes.statement: Assume first $l=k$. By \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we conclude $y'=y$, and thus \eqref{3dyadicproperty}.
nodes.statement_short: Same scale: equal centres by disjointness

nodes.name: Different scales
nodes.statement: Now assume $l<k$. By induction, we may assume that the statement of the lemma is proven for $k-1$ in place of $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower scale: induction on $k$

nodes.name: Intermediate cube
nodes.statement: By \Cref{cover-by-cubes}, there is a $y''\in Y_{k-1}$ such that $x\in I_3(y'',k-1)$. By induction, we have $I_3(y',l)\subset I_3(y'',k-1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass through a scale-$(k-1)$ cube

nodes.name: Remaining claim
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to (wyclaim)

nodes.name: Intermediate inclusion (wyclaim)
nodes.statement: I_3(y'',k-1)\subset I_3(y,k).
nodes.label: wyclaim

nodes.name: Case in X_k
nodes.statement: We make a case distinction and assume first $x\in X_k$. By Definition \eqref{definei3}, we have $x\in I_1(y,k)$. By Definition \eqref{defineij}, there is a $v\in Y_{k-1}\cap B(y,D^k)$ with $x\in I_3(v,k-1)$. By \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we have $v=y''$. By Definition \eqref{defineij}, we then have $I_3(y'',k-1)\subset I_1(y,k)$. Then \eqref{wyclaim} follows by Definition \eqref{definei3} in the given case.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x\in X_k$

nodes.name: Case not in X_k
nodes.statement:
Assume now the case $x
otin X_k$. By \eqref{definei3}, we have $x\in I_2(y,k)$. Moreover, for any $u<y$ in $Y_k$, we have $x
ot\in I_3(u,k)$. Let $u<y$. By transitivity of the order in $Y_k$, we conclude $x
ot \in I_2(u,k)$. By \eqref{defineij} and the disjointedness property of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}, we have $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_2(u,k)= \emptyset$. Similarly, $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_1(u,k)= \emptyset$. Hence $I_3(y'',k-1)\cap I_3(u,k)=\emptyset$. As $u<y$ was arbitrary, we conclude with \eqref{definei3} the claim in the given case. This completes the proof of \eqref{wyclaim}, and thus also \eqref{3dyadicproperty}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $x\notin X_k$

nodes.name: Boundary relation $(y',k'|y,k)$
nodes.statement:
For $-S\le k'\le k\le S$ and $y'\in Y_{k'}$, $y\in Y_k$
write $(y',k'|y,k)$ if $I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)$ and
\begin{equation} \inf_{x\in X\setminus I_3(y,k)}\rho(y',x)<6D^{k'}\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $(y',k'|y,k)$: $I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)$ and $y'$ lies within $6D^{k'}$ of the complement of $I_3(y,k)$.

nodes.name: Boundary condition (bdcond)
nodes.statement: \inf_{x\in X\setminus I_3(y,k)}\rho(y',x)<6D^{k'}\, .
nodes.label: bdcond

nodes.name: transitive boundary
nodes.statement_short: The boundary relation passes to intermediate scales of a nested chain of cubes.
assumptions: $-S\le k''< k'< k\le S$ and $y''\in Y_{k''}$, $y'\in Y_{k'}$, $y\in Y_k$
there is $x\in X$ such that \begin{equation} x\in I_3(y'',k'')\cap I_3(y',k')\cap I_3(y,k)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement: Assume $-S\le k''< k'< k\le S$ and $y''\in Y_{k''}$, $y'\in Y_{k'}$, $y\in Y_k$. Assume there is $x\in X$ such that \begin{equation} x\in I_3(y'',k'')\cap I_3(y',k')\cap I_3(y,k)\, . \end{equation} If $(y'',k''|y,k)$, the also $(y'',k''|y',k')$ and $(y',k'|y,k)$
nodes.label: transitive-boundary

nodes.name: Common point of three cubes
nodes.statement: x\in I_3(y'',k'')\cap I_3(y',k')\cap I_3(y,k)\, .

nodes.name: Proof of the transitive boundary lemma
nodes.statement_short: Nesting from the dyadic property and a triangle inequality estimate of the distance to the complement.
nodes.statement: As $x\in I_3(y'',k'')\cap I_3(y',k')$ and $k''< k'$, we have by \Cref{dyadic-property} that $I_3(y'',k'')\subset I_3(y',k')$. Similarly, $I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)$. Pick $x'\in X\setminus I_3(y,k)$ such that \begin{equation} \rho(y'',x')< 6D^{k''}\, , \end{equation} which exists as $(y'',k''|y,k)$. As $x'\in X\setminus I_3(y',k')$ as well, we conclude $(y'',k''| y',k')$. By the triangle inequality, we have \begin{equation} \rho(y',x')\le \rho(y',x)+\rho(x,y'')+\rho(y'',x') \end{equation} Using the choice of $x$ and \eqref{squeezedyadic} as well as \eqref{yppxp}, we estimate this by \begin{equation} < 4D^{k'}+4D^{k''}+6D^{k''}\le 6D^{k'}\, , \end{equation} where we have used $D>5$ and $k''<k'$. We conclude $(y',k'|y,k)$.

nodes.name: Nesting
nodes.statement:
As $x\in I_3(y'',k'')\cap I_3(y',k')$ and $k''< k'$, we have by \Cref{dyadic-property} that
    $I_3(y'',k'')\subset I_3(y',k')$. Similarly,
    $I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Nesting by the dyadic property

nodes.name: Outside point
nodes.statement:
Pick $x'\in X\setminus I_3(y,k)$ such that
    \begin{equation} \rho(y'',x')< 6D^{k''}\, ,
    \end{equation}
    which exists as $(y'',k''|y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a nearby point outside $I_3(y,k)$

nodes.name: First relation
nodes.statement:
As
    $x'\in X\setminus I_3(y',k')$ as well, we conclude
    $(y'',k''| y',k')$.
nodes.statement_short: First relation

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for $\rho(y',x')$
nodes.statement: \rho(y',x')\le \rho(y',x)+\rho(x,y'')+\rho(y'',x')

nodes.name: Distance bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound the distance by $6D^{k'}$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We conclude $(y',k'|y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Second relation

nodes.name: small boundary
nodes.statement_short: The cubes $K$ scales below that touch the boundary of $I_3(y,k)$ carry at most half of its measure.
nodes.statement: Let $K = 2^{4a+1}$. For each $-S+K\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{z\in Y_{k-K}: (z,k-K|y,k)}\mu(I_3(z,k-K)) \le \frac 12 \mu(I_3(y,k))\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: small-boundary

nodes.name: Small boundary estimate
nodes.statement: \sum_{z\in Y_{k-K}: (z,k-K|y,k)}\mu(I_3(z,k-K)) \le \frac 12 \mu(I_3(y,k))\,.
nodes.label: new-small-boundary

nodes.name: Proof of the small boundary lemma
nodes.statement_short: Compare boundary cubes across the $K$ intermediate scales, sum the disjoint inner balls inside $I_3(y,k)$, and use $K=2^{4a+1}$. Key step: disjointness of the balls by a contradiction with the boundary relation.
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be as in the lemma. Let $-S+K\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$. Pick $k'$ so that $k-K\le k'\le k$. For each $y''\in Y_{k-K}$ with $(y'',k-K| y,k)$, by \Cref{cover-by-cubes} and \Cref{dyadic-property}, there is a unique $y'\in Y_{k'}$ such that \begin{equation} I_3(y'',k-K)\subset I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)\, . \end{equation} Using \Cref{transitive-boundary}, $(y',k'|y,k)$. We conclude using the disjointedness property of \Cref{basic-grid-structure} that \begin{equation} \sum_{y'': (y'',k-K|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-K)) \le \sum_{y': (y',k'|y,k)} \mu(I_3(y',k')) \, . \end{equation} Adding over $k-K<k'\le k$, and using \[\mu(I_3(y',k'))\le 2^{4a} \mu(B(y', \frac 14 D^{k'}))\] from the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} and \eqref{squeezedyadic} gives \begin{equation} K\sum_{y'': (y'',k-K|y,k)} \mu(I_3(y'',k-K)) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{4a} \sum_{k-K<k'\le k} \left[ \sum_{y': (y',k'|y,k)} \mu(B(y', \frac 14 D^{k'}))\right] \end{equation} Each ball $B(y', \frac 14 D^{k'})$ occurring in \eqref{sumcompare1} is contained in $I_3(y',k')$ by \eqref{squeezedyadic} and in turn contained in $I_3(y,k)$ by \eqref{4.31}. Assume for the moment all these balls are pairwise disjoint. Then by additivity of the measure, \begin{equation} K\sum_{y'': (y'',k-K|y,k)} \mu(I_3(y'',k-K)) \le 2^{4a} \mu(I_3(y,k))\, \end{equation} which by $K=2^{4a+1}$ implies \eqref{new-small-boundary}. It thus remains to prove that the balls occurring in \eqref{sumcompare1} are pairwise disjoint. Let $(u,l)$ and $(u',l')$ be two parameter pairs occurring in the sum of \eqref{sumcompare1} and let $ B(u, \frac 14 D^l)$ and $B({u'}, \frac 14 D^{l'})$ be the corresponding balls. If $l=l'$, then the balls are equal or disjoint by \eqref{squeezedyadic} and \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}. Assume then without loss of generality that $l'<l$. Towards a contradiction, assume that \begin{equation} B(u, \frac 14 D^l)\cap B({u'}, \frac 14 D^{l'})\neq \emptyset \end{equation} As $(u',l'|y,k)$, there is a point $x$ in $X\setminus I_3(y,k)$ with $\rho(x,u')<6D^{l'}$. Using $D>25$, we conclude from the triangle inequality and \eqref{bulbul} that $x\in B(u,\frac 12D^l)$. However, $B(u,\frac 12 D^l)\subset I_3(u,l)$, and $I_3(u,l)\subset I_3(y,k)$, a contradiction to $x\not\in I_3(y,k)$. This proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Fix data
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be as in the lemma. Let $-S+K\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $K$, $k$, $y$

nodes.name: Intermediate cubes
nodes.statement:
Pick $k'$ so that $k-K\le k'\le k$.
For each $y''\in Y_{k-K}$ with $(y'',k-K| y,k)$,
by \Cref{cover-by-cubes} and \Cref{dyadic-property}, there is a unique $y'\in Y_{k'}$ such that
\begin{equation} I_3(y'',k-K)\subset I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)\, .
\end{equation}
Using \Cref{transitive-boundary}, $(y',k'|y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Each boundary cube lies in a boundary cube of scale $k'$

nodes.name: Intermediate cube nesting (4.31)
nodes.statement: I_3(y'',k-K)\subset I_3(y',k')\subset I_3(y,k)\, .

nodes.name: Scale comparison
nodes.statement:
We conclude using the disjointedness property of
\Cref{basic-grid-structure} that
\begin{equation} \sum_{y'': (y'',k-K|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-K))
   \le
\sum_{y': (y',k'|y,k)}
\mu(I_3(y',k')) \, .
   \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compare sums across scales

nodes.name: Sum over scales
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $K$ scales and bound by inner balls

nodes.name: Bound by inner balls
nodes.statement: \le 2^{4a} \sum_{k-K<k'\le k} \left[ \sum_{y': (y',k'|y,k)} \mu(B(y', \frac 14 D^{k'}))\right]
nodes.label: sumcompare1

nodes.name: Containment
nodes.statement:
Each ball $B(y', \frac 14 D^{k'})$ occurring in
\eqref{sumcompare1} is contained in $I_3(y',k')$
by \eqref{squeezedyadic} and in turn contained in
$I_3(y,k)$ by \eqref{4.31}.
nodes.statement_short: The inner balls lie in $I_3(y,k)$

nodes.name: Conditional conclusion
nodes.statement_short: If disjoint, additivity gives the bound

nodes.name: Remaining claim
nodes.statement:
It thus remains to prove that the balls
occurring in
\eqref{sumcompare1} are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to disjointness of the balls

nodes.name: Two balls
nodes.statement:
Let $(u,l)$ and $(u',l')$ be two parameter pairs occurring
in the sum of \eqref{sumcompare1} and let
$ B(u, \frac 14 D^l)$ and $B({u'}, \frac 14 D^{l'})$
be the corresponding balls.
nodes.statement_short: Take two balls

nodes.name: Same scale
nodes.statement:
If
$l=l'$, then the balls are equal or disjoint by
\eqref{squeezedyadic} and \eqref{disji} of \Cref{basic-grid-structure}.
nodes.statement_short: Same scale: equal or disjoint

nodes.name: Contradiction hypothesis
nodes.statement_short: Different scales: assume they intersect

nodes.name: Intersecting balls hypothesis (bulbul)
nodes.statement: B(u, \frac 14 D^l)\cap B({u'}, \frac 14 D^{l'})\neq \emptyset
nodes.label: bulbul

nodes.name: Outside point
nodes.statement:
As $(u',l'|y,k)$, there is a point $x$ in
$X\setminus I_3(y,k)$ with $\rho(x,u')<6D^{l'}$.
nodes.statement_short: A nearby point outside $I_3(y,k)$

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement:
Using $D>25$, we conclude from the triangle inequality and \eqref{bulbul} that
$x\in B(u,\frac 12D^l)$. However, $B(u,\frac 12 D^l)\subset I_3(u,l)$,
and $I_3(u,l)\subset I_3(y,k)$, a contradiction to
$x\not\in I_3(y,k)$.
This proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The point lies in $I_3(y,k)$, a contradiction

nodes.name: smaller boundary
nodes.statement_short: Boundary cubes $nK$ scales below carry at most a $2^{-n}$ fraction of the measure of $I_3(y,k)$.
nodes.statement: Let $K = 2^{4a+1}$ and let $n\ge 0$ be an integer. Then for each $-S+nK\le k\le S$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{y'\in Y_{k-nK}: (y',k-nK|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y',k-nK)) \le 2^{-n} \mu(I_3(y,k))\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: smaller-boundary

nodes.name: Smaller boundary estimate
nodes.statement: \sum_{y'\in Y_{k-nK}: (y',k-nK|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y',k-nK)) \le 2^{-n} \mu(I_3(y,k))\,.
nodes.label: very-new-small

nodes.name: Proof of the smaller boundary lemma
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$, iterating the small boundary lemma.
nodes.statement: We prove this by induction on $n$. If $n=0$, both sides of \eqref{very-new-small} are equal to $\mu(I_3(y,k))$ by \eqref{disji}. If $n=1$, this follows from \Cref{small-boundary}. Assume $n>1$ and \eqref{very-new-small} has been proven for $n-1$. We write \eqref{very-new-small} \begin{equation} \sum_{y''\in Y_{k-nK}: (y'',k-nK|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-nK)) \end{equation} \begin{equation} = \sum_{y'\in Y_{k-K}:(y',k-K|y,k)} \left[ \sum_{y''\in Y_{k-nK}: (y'',k-nK|y',k-K)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-nK)) \right] \end{equation} Applying the induction hypothesis, this is bounded by \begin{equation} = \sum_{y'\in Y_{k-K}:(y',k-K|y,k)} 2^{1-n}\mu(I_3(y',k-K)) \end{equation} Applying \eqref{new-small-boundary} gives \eqref{very-new-small}, and proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Induction setup
nodes.statement: We prove this by induction on $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$

nodes.name: Base case n=0
nodes.statement:
If $n=0$,
    both sides of \eqref{very-new-small} are equal to
    $\mu(I_3(y,k))$ by \eqref{disji}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $n=0$

nodes.name: Base case n=1
nodes.statement: If $n=1$, this follows from \Cref{small-boundary}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $n=1$ is the small boundary lemma

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: Assume $n>1$ and \eqref{very-new-small} has been proven for $n-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive hypothesis

nodes.name: Regroup
nodes.statement_short: Regroup the sum by scale-$(k-K)$ cubes

nodes.name: Boundary sum at scale $k-nK$
nodes.statement: \sum_{y''\in Y_{k-nK}: (y'',k-nK|y,k)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-nK))

nodes.name: Regrouped boundary sum
nodes.statement: = \sum_{y'\in Y_{k-K}:(y',k-K|y,k)} \left[ \sum_{y''\in Y_{k-nK}: (y'',k-nK|y',k-K)}\mu(I_3(y'',k-nK)) \right]

nodes.name: Apply hypothesis
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inductive hypothesis

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Applying \eqref{new-small-boundary} gives
    \eqref{very-new-small}, and proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the small boundary estimate

nodes.name: boundary measure
nodes.statement_short: The $tD^k$-neighbourhood of the boundary inside $I_3(y,k)$ has measure at most $2t^\kappa\mu(I_3(y,k))$.
assumptions: For each $-S\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$ and $0<t<1$ with $tD^k\ge D^{-S}$
conclusions: \mu(\{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}) \le 2 t^\kappa \mu(I_3(y,k))\,.
nodes.statement: For each $-S\le k\le S$ and $y\in Y_k$ and $0<t<1$ with $tD^k\ge D^{-S}$ we have \begin{equation} \mu(\{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}) \le 2 t^\kappa \mu(I_3(y,k))\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: boundary-measure

nodes.name: Small boundary measure estimate (old-small-boundary)
nodes.statement: \mu(\{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}) \le 2 t^\kappa \mu(I_3(y,k))\,.
nodes.label: old-small-boundary

nodes.name: Proof of the boundary measure lemma
nodes.statement_short: Cover the boundary layer by cubes of scale $k-nK$ in boundary relation with $I_3(y,k)$ and apply the smaller boundary lemma with $n$ chosen from $t$.
nodes.statement: Let $x\in I_3(y,k)$ with $\rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}$. Let $K = 2^{4a+1}$ as in \Cref{smaller-boundary}. Let $n$ be the largest integer such that $D^{nK} \le \frac{1}{t}$, so that $tD^k \le D^{k-nK}$ and \begin{equation} D^{nK} > \frac{1}{tD^K}\,. \end{equation} Let $k' = k - nK$, by the assumption $tD^k \ge D^{-S}$, we have $k' \ge -S$. By \eqref{3coverdyadic}, there exists $y' \in Y_{k'}$ with $x \in I_3(y',k')$. By the squeezing property \eqref{squeezedyadic} and the assumption on $x$, we have $$ \rho(y', X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \le \rho(x,y') + \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \le 4 D^{k'} + t D^{k}\,. $$ By the assumption on $n$ and the definition of $k'$, this is $$ \le 4D^{k'} + D^{k - nK} < 6D^{k'}\,. $$ Together with \eqref{3dyadicproperty} thus $(y',k'|y,k)$. We have shown that $$ \{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\} $$ $$ \subset \bigcup_{y'\in Y_{k-nK}: (y',k-nK|y,k)}I_3(y',k-nK)\,. $$ Using monotonicity and additivity of the measure and \Cref{smaller-boundary}, we obtain $$ \mu(\{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}) \le 2^{-n} \mu(I_3(y,k))\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-n-size} and the definition \eqref{defineD} of $D$, this is bounded by $$ 2 t^{1/(100a^2 K)} \mu(I_3(y,k))\,, $$ which completes the proof by the definition \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$.

nodes.name: Fix data
nodes.statement: Let $x\in I_3(y,k)$ with $\rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}$. Let $K = 2^{4a+1}$ as in \Cref{smaller-boundary}.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a boundary-layer point and $K$

nodes.name: Choose n
nodes.statement:
Let $n$ be the largest integer such that
$D^{nK} \le \frac{1}{t}$, so that $tD^k \le D^{k-nK}$ and
\begin{equation} D^{nK} > \frac{1}{tD^K}\,.
\end{equation}
Let $k' = k - nK$, by the assumption $tD^k \ge D^{-S}$, we have $k' \ge -S$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $n$ and $k'=k-nK$

nodes.name: Size of $D^{nK}$ (eq-n-size)
nodes.statement: D^{nK} > \frac{1}{tD^K}\,.
nodes.label: eq-n-size

nodes.name: Cube at k'
nodes.statement: By \eqref{3coverdyadic}, there exists $y' \in Y_{k'}$ with $x \in I_3(y',k')$.
nodes.statement_short: Find a scale-$k'$ cube containing $x$

nodes.name: Distance bound
nodes.statement:
By the squeezing property \eqref{squeezedyadic} and the assumption on $x$, we have
$$
    \rho(y', X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \le \rho(x,y') + \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \le 4 D^{k'} + t D^{k}\,.
$$
By the assumption on $n$ and the definition of $k'$, this is
$$
    \le 4D^{k'} + D^{k - nK} < 6D^{k'}\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Its centre is within $6D^{k'}$ of the complement

nodes.name: Boundary relation
nodes.statement: Together with \eqref{3dyadicproperty} thus $(y',k'|y,k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary relation holds

nodes.name: Covering
nodes.statement:
We have shown that
$$
    \{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}
$$
$$
    \subset \bigcup_{y'\in Y_{k-nK}: (y',k-nK|y,k)}I_3(y',k-nK)\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Boundary layer is covered by boundary cubes

nodes.name: Apply lemma
nodes.statement:
Using monotonicity and additivity of the measure and \Cref{smaller-boundary}, we obtain
$$
    \mu(\{x \in I_3(y,k) \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus I_3(y,k)) \leq t D^{k}\}) \le 2^{-n} \mu(I_3(y,k))\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the smaller boundary lemma

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-n-size} and the definition \eqref{defineD} of $D$, this is bounded by
$$
    2 t^{1/(100a^2 K)}  \mu(I_3(y,k))\,,
$$
which completes the proof by the definition \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Convert $2^{-n}$ into $2t^\kappa$

nodes.name: Collection $\tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ of all cubes
nodes.statement:
Let $\tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ be the set of all $I_3(y,k)$ with $k\in [-S,S]$ and
$y\in Y_k$.

nodes.name: Scale and centre functions $s$, $c$ of the constructed cubes
Grid $\mathcal{D}$ of cubes inside $I_3(o,S)$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathcal{D}$ to be the set of all $I \in \tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ such that $I \subset I_3(o, S)$.

nodes.name: Proof of the grid existence lemma
nodes.statement_short: Verify the grid structure axioms for $\tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ (covering and nesting by minimal counterexamples, size and boundary from the previous lemmas) and restrict to $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement:
We first show that $(	ilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ satisfies properties \eqref{coverdyadic}, \eqref{dyadicproperty}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{eq-small-boundary}. Property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} follows from \eqref{squeezedyadic}, while \eqref{eq-small-boundary} follows from \Cref{boundary-measure}. Let $x\in B(o, D^S)$. We show properties \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty} for $(	ilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ and $x$. We first show \eqref{coverdyadic} for $(	ilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ by contradiction. Then there is an $I$ violating the conclusion of \eqref{coverdyadic}. Pick such $I=I_3(y,l)$ such that $l$ is minimal. {By assumption, we have $-S\le k<l$; in particular $-S<l$}. By definition, $I_3(y, l)$ is contained in $I_1(y, l)\cup I_2(y, l)$, which is contained in the union of $I_3(y',l-1)$ with $y'\in Y_{l-1}$. By minimality of $l$, each such $I_3(y',l-1)$ is contained in the union of all $I_3(z,k)$ with $z\in Y_k$. This proves \eqref{coverdyadic}. We now show \eqref{dyadicproperty} for $(	ilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$. Assume to get a contradiction that there are non-disjoint $I, J\in 	ilde{\mathcal{D}}$ with $s(I)\le s(J)$ and $I 
ot \subset J$. We may assume the existence of such $I$ and $J$ with minimal $s(J)-s(I)$. Let $k=s(I)$. Assume first $s(J)=k$. Let $I=I_3(y_1,k)$ and $J=I_3(y_2,k)$ with $y_1,y_2\in Y_k$. If $y_1=y_2$, then $I=J$, a contradiction to $I
ot \subset J$. If $y_1
eq y_2$, then $I\cap J=\emptyset$ by \eqref{disji}, a contradiction to the non-disjointedness of $I,J$. Assume now $s(J)>k$. Choose $y\in I\cap J$. By property \eqref{coverdyadic}, there is $K\in 	ilde{\mathcal{D}}$ with $s(K)=s(J)-1$ and $y\in K$. By construction of $J$, and pairwise disjointedness of all $I_3(w,s(J)-1)$ that we have already seen, we have $K\subset J$. By minimality of $s(J)$, we have $I\subset K$. This proves $I\subset J$ and thus \eqref{dyadicproperty}. Now note that properties \eqref{dyadicproperty}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{eq-small-boundary} immediately carry over to $(\mathcal{D},c, s)$ by restriction. \eqref{subsetmaxcube} is true for $(\mathcal{D}, c, s)$ by definition, and \eqref{coverdyadic} follows from \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty} for $(	ilde{\mathcal{D}}, c, s)$.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: We first show that $(\tilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ satisfies properties \eqref{coverdyadic}, \eqref{dyadicproperty}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{eq-small-boundary}.
nodes.statement_short: First treat $\tilde{\mathcal{D}}$

nodes.name: Size and boundary
nodes.statement:
Property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}
follows from \eqref{squeezedyadic}, while \eqref{eq-small-boundary} follows from \Cref{boundary-measure}.
nodes.statement_short: Size and small boundary properties from the squeezing and boundary measure lemmas

nodes.name: Fix point
nodes.statement:
Let $x\in B(o, D^S)$.
We show properties
\eqref{coverdyadic} and
\eqref{dyadicproperty}
for $(\tilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ and $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $x$ for covering and nesting

nodes.name: Covering
nodes.statement:
We first show \eqref{coverdyadic} for $(\tilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$ by contradiction. Then there is an $I$ violating the conclusion of
\eqref{coverdyadic}. Pick such $I=I_3(y,l)$ such that $l$ is minimal.
{By assumption, we have $-S\le k<l$; in particular $-S<l$}.
By definition, $I_3(y, l)$ is contained in $I_1(y, l)\cup I_2(y, l)$, which is contained in the union of $I_3(y',l-1)$ with $y'\in Y_{l-1}$.
By minimality of $l$, each such $I_3(y',l-1)$ is contained in the union of
all $I_3(z,k)$ with $z\in Y_k$. This proves \eqref{coverdyadic}.
nodes.statement_short: Covering property via a minimal-scale counterexample

nodes.name: Nesting
nodes.statement:
We now show \eqref{dyadicproperty} for $(\tilde{\mathcal{D}},c,s)$. Assume to get a contradiction that
there are non-disjoint $I, J\in \tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ with $s(I)\le s(J)$
and $I \not \subset J$. We may assume the existence of such $I$ and $J$ with minimal
$s(J)-s(I)$. Let $k=s(I)$. Assume first $s(J)=k$. Let $I=I_3(y_1,k)$ and $J=I_3(y_2,k)$ with $y_1,y_2\in Y_k$.
If $y_1=y_2$, then $I=J$, a contradiction to $I\not \subset J$.
If $y_1\neq y_2$, then $I\cap J=\emptyset$ by \eqref{disji}, a contradiction to the non-disjointedness of $I,J$.
Assume now $s(J)>k$. Choose $y\in I\cap J$. By property \eqref{coverdyadic},
there is $K\in \tilde{\mathcal{D}}$ with $s(K)=s(J)-1$ and $y\in K$. By construction
of $J$, and pairwise disjointedness of all $I_3(w,s(J)-1)$ that we have already seen,
we have $K\subset J$. By minimality of $s(J)$, we have $I\subset K$.
This proves $I\subset J$ and thus \eqref{dyadicproperty}.
nodes.statement_short: Nesting property via a minimal scale-gap counterexample

nodes.name: Restriction
nodes.statement: Now note that properties \eqref{dyadicproperty}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{eq-small-boundary} immediately carry over to $(\mathcal{D},c, s)$ by restriction. \eqref{subsetmaxcube} is true for $(\mathcal{D}, c, s)$ by definition, and \eqref{coverdyadic} follows from \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty} for $(\tilde{\mathcal{D}}, c, s)$.
nodes.statement_short: The properties pass to $\mathcal{D}$ by restriction

nodes.name: Maximal frequency separated set $\mathcal{Z}(I)$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{Z}(I)\subset Q(X)$: a maximal set of frequencies whose $0.3$-balls in $d_{I^\circ}$ are disjoint on $Q(X)$.

nodes.name: Frequency set $\mathcal{Z}\subset Q(X)$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{Z} \subset {Q}(X)
nodes.label: eq-tile-Z

nodes.name: Disjoint $0.3$-balls
nodes.statement: B_{I^\circ}({\vartheta}, 0.3) \cap B_{I^\circ}({\theta}, 0.3) \cap {Q}(X) = \emptyset\,.
nodes.label: eq-tile-disjoint-Z

nodes.name: frequency ball cover
nodes.statement_short: The $0.7$-balls around $\mathcal{Z}(I)$ cover $Q(X)$.
nodes.statement: For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, we have \begin{equation} {Q}(X) \subset \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: frequency-ball-cover

nodes.name: Covering of $Q(X)$ (eq-tile-cover)
nodes.statement: {Q}(X) \subset \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)\,.
nodes.label: eq-tile-cover

nodes.name: Proof of the frequency ball cover lemma
nodes.statement_short: Maximality of $\mathcal{Z}(I)$ plus the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement: Let ${\theta} \in \bigcup_{{\vartheta} \in {Q}(X)} B_{I^\circ}({\vartheta}, 1)$. By maximality of $\mathcal{Z}(I)$, there must be a point $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ such that $B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \cap B_{I^\circ}({\theta}, 0.3) \ne \emptyset$. Else, $\mathcal{Z}(I) \cup \{{\theta}\}$ would be a set of larger cardinality than $\mathcal{Z}(I)$ satisfying \eqref{eq-tile-Z} and \eqref{eq-tile-disjoint-Z}. Fix such $z$, and fix a point $z_1 \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \cap B_{I^\circ}({\theta}, 0.3)$. By the triangle inequality, we deduce that $$ d_{I^\circ}(z,{\theta}) \le d_{I^\circ}(z,z_1) + d_{I^\circ}({\theta}, z_1) < 0.3 + 0.3 = 0.6\,, $$ and hence ${\theta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)$.

nodes.name: Maximality
nodes.statement: Let ${\theta} \in \bigcup_{{\vartheta} \in {Q}(X)} B_{I^\circ}({\vartheta}, 1)$. By maximality of $\mathcal{Z}(I)$, there must be a point $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ such that $B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \cap B_{I^\circ}({\theta}, 0.3) \ne \emptyset$. Else, $\mathcal{Z}(I) \cup \{{\theta}\}$ would be a set of larger cardinality than $\mathcal{Z}(I)$ satisfying \eqref{eq-tile-Z} and \eqref{eq-tile-disjoint-Z}.
nodes.statement_short: Maximality gives an overlapping $0.3$-ball

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Fix such $z$, and fix a point $z_1 \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \cap B_{I^\circ}({\theta}, 0.3)$. By the triangle inequality, we deduce that
    $$
        d_{I^\circ}(z,{\theta}) \le d_{I^\circ}(z,z_1) + d_{I^\circ}({\theta}, z_1) < 0.3 + 0.3 = 0.6\,,
    $$
    and hence ${\theta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives distance $<0.6$

nodes.name: Tiles $\mathfrak P$ and maps $\mathcal{I}$, $\mathcal{Q}$
nodes.statement:
We define
$$
    {\mathfrak P} = \{(I, z) \ : \ I \in \mathcal{D}, z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)\}\,,
$$
$${\mathcal{I}}((I, z)) = I\qquad \text{and} \qquad {\mathcal{Q}}((I, z)) = z.$$

nodes.name: Tile scale and centre ${\mathrm{s}}$, ${\mathrm{c}}$
nodes.statement: We further set $${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})),\qquad \qquad {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}) = c({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})).$$

nodes.name: Tile centre and scale properties hold
nodes.statement: Then \eqref{tilecenter}, \eqref{tilescale} hold by definition.

nodes.name: Enumeration $z_1,\dots,z_M$ of $\mathcal{Z}(I)$
nodes.statement:
For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, we pick an enumeration of the finite set $\mathcal{Z}(I)$
$$
    \mathcal{Z}(I) = \{z_1, \dotsc, z_M\}\,.
$$

nodes.name: Auxiliary frequency cubes $\Omega_1$
nodes.statement:
We define {$\Omega_1:{\mathfrak P} \mapsto \mathcal{P}({\Theta}) $ as below}. Set
$$
    \Omega_1((I, z_1)) = B_{I^\circ}(z_1, 0.7) \setminus \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)\setminus \{z_1\}} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3)
$$
and then define iteratively
\begin{equation} \Omega_1((I, z_k)) = B_{I^\circ}(z_k, 0.7) \setminus \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I) \setminus \{z_k\}} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{k-1} \Omega_1((I, z_i))\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega_1((I,z_k))$: the $0.7$-ball around $z_k$ minus the other $0.3$-balls and the earlier $\Omega_1((I,z_i))$.

nodes.name: Recursive definition of $\Omega_1$
nodes.statement: \Omega_1((I, z_k)) = B_{I^\circ}(z_k, 0.7) \setminus \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I) \setminus \{z_k\}} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3) \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{k-1} \Omega_1((I, z_i))\,.
nodes.label: eq-def-omega1

nodes.name: disjoint frequency cubes
nodes.statement_short: The sets $\Omega_1(\mathfrak p)$ for tiles over one cube are pairwise disjoint.
assumptions: For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, and ${\mathfrak p}_1, {\mathfrak p}_2\in {\mathfrak P}(I)$
nodes.statement: For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, and ${\mathfrak p}_1, {\mathfrak p}_2\in {\mathfrak P}(I)$, if $$\Omega_1({\mathfrak p}_1)\cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}_2)\neq \emptyset,$$ then ${\mathfrak p}_1={\mathfrak p}_2$.
nodes.label: disjoint-frequency-cubes

nodes.name: Proof of the disjoint frequency cubes lemma
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the recursive definition of $\Omega_1$, which removes earlier sets.
nodes.statement: By the definition of the map ${\mathcal{I}}$, we have $$ {\mathfrak P}(I) = \{(I, z) \, : \, z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)\}\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, the set $\Omega_1((I, z_k))$ is disjoint from each $\Omega_1((I, z_i))$ with $i < k$. Thus the sets $\Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$, ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ are pairwise disjoint.

nodes.name: Tiles over I
nodes.statement:
By the definition of the map ${\mathcal{I}}$, we have
    $$
        {\mathfrak P}(I) = \{(I, z) \, : \, z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)\}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Describe $\mathfrak P(I)$

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, the set $\Omega_1((I, z_k))$ is disjoint from each $\Omega_1((I, z_i))$ with $i < k$. Thus the sets $\Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$, ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.statement_short: The recursive definition removes earlier sets

nodes.name: frequency cube cover
nodes.statement_short: The sets $\Omega_1(\mathfrak p)$ cover the $0.7$-balls and are squeezed between the $0.3$- and $0.7$-balls around $\mathcal{Q}(\mathfrak p)$.
conclusions: B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.3) \subset \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7)\,.
B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.3) \subset \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7)\,.

nodes.statement: For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, it holds that \begin{equation} \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)\subset \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)} \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})\,. \end{equation} For every ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, it holds that \begin{equation} B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.3) \subset \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: frequency-cube-cover

nodes.name: Covering by $\Omega_1$ (eq-omega1-cover)
nodes.statement: \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)\subset \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)} \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})\,.
nodes.label: eq-omega1-cover

nodes.name: Squeezing of $\Omega_1(\mathfrak p)$ (eq-omega1-incl)
nodes.statement: B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.3) \subset \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7)\,.
nodes.label: eq-omega1-incl

nodes.name: Proof of the frequency cube cover lemma
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the recursive definition of $\Omega_1$; for the covering, split on whether the frequency lies in some $0.3$-ball.
nodes.statement: For \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} let ${\mathfrak p} = (I, z)$. The second inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} then follows from \eqref{eq-def-omega1} and the equality $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7) = B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)$, which is true by definition. For the first inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} let ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),0.3)$. Let $k$ be such that $z = z_k$ in the enumeration we chose above. It follows immediately from \eqref{eq-def-omega1} and \eqref{eq-tile-disjoint-Z} that ${\vartheta} \notin \Omega_1((I, z_i))$ for all $i < k$. Thus, again from \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, we have ${\vartheta} \in \Omega_1((I,z_k))$. To show \eqref{eq-omega1-cover} let ${\vartheta} \in \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z,0.7)$. If there exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z,0.3)$, then $$ z \in \Omega_1((I, z)) \subset \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)} \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}) $$ by the first inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}. Now suppose that there exists no $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3)$. Let $k$ be minimal such that ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z_k, 0.7)$. Since $\Omega_1((I, z_i)) \subset B_{I^\circ}(z_i, 0.7)$ for each $i$ by \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, we have that ${\vartheta} \notin \Omega_1((I, z_i))$ for all $i < k$. Hence ${\vartheta} \in \Omega_1((I, z_k))$, again by \eqref{eq-def-omega1}.

nodes.name: Second inclusion
nodes.statement:
For \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} let ${\mathfrak p} = (I, z)$.
    The second inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} then follows from \eqref{eq-def-omega1} and the equality $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7) = B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.7)$, which is true by definition.
nodes.statement_short: Second inclusion from the definition

nodes.name: First inclusion
nodes.statement:
For the first inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} let ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),0.3)$. Let $k$ be such that $z = z_k$ in the enumeration we chose above. It follows immediately from \eqref{eq-def-omega1} and \eqref{eq-tile-disjoint-Z} that
    ${\vartheta} \notin \Omega_1((I, z_i))$ for all $i < k$. Thus, again from \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, we have
    ${\vartheta} \in \Omega_1((I,z_k))$.
nodes.statement_short: First inclusion from the separation of $\mathcal{Z}(I)$

nodes.name: Case in 0.3-ball
nodes.statement:
To show \eqref{eq-omega1-cover} let ${\vartheta} \in \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)} B_{I^\circ}(z,0.7)$.
    If there exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z,0.3)$, then
    $$
        z \in \Omega_1((I, z)) \subset \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)} \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})
    $$
    by the first inclusion in \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}.
nodes.statement_short: Case: frequency in some $0.3$-ball

nodes.name: Case otherwise
nodes.statement: Now suppose that there exists no $z \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z, 0.3)$. Let $k$ be minimal such that ${\vartheta} \in B_{I^\circ}(z_k, 0.7)$. Since $\Omega_1((I, z_i)) \subset B_{I^\circ}(z_i, 0.7)$ for each $i$ by \eqref{eq-def-omega1}, we have that ${\vartheta} \notin \Omega_1((I, z_i))$ for all $i < k$. Hence ${\vartheta} \in \Omega_1((I, z_k))$, again by \eqref{eq-def-omega1}.
nodes.statement_short: Case: otherwise take the minimal $k$

nodes.name: Frequency cubes $\Omega$
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega=\Omega_1$ on the top cube; below, $\Omega(\mathfrak p)$ is the union of the $\Omega$ of the parent cube's tiles with frequency in $\Omega_1(\mathfrak p)$, plus a $0.2$-ball.

nodes.name: $\Omega$ on the top cube
nodes.statement: {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})\,.
nodes.label: eq-max-omega

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the minimal parent cube
nodes.statement: This $J$ is unique:

nodes.name: Proof of uniqueness of the minimal parent cube
nodes.statement: Suppose that $J'$ is another inclusion minimal cube with $I \subset J'$ and $I \ne J'$. Without loss of generality, we have that $s(J) \le s(J')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, it follows that $J \subset J'$. Since $J'$ is minimal with respect to inclusion, it follows that $J = J'$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $s(J)\le s(J')$; nesting gives $J\subset J'$ and minimality gives equality.

nodes.name: Recursive definition of $\Omega$
nodes.statement: {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = \bigcup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})} \Omega((J, z)) \cup B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),0.2)\,.
nodes.label: eq-it-omega

nodes.name: Proof of the tile structure lemma
nodes.statement_short: Induction down the tree of cubes from $I_0$, verifying the frequency ball inclusion, disjoint cover and nesting properties of $\Omega$. Key step: the four-case analysis for disjointness using the metric comparison $d_{I^\circ}\le 2^{-95a}d_{J^\circ}$.
nodes.statement:
First, we prove \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. If $I =I_0$, then \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ by \eqref{eq-max-omega} and \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}. Now suppose that $I$ is not maximal in $\mathcal{D}$ with respect to set inclusion. Then we may assume by induction that for all $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$ and all ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds. Let $J$ be the unique minimal cube in $\mathcal{D}$ with $I \subsetneq J$. Suppose that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega({\mathfrak p})$. If ${\vartheta}\in B_{{\mathfrak p}}(\mathcal{Q}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)$, then since  egin{equation*} B_{{\mathfrak p}}(\mathcal{Q}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)\subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}(\mathcal{Q}({\mathfrak p}), 1)\, , \end{equation*} we conclude that ${\vartheta}\in B_{{\mathfrak p}}(\mathcal{Q}({\mathfrak p}), 0.7)$. If not, by \eqref{eq-it-omega}, there exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z)$. Using the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}, we obtain $$ d_{I^\circ}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),{\vartheta}) \le d_{I^\circ}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), z) + d_{I^\circ}(z, {\vartheta}) \le 0.7 + d_{I^\circ}(z, {\vartheta})\,. $$ By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the induction hypothesis, this is estimated by $$ \le 0.7 + 2^{-95a} d_{J^\circ}(z,{\vartheta}) \le 0.7 + 2^{-95a}\cdot 1 < 1\,. $$ This shows the second inclusion in \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. The first inclusion is immediate from \eqref{eq-it-omega}. Next, we show \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. Let $I \in \mathcal{D}$. If $I = I_0$, then disjointedness of the sets ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ follows from the definition \eqref{eq-max-omega} and \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}. To obtain the inclusion in \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} one combines the inclusions \eqref{eq-tile-cover} and \eqref{eq-omega1-cover} of \Cref{frequency-cube-cover} with \eqref{eq-max-omega}. Now we turn to the case where there exists $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$ and $I
e J$. In this case we use induction: It suffices to show \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} under the assumption that it holds for all cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$. As shown before definition \eqref{eq-it-omega}, we may choose the unique inclusion minimal such $J$. To show disjointedness of the sets ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ we pick two tiles ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ and ${\vartheta} \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. Then we are by \eqref{eq-it-omega} in one of the following four cases. 1. There exist $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J, z)$, and there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J, z')$. By the induction hypothesis, that \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} holds for $J$, we must have $z = z'$. By \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}, we must then have ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$. 2. There exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z)$, and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)$. Using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, we obtain $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),z) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}(z, {\vartheta}) \le 0.2 + 2^{-95a} \cdot 1 < 0.3\,. $$ Thus $z \in \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ by \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}. By \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}, it follows that ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$. 3. There exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z')$, and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)$. This case is the same as case 2., after swapping ${\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathfrak p}'$. 4. We have ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)$. In this case it follows that ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$ since the sets $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)$ are pairwise disjoint by the inclusion \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} and \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}. To show the inclusion in \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, let ${\vartheta} \in {Q}(X)$. By the induction hypothesis, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega({\mathfrak p})$. By definition of the set ${\mathfrak P}$, we have ${\mathfrak p} = (J, z)$ for some $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J)$. Thus, by \eqref{eq-tile-cover}, there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with $z \in B_{I^\circ}(z', 0.7)$. Then by Lemma \eqref{frequency-cube-cover} there exists ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ with $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$. Consequently, by \eqref{eq-it-omega}, ${\vartheta} \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. Finally, we show \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}. Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) 
e \emptyset$. If we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \ge {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})$, then it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $I = J$, thus ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$. By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} we have then either ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) = \emptyset$ or ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = {\Omega}({\mathfrak q})$. By the assumption in \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) 
e \emptyset$, so we must have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = {\Omega}({\mathfrak q})$ and in particular ${\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$. So it remains to show \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} under the additional assumption that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) > {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. In this case, we argue by induction on ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - 1$ and $J \cap{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) 
e \emptyset$. We pick one such $J$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset J \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$. Thus, by \eqref{eq-tile-cover}, there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J)$ with ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}) \in B_{J^\circ}(z', 0.7)$. Then by \Cref{frequency-cube-cover} there exists ${\mathfrak q}' \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$ with ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}) \in\Omega_1({\mathfrak q}')$. By \eqref{eq-it-omega}, it follows that $\Omega({\mathfrak q}) \subset \Omega({\mathfrak q}')$. Note that then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q}')$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}') 
e \emptyset$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}') - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) - 1$. Thus, we have by the induction hypothesis that $\Omega({\mathfrak q}') \subset \Omega({\mathfrak p})$. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Ball inclusions
nodes.statement: First, we prove \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. If $I =I_0$, then \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ by \eqref{eq-max-omega} and \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}. Now suppose that $I$ is not maximal in $\mathcal{D}$ with respect to set inclusion. Then we may assume by induction that for all $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$ and all ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds. Let $J$ be the unique minimal cube in $\mathcal{D}$ with $I \subsetneq J$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the ball inclusions, by induction from the top cube

nodes.name: Top cube
nodes.statement: If $I =I_0$, then \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ by \eqref{eq-max-omega} and \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}.
nodes.statement_short: Top cube case

nodes.name: Inductive case
nodes.statement: Now suppose that $I$ is not maximal in $\mathcal{D}$ with respect to set inclusion. Then we may assume by induction that for all $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$ and all ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} holds. Let $J$ be the unique minimal cube in $\mathcal{D}$ with $I \subsetneq J$.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive hypothesis for the parent cube $J$

nodes.name: Small ball case
nodes.statement_short: Case: $\vartheta$ in the $0.2$-ball

nodes.name: Inherited case
nodes.statement:
If not, by \eqref{eq-it-omega}, there exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z)$. Using the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}, we obtain
    $$
        d_{I^\circ}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),{\vartheta}) \le d_{I^\circ}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), z) + d_{I^\circ}(z, {\vartheta}) \le 0.7 + d_{I^\circ}(z, {\vartheta})\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Case: $\vartheta\in\Omega(J,z)$, triangle inequality

nodes.name: Metric comparison
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the induction hypothesis, this is estimated by
    $$
        \le 0.7 + 2^{-95a} d_{J^\circ}(z,{\vartheta}) \le 0.7 + 2^{-95a}\cdot 1 < 1\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Metric comparison across scales

nodes.name: Inclusions done
nodes.statement: This shows the second inclusion in \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. The first inclusion is immediate from \eqref{eq-it-omega}.
nodes.statement_short: Both inclusions hold

nodes.name: Disjoint cover
nodes.statement: Next, we show \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. Let $I \in \mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: Turn to the disjoint cover property

nodes.name: Top cube
nodes.statement:
If $I = I_0$, then disjointedness of the sets ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ follows from the definition \eqref{eq-max-omega} and \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}. To obtain the inclusion in \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} one combines the inclusions \eqref{eq-tile-cover} and \eqref{eq-omega1-cover}
    of \Cref{frequency-cube-cover} with \eqref{eq-max-omega}.
nodes.statement_short: Top cube case

nodes.name: Inductive case
nodes.statement:
Now we turn to the case where there exists $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$ and $I\ne J$. In this case we use induction: It suffices to show \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} under the assumption that it holds for all cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $I \subset J$. As shown before definition \eqref{eq-it-omega}, we may choose the unique inclusion minimal such $J$. To show disjointedness of the sets ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ we pick two tiles ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ and ${\vartheta} \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$.
    Then we are by \eqref{eq-it-omega} in one of the following four cases.
nodes.statement_short: Non-top cube: induction, four cases for disjointness

nodes.name: Case 1
nodes.statement: 1. There exist $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J, z)$, and there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J, z')$. By the induction hypothesis, that \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} holds for $J$, we must have $z = z'$. By \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}, we must then have ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Both inherited

nodes.name: Case 2
nodes.statement:
2. There exists $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p})$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z)$, and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)$. Using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, we obtain
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),z) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}(z, {\vartheta}) \le 0.2 + 2^{-95a} \cdot 1 < 0.3\,.
    $$
    Thus $z \in \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ by \eqref{eq-omega1-incl}. By \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}, it follows that ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Inherited and small ball

nodes.name: Case 3
nodes.statement: 3. There exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega(J,z')$, and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)$. This case is the same as case 2., after swapping ${\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric to case 2

nodes.name: Case 4
nodes.statement: 4. We have ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)$. In this case it follows that ${\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}'$ since the sets $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 0.2)$ are pairwise disjoint by the inclusion \eqref{eq-omega1-incl} and \Cref{disjoint-frequency-cubes}.
nodes.statement_short: Both small balls

nodes.name: Cover
nodes.statement:
To show the inclusion in \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, let ${\vartheta} \in {Q}(X)$. By the induction hypothesis, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$ such that ${\vartheta} \in \Omega({\mathfrak p})$. By definition of the set ${\mathfrak P}$, we have ${\mathfrak p} = (J, z)$ for some $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J)$.
    Thus, by \eqref{eq-tile-cover}, there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(I)$ with $z \in B_{I^\circ}(z', 0.7)$. Then by Lemma \eqref{frequency-cube-cover} there exists ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ with $z \in \mathcal{Z}(J) \cap \Omega_1({\mathfrak p}')$. Consequently, by \eqref{eq-it-omega}, ${\vartheta} \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. This completes the proof of \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}.
nodes.statement_short: Covering of $Q(X)$ by induction and the frequency cube cover lemma

nodes.name: Nesting, equal scales
nodes.statement: Finally, we show \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}. Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) \ne \emptyset$. If we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \ge {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})$, then it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $I = J$, thus ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$. By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} we have then either ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) = \emptyset$ or ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = {\Omega}({\mathfrak q})$. By the assumption in \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) \ne \emptyset$, so we must have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) = {\Omega}({\mathfrak q})$ and in particular ${\Omega}({\mathfrak q}) \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: Nesting property: equal scales

nodes.name: Nesting, induction
nodes.statement: So it remains to show \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} under the additional assumption that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) > {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. In this case, we argue by induction on ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - 1$ and $J \cap{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne \emptyset$. We pick one such $J$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset J \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$.
nodes.statement_short: Different scales: induction on the scale gap via an intermediate cube

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Thus, by \eqref{eq-tile-cover}, there exists $z' \in \mathcal{Z}(J)$ with ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}) \in B_{J^\circ}(z', 0.7)$. Then by \Cref{frequency-cube-cover} there exists ${\mathfrak q}' \in {\mathfrak P}(J)$ with ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}) \in\Omega_1({\mathfrak q}')$.
    By \eqref{eq-it-omega}, it follows that $\Omega({\mathfrak q}) \subset \Omega({\mathfrak q}')$. Note that then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q}')$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak q}') \ne \emptyset$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}') - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) - 1$. Thus, we have by the induction hypothesis that $\Omega({\mathfrak q}') \subset \Omega({\mathfrak p})$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Pass through a tile over the intermediate cube and apply the hypothesis

nodes.name: set C(G,k) of dyadic cubes
nodes.statement:
Define
$\mathcal{C}(G,k)$ to be the set of $I\in \mathcal{D}$
such that there exists a $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with $I\subset J$
and
\begin{equation} {\mu(G \cap J)} > 2^{-k-1}{\mu(J)}\, ,
\end{equation}
but there does not exist a $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with $I\subset J$ and
\begin{equation} {\mu(G \cap J)} > 2^{-k}{\mu(J)}\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: C(G,k): dyadic cubes contained in some cube with G-density above 2^{-k-1} but in none with density above 2^{-k}.

nodes.name: tiles P(k)
nodes.statement_short: P(k): tiles whose cube lies in C(G,k).

nodes.name: definition of P(k)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak P}(k)=\{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P} \ : \ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\in \mathcal{C}(G,k)\}
nodes.label: eq-defPk

nodes.name: maximal dense tiles M(k,n)
nodes.statement:
Define $ {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n)$ to be the set of ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ such that
 \begin{equation} \mu({E_1}({\mathfrak p})) > 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))
 \end{equation}
and there does not exist ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ with
${\mathfrak p}'\neq {\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathfrak p}\le {\mathfrak p}'$ such that
 \begin{equation} \mu({E_1}({\mathfrak p}')) > 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')).
 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: M(k,n): tiles of P(k) with E_1-density above 2^{-n} that are maximal with this property.

nodes.name: E_1 density condition (ebardense)
nodes.statement: \mu({E_1}({\mathfrak p})) > 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))
nodes.label: ebardense

nodes.name: maximality condition (mnkmax)
nodes.statement: \mu({E_1}({\mathfrak p}')) > 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')).
nodes.label: mnkmax

nodes.name: density dens_k'
nodes.statement_short: dens_k'(P'): sup over p' in P', lambda>=2 of lambda^{-a} times the E_2 density of tiles p in P(k) with lambda p' <~ lambda p.

nodes.name: definition of dens_k'
nodes.statement: \operatorname{dens}_k' ({\mathfrak P}'):= \sup_{{\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'}\sup_{\lambda \geq 2} \lambda^{-a} \sup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k): \lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))}\,.
nodes.label: eq-densdef

nodes.name: density class C(k,n)
nodes.statement:
Sorting by density, we define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}(k,n):=\{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}(k) \ : \
    2^{4a}2^{-n}< \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le
    2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\}\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: C(k,n): tiles of P(k) whose dens_k' lies in (2^{4a-n}, 2^{4a-n+1}].

nodes.name: definition of C(k,n)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}(k,n):=\{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}(k) \ : \ 2^{4a}2^{-n}< \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\}\,.
nodes.label: def-cnk

nodes.name: B(p), C_1(k,n,j) and L_0(k,n)
nodes.statement_short: B(p): maximal tiles m with 100p <~ m; C_1(k,n,j): tiles with |B(p)| in [2^j,2^{j+1}); L_0(k,n): tiles with B(p) empty.

nodes.name: definition of B(p)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}) := \{ \mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n) \ : \ 100 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}\}
nodes.label: defbfp

nodes.name: definition of C_1(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) := \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n) \ : \ 2^{j} \leq |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| < 2^{j+1}\}\,.
nodes.label: defcnkj

nodes.name: definition of L_0(k,n)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) := \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n) \ : \ |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| <1\}\,.
nodes.label: defl0nk

nodes.name: minimal layers L_1(k,n,j,l)
nodes.statement_short: L_1(k,n,j,l): recursively, the minimal elements of C_1(k,n,j) after removing earlier layers.

nodes.name: symbol L_1(k,n,j,l)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)
nodes.label: eq-L1-def

nodes.name: remaining set for minimal layers
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)\setminus \bigcup_{0\le l'<l} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')\, .

nodes.name: C_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement_short: C_2(k,n,j): C_1(k,n,j) with the minimal layers removed.

nodes.name: definition of C_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j):= {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)\setminus \bigcup_{0\le l'\le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')\, .
nodes.label: eq-C2-def

nodes.name: prospective tree tops U_1(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)
\end{equation}
to be the set of all
${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ such that
for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$
with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ strictly contained in
${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ we have $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),100) = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: U_1(k,n,j): tiles u of C_1(k,n,j) whose 100-ball is disjoint from that of every tile of C_1 with strictly larger cube.

nodes.name: symbol U_1(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)
nodes.label: defunkj

nodes.name: L_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)
\end{equation}
to be the set of all ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$ such that there
does not exist
${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$
with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and $2{\mathfrak p}\lesssim {\mathfrak u}$.
nodes.statement_short: L_2(k,n,j): tiles of C_2(k,n,j) not 2-dominated by any prospective tree top with a different cube.

nodes.name: symbol L_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)
nodes.label: eq-L2-def

nodes.name: C_3(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)
  \setminus {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: C_3(k,n,j) = C_2(k,n,j) minus L_2(k,n,j).

nodes.name: definition of C_3(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j) \setminus {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)\, .
nodes.label: eq-C3-def

nodes.name: maximal layers L_3(k,n,j,l)
nodes.statement_short: L_3(k,n,j,l): recursively, the maximal elements of C_3(k,n,j) after removing earlier layers.

nodes.name: symbol L_3(k,n,j,l)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)
nodes.label: eq-L3-def

nodes.name: remaining set for maximal layers
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{0 \le l' < l} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l')\,.

nodes.name: C_4(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)
  \setminus \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: C_4(k,n,j): C_3(k,n,j) with the maximal layers removed.

nodes.name: definition of C_4(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)\,.
nodes.label: eq-C4-def

nodes.name: boundary cubes L(u)
nodes.statement_short: L(u): cubes I inside I(u) of scale s(u)-Z(n+1)-1 whose ball B(c(I),8D^{s(I)}) is not contained in I(u).

nodes.name: symbol L(u)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})
nodes.label: eq-L-def

nodes.name: boundary condition on cube I
nodes.statement: B(c(I), 8 D^{s(I)})\not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})\, .

nodes.name: L_4(k,n,j) and C_5(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)
\end{equation}
to be the set of all ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ such that there exists
${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$
with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset \bigcup \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})$, and define
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)
  \setminus {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: L_4: tiles of C_4 whose cube lies in the boundary cubes L(u) of some tree top; C_5 = C_4 minus L_4.

nodes.name: symbol L_4(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)
nodes.label: eq-L4-def

nodes.name: definition of C_5(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j):={\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j) \setminus {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)\, .
nodes.label: defc5

nodes.name: tiles P_{F,G}
nodes.statement_short: P_{F,G}: tiles whose dens_2 exceeds 2^{2a+5} mu(F)/mu(G).

nodes.name: density threshold for P_{F,G}
nodes.statement: \operatorname{dens}_2(\{{\mathfrak p}\})> 2^{2a+5}\frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,.

nodes.name: first exceptional set G_1
definition of G_1
nodes.statement: G_1:=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} }{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, .
nodes.label: definegone

nodes.name: overlap set A(lambda,k,n) and second exceptional set G_2
nodes.statement_short: A(lambda,k,n): points covered by more than lambda 2^{n+1} cubes of M(k,n); G_2 = union of A(2n+6,k,n).

nodes.name: overlap condition defining A(lambda,k,n)
nodes.statement: \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)}\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(x)>\lambda 2^{n+1}
nodes.label: eq-Aoverlap-def

nodes.name: definition of G_2
nodes.statement: G_2:= \bigcup_{k\ge 0}\bigcup_{k\le n} A(2n+6,k,n)\, .
nodes.label: definegone2

nodes.name: third exceptional set G_3
nodes.statement_short: G_3: union of the cubes of all tiles in the boundary layers L_4(k,n,j).

nodes.name: definition of G_3
nodes.statement: G_3 := \bigcup_{k\ge 0}\, \bigcup_{n \geq k}\, \bigcup_{0\le j\le 2n+3} \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4 (k,n,j)} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, .
nodes.label: defineg3

nodes.name: exceptional set G'
nodes.statement: Define $G'=G_1\cup G_2 \cup G_3$.

nodes.name: Exceptional Sets Lemma
nodes.statement_short: The exceptional set G' has at most half the measure of G.
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \mu(G')\le 2^{-1}\mu(G)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: exceptional-set

nodes.name: Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: The tiles of P_1 (union of the C_5(k,n,j)) give an operator bounded on G minus G' by 2^{441a^3}/(q-1)^4 mu(G)^{1-1/q} mu(F)^{1/q}.
conclusions: \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_1} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \right|\, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{441a^3}}{(q-1)^4} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} {\mathfrak P}_1 =\bigcup_{k\ge 0}\bigcup_{n\ge k} \bigcup_{0\le j\le 2n+3}{\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j) \end{equation} For all $f:X\to \mathbb{C}$ with $|f|\le \mathbf{1}_F$ we have \begin{equation} \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_1} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \right|\, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{441a^3}}{(q-1)^4} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: forest-union

nodes.name: definition of P_1
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak P}_1 =\bigcup_{k\ge 0}\bigcup_{n\ge k} \bigcup_{0\le j\le 2n+3}{\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)

nodes.name: forest union estimate
nodes.statement: \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_1} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \right|\, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{441a^3}}{(q-1)^4} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\,.
nodes.label: disclesssim1

nodes.name: Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.statement_short: The tiles of P_2 = P minus P_1 give an operator bounded on G minus G' by 2^{120a^3}/(q-1)^5 mu(G)^{1-1/q} mu(F)^{1/q}.
conclusions: \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{120a^3}}{(q-1)^5} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} {\mathfrak P}_2 ={\mathfrak P}\setminus {\mathfrak P}_1\,. \end{equation} For all $f:X\to \mathbb{C}$ with $|f|\le \mathbf{1}_F$ we have \begin{equation} \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{120a^3}}{(q-1)^5} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: forest-complement

nodes.name: definition of P_2
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak P}_2 ={\mathfrak P}\setminus {\mathfrak P}_1\,.

nodes.name: forest complement estimate
nodes.statement: \int_{G \setminus G'} \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \frac{2^{120a^3}}{(q-1)^5} \mu(G)^{1 - \frac{1}{q}} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}}\,.
nodes.label: disclesssim2

nodes.name: Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality over the splitting P = P_1 + P_2, using the Forest Union and Forest Complement Lemmas and the bound on G'.
nodes.statement: \Cref{discrete-Carleson} follows by applying the triangle inequality to \eqref{disclesssim} according to the splitting in \Cref{forest-union} and \Cref{forest-complement} and using both Lemmas as well as the bound on the set $G'$ given by \Cref{exceptional-set}.

nodes.name: first exception lemma
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \mu(G_1)\le 2^{-5}\mu(G)\, . \end{equation}

nodes.label: first-exception

nodes.name: bound on G_1

nodes.name: Proof of first exception lemma
nodes.statement_short: Cover G_1 by dense balls around tiles of P_{F,G} and apply the Vitali covering lemma to 1_F.
nodes.statement: Let $$ K = 2^{2a+5}\frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,. $$ For each ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}_{F,G}$ pick a $r({\mathfrak p})>4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ with $$ {\mu(F\cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})))}\ge K{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})))}\, . $$ This ball exists by definition of ${\mathfrak P}_{F,G}$ and $\operatorname{dens}_2$. By applying \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} to the collection of balls $$ \mathcal{B} = \{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})) \ : \ {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{F,G}\} $$ and the function $u = \mathbf{1}_F$, we obtain $$ \mu(\bigcup \mathcal{B}) \le 2^{2a} K^{-1} \mu(F)\,. $$ We conclude with \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and $r({\mathfrak p})>4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ $$ \mu(G_1)= \mu(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}_{F,G}} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le \mu(\bigcup \mathcal{B})\le 2^{2a} K^{-1} \mu (F) = 2^{-5}\mu(G)\,. $$
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma

nodes.name: Set K and pick dense balls B(c(p), r(p)) for each p in P_{F,

Let
    $$
        K = 2^{2a+5}\frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,.
    $$

    $$
    {\mu(F\cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})))}\ge K{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})))}\, .
    $$

nodes.statement_short: Set K and pick dense balls B(c(p), r(p)) for each p in P_{F,G}

nodes.name: Apply the Hardy-Littlewood/Vitali lemma to the balls and 1_F
nodes.statement:
By applying \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} to the collection of balls
    $$
        \mathcal{B} = \{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),r({\mathfrak p})) \ : \ {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{F,G}\}
    $$
    and the function $u = \mathbf{1}_F$, we obtain

nodes.name: Cubes lie in the balls, giving mu(G_1) <= 2^{-5} mu(G)

We conclude with \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and $r({\mathfrak p})>4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$
