nodes.name: Dyadic Covering Lemma
conclusions:
the union of all dyadic cubes
in $\mathcal{C}(G,k)$ has measure at most $2^{k+1} \mu(G)$
nodes.statement: For each $k\ge 0$, the union of all dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{C}(G,k)$ has measure at most $2^{k+1} \mu(G)$ .
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma
nodes.label: dense-cover

nodes.name: Proof of Dyadic Covering Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the maximal dense cubes M*(k), which are disjoint, and sum their measures against G.
nodes.statement: The union of dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{C}(G,k)$ is contained the union of elements of the set $\mathcal{M}(k)$ of all dyadic cubes $J$ with ${\mu(G \cap J)} > 2^{-k-1}{\mu(J)}$. The union of elements in the set $\mathcal{M}(k)$ is contained in the union of elements in the set $\mathcal{M}^*(k)$ of maximal elements in $\mathcal{M}(k)$ with respect to set inclusion. Hence \begin{equation} \mu (\bigcup \mathcal{C}(G,k))\le \mu (\bigcup \mathcal{M}^*(k))\le \sum_{J\in \mathcal{M}^*(k)}\mu(J) \end{equation} Using the definition of $\mathcal{M}(k)$ and then the pairwise disjointedness of elements in $\mathcal{M}^*(k)$, we estimate \eqref{cbymstar} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{k+1}\sum_{J\in \mathcal{M}^*(k)}\mu(J\cap G) \le 2^{k+1}\mu(G). \end{equation} This proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma

nodes.name: Introduce M(k), the cubes with G-density above 2^{-k-1}
nodes.statement:
The union of dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{C}(G,k)$
is contained the union of elements of the set $\mathcal{M}(k)$
of all dyadic cubes $J$ with
${\mu(G \cap J)} > 2^{-k-1}{\mu(J)}$.

Using the definition of $\mathcal{M}(k)$ and then
the pairwise disjointedness of elements in

we estimate \eqref{cbymstar} by

\le
2^{k+1}\sum_{J\in \mathcal{M}^*(k)}\mu(J\cap G)

This proves the lemma.

nodes.name: bound via disjoint maximal cubes
nodes.statement: \le 2^{k+1}\sum_{J\in \mathcal{M}^*(k)}\mu(J\cap G) \le 2^{k+1}\mu(G).

nodes.name: pairwise disjoint lemma
nodes.statement_short: The sets E_1(p) for distinct tiles p of M(k,n) are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n)$ and \begin{equation} {E_1}({\mathfrak p})\cap {E_1}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset, \end{equation} then ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma
nodes.label: pairwise-disjoint

nodes.name: intersection of E_1 sets (eintersect)
nodes.statement: {E_1}({\mathfrak p})\cap {E_1}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset,
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma
nodes.label: eintersect

nodes.name: Proof of pairwise disjoint lemma
nodes.statement_short: Intersecting E_1 sets force nested cubes and frequency sets, so the tiles are ordered; maximality in M(k,n) gives equality.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'$ be as in the lemma. By definition of $E_1$, we have $E_1({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and analogously for ${\mathfrak p}'$, we conclude from \eqref{eintersect} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset$. Let without loss of generality ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ be maximal in $\{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}),{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\}$, then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. By \eqref{eintersect}, we conclude by definition of $E_1$ that ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset$. By \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we conclude ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p}'\le {\mathfrak p}$. By maximality \eqref{mnkmax} of ${\mathfrak p}'$, we have ${\mathfrak p}'={\mathfrak p}$. This proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma

nodes.name: E_1 lies in the cube, so the cubes of p and p' intersect
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'$ be as in the lemma. By definition of $E_1$,
we have
$E_1({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and analogously for ${\mathfrak p}'$, we conclude from \eqref{eintersect} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: E_1 lies in the cube, so the cubes of p and p' intersect
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma

nodes.name: WLOG I(p) is maximal, so I(p') is contained in I(p)

Let without loss of generality ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ be maximal in
$\{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}),{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\}$, then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG I(p) is maximal, so I(p') is contained in I(p)

nodes.name: Frequency sets intersect, hence are nested, so p' <= p
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eintersect}, we conclude by definition of $E_1$ that ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')\neq \emptyset$. By
\eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we conclude ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p}'\le {\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Frequency sets intersect, hence are nested, so p' <= p

nodes.name: dyadic union lemma
conclusions:
there is a dyadic cube $I$
that contains $x$ and is
a subset of
$A(\lambda,k,n)$
nodes.statement: For each $x\in A(\lambda,k,n)$, there is a dyadic cube $I$ that contains $x$ and is a subset of $A(\lambda,k,n)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proof of the Exceptional Sets Lemma
nodes.label: dyadic-union

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic union lemma
nodes.statement_short: Take the smallest-scale cube among the tiles of M(k,n) containing x; it lies in all of them, hence in A(lambda,k,n).
nodes.statement: Fix $k,n,\lambda,x$ as in the lemma such that $x\in A(\lambda,k,n)$. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be the set of dyadic cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p}$ in $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ and $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. By definition of $A(\lambda,k,n)$, the cardinality of $\mathcal{M}$ is at least $1+\lambda 2^{n+1}$. Let $I$ be a cube of smallest scale in $\mathcal{M}$. Then $I$ is contained in all cubes of $\mathcal{M}$. It follows that $I\subset A(\lambda,k,n)$.

nodes.name: Fix x and let M be the cubes of M(k,n)-tiles containing x

Fix $k,n,\lambda,x$ as in the lemma such that $x\in A(\lambda,k,n)$.

nodes.name: John-Nirenberg lemma
nodes.statement_short: The set where cubes of M(k,n) overlap more than lambda 2^{n+1} times has measure decaying like 2^{-lambda}.
nodes.statement: For all integers $k,n,\lambda\ge 0$, we have \begin{equation} \mu(A(\lambda,k,n)) \le 2^{k+1-\lambda}\mu(G)\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: John-Nirenberg bound (alambdameasure)
nodes.statement: \mu(A(\lambda,k,n)) \le 2^{k+1-\lambda}\mu(G)\,.

nodes.label: alambdameasure

nodes.name: Proof of John-Nirenberg lemma
nodes.statement_short: Induction on lambda. In the inductive step, each maximal cube L of A(lambda) carries at least 2^{n+1} overlapping tile cubes inside it, which halves the measure.
nodes.statement: Fix $k,n$ as in the lemma and suppress notation to write $A(\lambda)$ for $A(\lambda,k,n)$. We prove the lemma by induction on $\lambda$. For $\lambda=0$, we use that $A(\lambda)$ by definition of $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ is contained in the union of elements in $ \mathcal{C}(G,k)$. \Cref{dense-cover} then completes the base of the induction. Now assume that the statement of \Cref{John-Nirenberg} is proven for some integer $\lambda\ge 0$. The set $A(\lambda+1)$ is contained in the set $A(\lambda)$. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be the set of dyadic cubes which are a subset of $A(\lambda)$. By \Cref{dyadic-union}, the union of $\mathcal{M}$ is $A(\lambda)$. Let $\mathcal{M}^*$ be the set of maximal dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{M}$. Let $x\in A(\lambda+1)$ and $L\in \mathcal{M}^*$ such that $x\in L$. Then by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(x) = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(x) + \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):L \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(x)\,. \end{equation} We now show \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(x)\ge 2^{n+1}\,. \end{equation} The left-hand side of \eqref{suminout} is strictly greater than $(\lambda+1)2^{n+1}$. If $L$ is the top cube the second sum $Q_2$ on the right-hand side of \eqref{suminout} is zero and \eqref{mnkonl} follows immediately. Otherwise consider the inclusion-minimal cube $\hat{L}$ with $L\subsetneq\hat{L}$; all tiles ${\mathfrak p}$ over which $Q_2$ is summed over satisfy $\hat{L}\subset{\mathfrak p}$, so $Q_2$ is constant for all $x\in\hat{L}$. By maximality of $L$, $Q_2$ is at most $\lambda 2^{n+1}$ somewhere on $\hat{L}$, thus on all of $\hat{L}$ and consequently also at $x$. Rearranging the inequality yields \eqref{mnkonl}. By \Cref{pairwise-disjoint}, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L} \mu({E_1}({\mathfrak p})) \leq \mu(L)\, . \end{equation} Multiplying by $2^n$ and applying \eqref{ebardense}, we obtain \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \leq 2^n \mu(L)\, . \end{equation} We then have with \eqref{mnkonl} and \eqref{mnkintl} \begin{equation} 2^{n+1}\mu(A(\lambda+1)\cap L) = \int_{A(\lambda+1)\cap L} 2^{n+1} d\mu \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \int \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak{M}}(k,n):{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} d\mu \le 2^n \mu(L)\, . \end{equation} Hence \begin{equation} 2\mu(A(\lambda+1))=2\sum_{L\in \mathcal{M}^*} \mu(A(\lambda+1)\cap L)\le \sum_{L\in \mathcal{M}^*}\mu( L)= \mu(A(\lambda))\, . \end{equation} Using the induction hypothesis, this proves \eqref{alambdameasure} for $\lambda+1$ and completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of tree count lemma
nodes.statement_short: Double counting of pairs (u, m) with 100u <~ m. Each m is reached by at most 2^{9a} tree tops, by a ball-covering argument with the doubling property.
nodes.statement: Let $x\in X$. For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, as ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$, there are at least $2^{j}$ elements $\mathfrak{m}\in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and in particular $x\in {\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})$. Hence \begin{equation} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(x) \le 2^{-j}\sum_{\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n): 100{\mathfrak u}\lesssim \mathfrak{m}} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})}(x)\, . \end{equation} Conversely, for each $\mathfrak{m}\in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})$, let ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$ be the set of ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. Summing \eqref{ubymsum} over ${\mathfrak u}$ and counting the pairs $({\mathfrak u},\mathfrak{m})$ with $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ differently gives \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(x) \le 2^{-j}\sum_{\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})}(x)\, . \end{equation} We estimate the number of elements in ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$. Let ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$. Then by definition of ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$ \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),{\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}))\le 100\, . \end{equation} If ${\mathfrak u}'$ is a further element in ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$ with ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$, then \begin{equation} {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}) \in B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100)\cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),100)\ . \end{equation} By the last display and definition of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, none of ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ is strictly contained in the other. As both contain $x$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})={\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. We then have $d_{{\mathfrak u}}=d_{{\mathfrak u}'}$. By \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, the balls $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),0.2)$ and $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),0.2)$ are contained respectively in ${\Omega}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak u}')$ and thus are disjoint by \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. By \eqref{dby2} and the triangle inequality, both balls are contained in $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), 100.2)$. By \eqref{thirddb} applied nine times, there is a collection of at most $2^{9a}$ balls of radius $0.2$ with respect to the metric $d_{{\mathfrak u}}$ which cover the ball $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}),100.2)$. Let $B'$ be a ball in this cover. As the center of $B'$ can be in at most one of the disjoint balls $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),0.2)$ and $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),0.2)$, the ball $B'$ can contain at most one of the points ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})$, ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')$. Hence the image of ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$ under ${\mathcal{Q}}$ has at most $2^{9a}$ elements; since ${\mathcal{Q}}$ is injective on ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$, the same is true of ${\mathfrak U}(\mathfrak{m})$. Inserting this into \eqref{usumbymsum} proves the lemma.

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,l)$. Let $I \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})$. Then we have $s(I) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$ and $I \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and $B(c(I), 8D^{s(I)}) \not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, the set $I$ is contained in $B(c(I), 4D^{s(I)})$. By the triangle inequality, the set $I$ is contained in \begin{equation} X({\mathfrak u}):=\{x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \, : \, \rho(x, X \setminus {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})) \leq 12 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1)-1}\}\,. \end{equation} By the small boundary property \eqref{eq-small-boundary}, noting that \begin{equation*} 12D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1} = 12D^{s(I)} > D^{-S}\ , \end{equation*} we have $$ \mu(X({\mathfrak u})) \le 2\cdot(12 D^{-Z(n+1)-1})^\kappa \mu({\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{u})). $$ Using $\kappa<1$ and $D \ge 12$, this proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of third exception lemma
nodes.statement_short: Bound each L_4(k,n,j) via boundary-exception, tree-count and top-tiles lemmas, then sum geometric series over k, n, j.
nodes.statement: As each ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ is contained in $\cup\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})$ for some ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,l)$, we have \begin{equation} \mu(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4 (k,n,j)}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)} \mu(\bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{L} ({\mathfrak u})}I). \end{equation} Using \Cref{boundary-exception} and then \Cref{tree-count}, we estimate this further by \begin{equation} \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)} D^{1-\kappa Z(n+1)} \mu({\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{u})) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{100a^2+9a+1-j} \sum_{\mathfrak{m}\in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)} D^{-\kappa Z(n+1)} \mu({\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m}))\,. \end{equation} Using \Cref{top-tiles}, we estimate this by \begin{equation} \le 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 1-j} D^{-\kappa Z(n+1)} 2^{n+k+3}\mu(G)\, . \end{equation} Now we estimate $G_3$ defined in \eqref{defineg3} by \begin{equation} \mu(G_3)\le \sum_{k\ge 0}\, \sum_{n \geq k}\, \sum_{0\le j\le 2n+3} \mu(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4 (k,n,j)} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \sum_{k\ge 0}\, \sum_{n \geq k}\, \sum_{0\le j\le 2n+3} 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 3 + n + k -j} D^{-\kappa Z(n+1)}\mu(G) \end{equation} Summing geometric series, using that $D^{\kappa Z}\ge 8$ by \eqref{defineD}, \eqref{definekappa} and \eqref{defineZ}, we estimate this by \begin{equation} \le \sum_{k\ge 0}\, \sum_{n \geq k}\, 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 4 + n + k} D^{-\kappa Z(n+1)}\mu(G) \end{equation} \begin{equation} = \sum_{k\ge 0} 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 4 + 2k} D^{-\kappa Z(k+1)} \sum_{n \geq k}\, 2^{n - k} D^{-\kappa Z(n-k)}\mu(G) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \sum_{k\ge 0} 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 5 + 2k} D^{-\kappa Z(k+1)}\mu(G) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{100a^2 + 9a + 6} D^{-\kappa Z}\mu(G) \end{equation} Using $D = 2^{100a^2}$ and $a \ge 4$ and $\kappa Z \ge 2$ by \eqref{defineD} and \eqref{definekappa} proves the lemma.

nodes.name: wiggle order 1
nodes.statement_short: The relation n p <~ m p' is monotone: increasing n and decreasing m preserves it.
nodes.statement: If $n{\mathfrak p} \lesssim m{\mathfrak p}'$ and $n' \ge n$ and $m \ge m'$ then $n'{\mathfrak p} \lesssim m'{\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.label: wiggle-order-1

nodes.name: Proof of wiggle order 1
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition of <~ and inclusion of balls.
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$ and the two inclusions $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), n) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), n')$ and $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), m') \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), m)$.

nodes.name: wiggle order 2
nodes.statement_short: If n p <~ k p' with distinct cubes, then (n + 2^{-95a} m) p <~ m p' for every m >= 1.
assumptions: ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$
nodes.statement: Let $n, m \ge 1$ and $k > 0$. If ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and \begin{equation} n {\mathfrak p} \lesssim k {\mathfrak p}' \end{equation} then \begin{equation} (n + 2^{-95 a} m) {\mathfrak p} \lesssim m{\mathfrak p}'\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: wiggle-order-2

nodes.name: assumption n p <~ k p' (eq-wiggle1)
nodes.statement: n {\mathfrak p} \lesssim k {\mathfrak p}'
nodes.label: eq-wiggle1

nodes.name: conclusion (eq-wiggle2)
nodes.statement: (n + 2^{-95 a} m) {\mathfrak p} \lesssim m{\mathfrak p}'\,.
nodes.label: eq-wiggle2

nodes.name: Proof of wiggle order 2
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality in d_p, using the comparison of cube metrics across scales.
nodes.statement: The assumption \eqref{eq-wiggle1} together with the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$ implies that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Let ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), m)$. Then we have by the triangle inequality $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\vartheta}) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\vartheta}) $$ The first summand is bounded by $n$ since $$ {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}') \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), k) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), n), $$ using \eqref{wiggleorder}. For the second summand we use \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} to show that the sum is estimated by $$ n + 2^{-95a} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\vartheta}) < n + 2^{-95a} m\,. $$ Thus $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),m) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),n + 2^{-95a}m)$. Combined with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$, this yields \eqref{eq-wiggle2}.

nodes.name: Proof of P convex
nodes.statement_short: Check both density conditions (muhj1), (muhj2) for the middle tile's cube.
nodes.statement: Suppose that ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ and ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$. By \eqref{eq-defPk} we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \in \mathcal{C}(G,k)$, so there exists by \eqref{muhj1} some $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset J $$ and $\mu(G \cap J) > 2^{-k-1} \mu(J)$. Thus \eqref{muhj1} holds for ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$. On the other hand, by \eqref{muhj2}, there exists no $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset J$ and $\mu(G \cap J) > 2^{-k} \mu(J)$. Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$, this implies that \eqref{muhj2} holds for ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Hence ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \in \mathcal{C}(G,k)$, and therefore by \eqref{eq-defPk} ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$.

nodes.name: Proof of C convex
nodes.statement_short: Use convexity of P(k) and the monotonicity of dens_k' along the tile order.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$. Then, in particular, ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$, so, by \Cref{P-convex}, ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$. Next, we show that if ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ then $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$. If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$, then it follows from ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$, \eqref{eq-sc1} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ that $\lambda {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$. Thus the supremum in the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}\})$ is over a superset of the set the supremum in the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$ is taken over, which shows $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} it then follows that $$ 2^{4a}2^{-n} < \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}''\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\})\,. $$ Similarly, it follows from ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}'$, ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} that $$ \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$ Thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.

If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$, then it follows from ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$, \eqref{eq-sc1} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ that $\lambda {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$. Thus the supremum in the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}\})$ is over a superset of the set the supremum in the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$ is taken over, which shows $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$.

nodes.name: By (eq-sc1) and transitivity, lambda q' <~ lambda p implies
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$, then it follows from ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$, \eqref{eq-sc1} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ that $\lambda {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: By (eq-sc1) and transitivity, lambda q' <~ lambda p implies lambda q <~ lambda p

nodes.name: The supremum for q runs over a superset
nodes.statement: Thus the supremum in the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}\})$ is over a superset of the set the supremum in the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$ is taken over, which shows $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$.
nodes.statement_short: The supremum for q runs over a superset

nodes.name: Lower density bound for p' from p''
nodes.statement:
From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} it then follows that
    $$
        2^{4a}2^{-n} < \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}''\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\})\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Lower density bound for p' from p''

nodes.name: Upper density bound for p' from p
nodes.statement:
Similarly, it follows from ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}'$, ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} that
    $$
        \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Upper density bound for p' from p

nodes.name: So p' is in C(k,n)
nodes.statement: Thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.
nodes.statement_short: So p' is in C(k,n)

nodes.name: C1 convex lemma
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C1-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C1 convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of C(k,n) plus monotonicity of B(p) along the tile order.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'\le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C-convex} and the inclusion ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, which holds by definition \eqref{defcnkj}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we have that ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$ and $100 {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ imply $100 {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. So, by \eqref{defbfp}, $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$. Consequently, by \eqref{defcnkj} $$ 2^j \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'')|\le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}')| \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| < 2^{j+1}\,, $$ thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$.

nodes.name: By convexity of C(k,n), p' is in C(k,n)
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'\le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C-convex} and the inclusion ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, which holds by definition \eqref{defcnkj}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.
nodes.statement_short: By convexity of C(k,n), p' is in C(k,n)

nodes.name: B(p) decreases along the tile order
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we have that ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$ and $100 {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ imply $100 {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. So, by \eqref{defbfp}, $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: B(p) decreases along the tile order

nodes.name: The count |B(p')| lies in [2^j, 2^{j+1}), so p' is in C_1
nodes.statement:
Consequently, by \eqref{defcnkj}
    $$
        2^j \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'')|\le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}')| \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| < 2^{j+1}\,,
    $$
    thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: The count |B(p')| lies in [2^j, 2^{j+1}), so p' is in C_1

nodes.name: C2 convex lemma
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C2-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C2 convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of C_1, then contradiction with minimality of a removed layer.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, we have \begin{equation*} {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)\ . \end{equation*} Combined with \Cref{C1-convex}, it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. If ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$ the statement is trivially true, otherwise suppose that ${\mathfrak p}' \notin {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, this implies that there exists $0 \le l' \le Z(n+1)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$. By the definition \eqref{eq-L1-def} of ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$, this implies that ${\mathfrak p}'$ is minimal with respect to $\le$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{l < l'} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$. Since ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$ and ${\mathfrak p}\in{\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Take p <= p' <= p'' in C_2, which is contained in C_1
nodes.statement_short: Take p <= p' <= p'' in C_2, which is contained in C_1

nodes.name: By convexity of C_1, p' is in C_1
nodes.statement: Combined with \Cref{C1-convex}, it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: By convexity of C_1, p' is in C_1

nodes.name: Suppose p' is not in C_2
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$ the statement is trivially true, otherwise suppose that ${\mathfrak p}' \notin {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose p' is not in C_2

nodes.name: Then p' lies in a minimal layer L_1(k,n,j,l')
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, this implies that there exists $0 \le l' \le Z(n+1)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$.
     By the definition \eqref{eq-L1-def} of ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$, this implies that ${\mathfrak p}'$ is minimal
     with respect to $\le$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{l < l'} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$.
nodes.statement_short: Then p' lies in a minimal layer L_1(k,n,j,l')

nodes.name: Minimality forces p = p', a contradiction
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$ and ${\mathfrak p}\in{\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality forces p = p', a contradiction

nodes.name: C3 convex lemma
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C3-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C3 convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of C_2 plus transferring the tree top domination from p'' to p'.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \Cref{C2-convex} it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \eqref{eq-L2-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we then have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$.

nodes.name: By convexity of C_2, p' is in C_2
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$.
    By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \Cref{C2-convex} it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: By convexity of C_2, p' is in C_2

nodes.name: A tree top u dominates p''
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \eqref{eq-L2-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with
    $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.
nodes.statement_short: A tree top u dominates p''

nodes.name: By (eq-sc1) and transitivity u also dominates p'
nodes.statement:
From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$,
    \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we then have
    $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: By (eq-sc1) and transitivity u also dominates p'

nodes.name: C4 convex lemma
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C4-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C4 convex
nodes.statement_short: Analogous to the proof of C2 convex.
nodes.statement: The proof is entirely analogous to \Cref{C2-convex}, substituting ${\mathfrak C}_4$ for ${\mathfrak C}_2$, ${\mathfrak C}_3$ for ${\mathfrak C}_1$ and ${\mathfrak p}'\le{\mathfrak p}''$ for ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$.

nodes.name: C5 convex lemma
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.label: C5-convex

nodes.name: Proof of C5 convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of C_4, then contraposition using the definition of L_4.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. Then ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ by \eqref{defc5}, and thus by \Cref{C4-convex} ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$. It suffices to show that if ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ by contraposition; this is true by \eqref{eq-L4-def} and ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$.

nodes.name: By convexity of C_4, p' is in C_4
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$.
    Then ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ by \eqref{defc5}, and thus by \Cref{C4-convex} ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: By convexity of C_4, p' is in C_4

nodes.name: By contraposition, L_4 is closed downward
nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that if ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ by contraposition;
    this is true by \eqref{eq-L4-def} and ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.statement_short: By contraposition, L_4 is closed downward

nodes.name: dens compare lemma
nodes.statement_short: For tile collections in P(k), the density dens_1 is bounded by dens_k'.
nodes.statement: We have for every $k\ge 0$ and ${\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$ \begin{equation} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak P}')\le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak P}')\, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: dens-compare

nodes.name: density comparison inequality
nodes.statement: \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak P}')\le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak P}')\, .

nodes.name: Proof of dens compare lemma
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing that every competing tile p lies in P(k), then verify (muhj1) directly and (muhj2) by contradiction.
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'$ and $\lambda\ge 2$ and ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))} \le \sup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k): \lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}''} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}. \end{equation} Let such ${\mathfrak p}'$, $\lambda$, ${\mathfrak p}$ be given. It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$, that is, it satisfies \eqref{muhj1} and \eqref{muhj2}. We show \eqref{muhj1}. As ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$, there exists ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}'$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By assumption on ${\mathfrak P}'$, we have ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J). \end{equation} Then also ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$, which proves \eqref{muhj1} for ${\mathfrak p}$. We show \eqref{muhj2}. Assume to get a contradiction that there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J). \end{equation} As $\lambda{\mathfrak p}'\lesssim \lambda{\mathfrak p}$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, and therefore ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$. This contradicts ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$. This proves \eqref{muhj2} for ${\mathfrak p}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to a comparison of suprema
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a comparison of suprema

nodes.name: supremum comparison
nodes.statement: \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))} \le \sup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k): \lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}''} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}.

nodes.name: It suffices to show p is in P(k)
nodes.statement:
Let such ${\mathfrak p}'$, $\lambda$, ${\mathfrak p}$ be given.
    It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$,
    that is, it satisfies \eqref{muhj1}
    and \eqref{muhj2}.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to show p is in P(k)

nodes.name: Verify (muhj1) for p
nodes.statement:
We show \eqref{muhj1}.
 As ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$, there exists
${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}'$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By assumption on ${\mathfrak P}'$, we have ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and there exists
$J\in \mathcal{D}$ with
   ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')\subset J$ and
   \begin{equation}
       \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J).
   \end{equation}
Then also ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$, which proves
\eqref{muhj1} for ${\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify (muhj1) for p

nodes.name: Find p'' in P' above p' and a dense cube J above I(p'')
nodes.statement:
We show \eqref{muhj1}.
 As ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$, there exists
${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}'$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By assumption on ${\mathfrak P}'$, we have ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and there exists
$J\in \mathcal{D}$ with
   ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')\subset J$ and
   \begin{equation}
       \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J).
   \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Find p'' in P' above p' and a dense cube J above I(p'')

nodes.name: density of J above I(p'')
nodes.statement: \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J).

nodes.name: J lies above I(p'), giving (muhj1)
nodes.statement:
Then also ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$, which proves
\eqref{muhj1} for ${\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: J lies above I(p'), giving (muhj1)

nodes.name: Verify (muhj2) for p by contradiction
nodes.statement:
We show \eqref{muhj2}. Assume to get a contradiction that
there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with
   ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset J$ and
   \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J).
   \end{equation}
   As $\lambda{\mathfrak p}'\lesssim \lambda{\mathfrak p}$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, and therefore
    ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$. This contradicts
   ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$. This proves
\eqref{muhj2} for ${\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify (muhj2) for p by contradiction

nodes.name: Assume a very dense cube J lies above I(p)
nodes.statement:
We show \eqref{muhj2}. Assume to get a contradiction that
there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with
   ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset J$ and
   \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J).
   \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Assume a very dense cube J lies above I(p)

nodes.name: contradiction hypothesis (mugj)
nodes.statement: \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J).
nodes.label: mugj

nodes.name: Then J lies above I(p'), contradicting p' in P(k)
nodes.statement:
As $\lambda{\mathfrak p}'\lesssim \lambda{\mathfrak p}$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, and therefore
    ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$. This contradicts
   ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$. This proves
\eqref{muhj2} for ${\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Then J lies above I(p'), contradicting p' in P(k)

nodes.name: C dens1 lemma
nodes.statement_short: Every subset of the density class C(k,n) has dens_1 at most 2^{4a-n+1}.
nodes.statement: For each set $\mathfrak{A} \subset \mathfrak{C}(k,n)$, we have $$ \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$
nodes.label: C-dens1

nodes.name: Proof of C dens1 lemma
nodes.statement_short: Compare dens_1 with dens_k' and use the defining density bound of C(k,n).
nodes.statement: We have by \Cref{dens-compare} that $\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A})$. Since $\mathfrak{A} \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, it follows from monotonicity of suprema and the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} that $ \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n))\,. $ By \eqref{eq-densdef} and \eqref{def-cnk}, we have $$ \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n)) = \sup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)} \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$

nodes.name: Apply the density comparison lemma
nodes.statement:
We have by \Cref{dens-compare} that
    $\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the density comparison lemma

nodes.name: Monotonicity of suprema
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathfrak{A} \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, it follows from monotonicity of suprema and the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} that
    $
        \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n))\,.
    $
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of suprema

nodes.name: Definition of C(k,n) bounds dens_k'
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-densdef} and \eqref{def-cnk}, we have
    $$
        \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n)) = \sup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)} \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Definition of C(k,n) bounds dens_k'

nodes.name: Set C_6(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define
$$
    {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)
$$
to be the set of all tiles ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset G'$.
nodes.genus: set of all tiles ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Tree candidates T_1(u)
nodes.statement_short: T_1(u): tiles of C_1 with cube different from that of u and 2p ≲ u.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Definition of T_1(u)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}):= \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \ : {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}), \ 2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}\}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-T1-def

nodes.name: Set U_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement_short: U_2: those u in U_1 whose T_1(u) meets C_6.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Definition of U_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j) := \{ {\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j) \, : \, \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}) \cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \ne \emptyset\}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: eq-U2-def

nodes.name: Relation ~ on U_2(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:
Define a relation $\sim$ on ${\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$
by setting ${\mathfrak u}\sim {\mathfrak u}'$
for ${\mathfrak u},{\mathfrak u}'\in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$
if ${\mathfrak u}={\mathfrak u}'$ or there exists ${\mathfrak p}$ in $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$
with $10 {\mathfrak p}\lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$.
differentia:
${\mathfrak u}={\mathfrak u}'$ or there exists ${\mathfrak p}$ in $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$
with $10 {\mathfrak p}\lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$
nodes.statement_short: u ~ u' iff u = u' or some p in T_1(u) has 10p ≲ u'.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: relation geometry
conclusions: B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \neq \emptyset
nodes.statement_short: Equivalent trees have the same cube and overlapping 100-balls around their frequencies.
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$, then ${\mathcal{I}}(u) = {\mathcal{I}}(u')$ and \begin{equation*} B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \neq \emptyset\ . \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: relation-geometry

nodes.name: Proof of relation geometry
nodes.statement_short: Case u = u' is trivial; otherwise a common tile p would have |B(p)| ≥ 2^{j+1}, contradicting p in C_1; nestedness then gives equal cubes.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u}, {\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$. If ${\mathfrak u} = {\mathfrak u}'$ then the conclusion of the Lemma clearly holds. Else, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and $2 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and $10 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$. Using \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \eqref{eq-sc2} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3}, we deduce that \begin{equation} 100 {\mathfrak p}\lesssim 100 {\mathfrak u}\,, \qquad 100 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim 100{\mathfrak u}'\,. \end{equation} Now suppose that $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$. Then we have $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}) \cap \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}') = \emptyset$, by the definition \eqref{defbfp} of $\mathfrak{B}$ and the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$, but also $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}) \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$ and $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$, by \eqref{defbfp}, \eqref{wiggleorder} and \eqref{eq-Fefferman-trick0}. Hence, $$ |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| \geq |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u})| + |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}')| \geq 2^{j} + 2^j = 2^{j+1}\,, $$ which contradicts ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. Therefore we must have \begin{equation*} B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \ne \emptyset\, . \end{equation*} It follows from $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and $10{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ are nested. Combining this with the conclusion of the last paragraph and definition \eqref{defunkj} of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, we obtain that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$.

Hence,

    which contradicts ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. Therefore we must have

        B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \ne \emptyset\, .

Using \eqref{defdp} and the fact that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}'')$ this equals
    \begin{align*}
        &\quad d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\vartheta}, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\\
        &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\theta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}''}({\theta}, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'')) +

nodes.name: Representatives U_3(k,n,j)
nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Trees T_2(u)
nodes.statement:
Define for each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$
\begin{equation} {\mathfrak T}_2({\mathfrak u}):=
   \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\sim {\mathfrak u}'}\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: T_2(u): union of T_1(u') over u' ~ u, intersected with C_6.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Definition of T_2(u)
nodes.statement: {\mathfrak T}_2({\mathfrak u}):= \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\sim {\mathfrak u}'}\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)\, .
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: definesv

nodes.name: C6 forest
nodes.statement_short: C_6 is the union of the trees T_2(u) over representatives u.
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)}\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})\, . \end{equation}

nodes.label: C6-forest

nodes.name: C_6 as union of T_2(u)

nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of C6 forest
nodes.statement_short: Unwind the definitions: each p in C_6 lies in some T_1(u), u in U_2, hence in T_2 of its representative.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C4-def} and \eqref{defc5}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-L2-def} and \eqref{eq-C3-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, that is, with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$. Then $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$ is clearly nonempty, so ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$. By the definition of ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$. By \eqref{definesv}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: p lies in C_3
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$.
    By \eqref{eq-C4-def} and \eqref{defc5}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: p lies in C_3
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Find u in U_1 with p in T_1(u), so u in U_2
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-L2-def} and \eqref{eq-C3-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, that is, with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$. Then $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$ is clearly nonempty, so ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Find u in U_1 with p in T_1(u), so u in U_2

nodes.name: Take the representative u' of u
nodes.statement: By the definition of ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the representative u' of u

nodes.name: Conclude p in T_2(u')
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definesv}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude p in T_2(u')
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: forest geometry
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ satisfies \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-geometry

nodes.name: Proof of forest geometry
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality with a common point of the 100-balls of u and u' gives 4p ≲ u.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{definesv}, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. Then we have $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$, so by \eqref{eq-sc3} $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$. Further, by \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and there exists ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100)$. Let ${\theta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1)$. Using the triangle inequality and the fact that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') ={\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, we obtain \begin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\theta}) &\le d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\ &= d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\ &< 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,. \end{align*} Combining this with $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$, we obtain $$ B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1) \subset B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 500) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 4)\,. $$ Together with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, this gives $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$, which is \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Find u' ~ u with p in T_1(u')
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{definesv}, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Find u' ~ u with p in T_1(u')
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Get 4p ≲ 500u'
nodes.statement: Then we have $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$, so by \eqref{eq-sc3} $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Get 4p ≲ 500u'
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Equal cubes and common point of the balls
nodes.statement: Further, by \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and there exists ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100)$.
nodes.statement_short: Equal cubes and common point of the balls
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Triangle inequality bound by 500
nodes.statement:
Let ${\theta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1)$.
    Using the triangle inequality and the fact that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') ={\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, we obtain
    \begin{align*}
        d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\theta}) &\le d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\
        &= d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\
        &< 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,.
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality bound by 500
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Chain of ball inclusions
nodes.statement:
Combining this with $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$, we obtain
    $$
        B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1) \subset B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 500) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 4)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Chain of ball inclusions
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Conclude 4p ≲ u
nodes.statement: Together with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, this gives $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$, which is \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude 4p ≲ u
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: forest convex
conclusions:
the set $\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$
    satisfies the convexity condition \eqref{forest2}
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ satisfies the convexity condition \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-convex

nodes.name: Proof of forest convex
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of C_5 puts p' in C_6, and p' ≤ p'' gives p' in T_1(u').
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$. By \eqref{definesv} we have ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C5-convex}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$ we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) 
ot \subset G'$, so ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
ot \subset G'$ and therefore also ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{definesv} there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') 
e {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. Together this implies ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. With the inclusion ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ from ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
e {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we further have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$, which shows \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Set up p ≤ p' ≤ p'' with p, p'' in C_6
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$. By \eqref{definesv} we have ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up p ≤ p' ≤ p'' with p, p'' in C_6
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: p' lies in C_5 by convexity
nodes.statement: By \Cref{C5-convex}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: p' lies in C_5 by convexity
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: p' lies in C_6
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$ we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset G'$, so ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \not \subset G'$ and therefore also ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: p' lies in C_6
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Strict cube inclusion I(p'') ⊊ I(u')
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definesv} there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. Together this implies ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Strict cube inclusion I(p'') ⊊ I(u')
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Hence I(p') ≠ I(u')
nodes.statement: With the inclusion ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ from ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence I(p') ≠ I(u')
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: 2p' ≲ u', so p' in T_1(u')
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we further have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: 2p' ≲ u', so p' in T_1(u')
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Conclude p' in T_2(u)
nodes.statement: It follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$, which shows \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude p' in T_2(u)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: forest separation
assumptions: ${\mathfrak u},{\mathfrak u}'\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$

${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}_2({\mathfrak u})$
    with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u},{\mathfrak u}'\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ we have \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-separation

nodes.name: Separation bound d_p(Q(p),Q(u')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}
nodes.statement: d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest separation
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a tile p' ≤ p at scale Z(n+1) lower, use monotonicity of cube metrics, and bound d_{p'} below by 8 since 10p' does not wiggle-precede u'.
nodes.statement:
By the definition \eqref{eq-C2-def} of ${\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})- Z(n+1)$. By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} we have $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) \ge 2^{95a Z(n+1)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-sc1} we have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim 2{\mathfrak p}$, so by transitivity of $\lesssim$ there exists $\mathfrak{v} \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \mathfrak{v}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
e {\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{v})$. Since ${\mathfrak u}, {\mathfrak u}'$ are not equivalent under $\sim$, we have $\mathfrak{v} 
ot \sim {\mathfrak u}'$, thus $10{\mathfrak p}' 
ot\lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$. This implies that there exists $q \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 1) \setminus B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 10)$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} it then follows that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak p}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak u}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &> -1 + 10 - 1 = 8\,. \end{align*} The lemma follows by combining the two displays with the fact that $95 a \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Pick p' ≤ p in C_1 at lower scale
nodes.statement: By the definition \eqref{eq-C2-def} of ${\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})- Z(n+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick p' ≤ p in C_1 at lower scale
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Compare d_p and d_{p'}
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} we have
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) \ge 2^{95a Z(n+1)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Compare d_p and d_{p'}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Find v ~ u with 2p' ≲ v
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-sc1} we have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim 2{\mathfrak p}$, so by transitivity of $\lesssim$ there exists $\mathfrak{v} \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \mathfrak{v}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \ne {\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{v})$.
nodes.statement_short: Find v ~ u with 2p' ≲ v
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Obtain q in B_{u'}(Q(u'),1) outside B_{p'}(Q(p'),10)
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathfrak u}, {\mathfrak u}'$ are not equivalent under $\sim$, we have $\mathfrak{v} \not \sim {\mathfrak u}'$, thus $10{\mathfrak p}' \not\lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$. This implies that there exists $q \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 1) \setminus B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 10)$.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain q in B_{u'}(Q(u'),1) outside B_{p'}(Q(p'),10)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Lower bound d_{p'}(Q(p),Q(u')) > 8
nodes.statement:
From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} it then follows that
    \begin{align*}
        &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\\
        &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak p}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\\
        &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak u}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\\
        &> -1 + 10 - 1 = 8\,.
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound d_{p'}(Q(p),Q(u')) > 8
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Combine the two displays
nodes.statement: The lemma follows by combining the two displays with the fact that $95 a \ge 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two displays
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: forest inner
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ we have \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-inner

nodes.name: Ball B(c(p), 8D^{s(p)}) inside I(u)
nodes.statement: B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}).
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest inner
nodes.statement_short: A chain above p gives s(p) ≤ s(u) - Z(n+1) - 1; the intermediate cube is not in L(u) since p is in C_5, so its 8-ball lies in I(u).
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. Then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$, hence there exists a chain $$ {\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}_{Z(n+1)} \le \dotsb \le {\mathfrak p}_0 $$ of distinct tiles in ${\mathfrak C}_3(n,k,j)$. We pick such a chain and set ${\mathfrak q} = {\mathfrak p}_0$. Then we have from distinctness of the tiles in the chain that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} there exists ${\mathfrak u}'' \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak q} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'')$. Then we have in particular by \Cref{wiggle-order-1} that $10 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$. Let ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ be such that ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. By the definition of $\sim$, it follows that ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}''$. By transitivity of $\sim$, we have ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}''$. By \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'') = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$, hence ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$. Thus, there exists some cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$ and $I \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset I$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$, we have that $I \notin \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})$, so $B(c(I), 8D^{s(I)}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By the triangle inequality, \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, the same then holds for the subcube ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset I$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Chain of distinct tiles above p in C_3
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. Then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$, hence there exists a chain
    $$
        {\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}_{Z(n+1)} \le \dotsb \le {\mathfrak p}_0
    $$
    of distinct tiles in ${\mathfrak C}_3(n,k,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of distinct tiles above p in C_3
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Set q = p_0, so s(p) ≤ s(q) - Z(n+1)
nodes.statement:
We pick such a chain and set ${\mathfrak q} = {\mathfrak p}_0$.
    Then we have from distinctness of the tiles in the chain that
    ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Set q = p_0, so s(p) ≤ s(q) - Z(n+1)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Find u'' with 2q ≲ u'' and 10p ≲ u''
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-C3-def} there exists ${\mathfrak u}'' \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak q} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'')$.
    Then we have in particular by \Cref{wiggle-order-1} that $10 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$.
nodes.statement_short: Find u'' with 2q ≲ u'' and 10p ≲ u''
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: u ~ u'' by transitivity
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ be such that ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$.
    By the definition of $\sim$, it follows that ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}''$.
    By transitivity of $\sim$, we have ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}''$.
nodes.statement_short: u ~ u'' by transitivity
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Scale bound s(p) ≤ s(u) - Z(n+1) - 1
nodes.statement: By \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'') = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$, hence ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Scale bound s(p) ≤ s(u) - Z(n+1) - 1

nodes.name: Intermediate cube I between I(p) and I(u)
nodes.statement: Thus, there exists some cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$ and $I \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset I$.

nodes.name: Transfer to the subcube I(p)

nodes.name: forest stacking
nodes.statement_short: The cubes of the representatives U_3(k,n,j) overlap at most (4n+12)2^n times.
nodes.statement: It holds for $k\le n$ that \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le (4n+12)2^{n}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma
nodes.label: forest-stacking

nodes.name: Overlap bound for cubes of U_3
nodes.statement: \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le (4n+12)2^{n}\,.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of forest stacking
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: an injective map u -> m(u) into M(k,n) puts x in A(2n+6,k,n) ⊂ G_2, so a minimal cube lies in G_2, contradicting u in U_2.
nodes.statement: Suppose that a point $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$. Since ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for each such ${\mathfrak u}$, there exists $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. We fix such an $\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u}) := \mathfrak{m}$ for each ${\mathfrak u}$, and claim that the map ${\mathfrak u} \mapsto\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u})$ is injective. Indeed, assume for ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ there is $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and $100{\mathfrak u}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, either ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{defunkj}, $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$. This contradicts $\Omega(\mathfrak{m})$ being contained in both sets by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. Thus $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})$, $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$. Consequently, we have by \eqref{eq-Aoverlap-def} that $x \in A(2n + 6, k,n) \subset G_2$. Let ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ be an inclusion minimal cube among the ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ for all cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ containing $x$. Thus $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset \{y \ : \ \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y) > 1 + (4n+12)2^{n}\} \subset G_2\,. $$ Thus $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}) \cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \emptyset$. This contradicts ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Assume x lies in too many cubes I(u)
nodes.statement: Suppose that a point $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume x lies in too many cubes I(u)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Each u has some m in M(k,n) with 100u ≲ m
nodes.statement:
Since ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for each such ${\mathfrak u}$,
    there exists $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Each u has some m in M(k,n) with 100u ≲ m
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Claim: u -> m(u) is injective
nodes.statement:
We fix such an $\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u}) := \mathfrak{m}$ for each ${\mathfrak u}$, and claim that the map ${\mathfrak u} \mapsto\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u})$ is injective.
    Indeed, assume for ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ there is $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that
    $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and $100{\mathfrak u}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty},
    either ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.
    By \eqref{defunkj}, $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$.
    This contradicts $\Omega(\mathfrak{m})$ being contained in both sets by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: u -> m(u) is injective
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Assume two u share an m
nodes.statement:
Indeed, assume for ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ there is $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that
    $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and $100{\mathfrak u}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume two u share an m

nodes.name: Their cubes are nested
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{dyadicproperty},
    either ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.
nodes.statement_short: Their cubes are nested

nodes.name: Their 100-balls are disjoint
nodes.statement: By \eqref{defunkj}, $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Their 100-balls are disjoint
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Contradiction with Ω(m) lying in both
nodes.statement: This contradicts $\Omega(\mathfrak{m})$ being contained in both sets by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with Ω(m) lying in both

nodes.name: x lies in many cubes I(m)
nodes.statement: Thus $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})$, $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$.
nodes.statement_short: x lies in many cubes I(m)
