nodes.name: x in A(2n+6,k,n) ⊂ G_2
nodes.statement: Consequently, we have by \eqref{eq-Aoverlap-def} that $x \in A(2n + 6, k,n) \subset G_2$.
nodes.statement_short: x in A(2n+6,k,n) ⊂ G_2
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Minimal cube containing x lies in G_2
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ be an inclusion minimal cube among the ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.
    By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ for all cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ containing $x$. Thus
    $$
        {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset \{y \ : \ \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y) > 1 + (4n+12)2^{n}\} \subset G_2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Minimal cube containing x lies in G_2
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Contradiction with u in U_2
nodes.statement:
Thus $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}) \cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \emptyset$.
    This contradicts ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with u in U_2
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of Forest Union Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Decompose U_3 into 4n+12 layers by forest stacking; each layer is an n-forest, so apply the Forest Operator Proposition and sum over k,n,j,l.
nodes.statement: We first fix $k,n, j$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{defineep}, we have that $\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)$ and hence $\mathbf{1}_{G \setminus G'} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)= 0$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j) \setminus {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. Thus it suffices to estimate the contribution of the sets ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{forest-stacking}, we can decompose ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ as a disjoint union of at most $4n + 12$ collections ${\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)$, $1 \le l \le 4n+12$, each satisfying $$ \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le 2^n\,. $$ By Lemmas \ref{forest-geometry}, \ref{forest-convex}, \ref{forest-separation}, \ref{forest-inner} and \ref{C-dens1}, the pairs $$ ({\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l), \mathfrak{T}_2|_{{\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)}) $$ are $n$-forests for each $k,n,j,l$, and by \Cref{C6-forest}, we have $$ {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \bigcup_{l = 1}^{4n + 12} \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})\,. $$ Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset G_1$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$, we have ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} = \emptyset$ and hence $$ \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})) \le 2^{2a + 5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,. $$ Using the triangle inequality according to the splitting by $k,n,j$ and $l$ in \eqref{disclesssim1} and applying \Cref{forest-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate $$ \sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k} (2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{440a^3}2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}(2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2 \|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 $$ for the left hand side of \eqref{disclesssim1}. Since $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. We get a bound $$ 2^{440a^3} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{1 -\frac{1}{q}} 2^{2a+5}\sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k}(2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}\,. $$ Interchanging the order of summation, the last factor equals $$ 2^{2a+5} \sum_{n \ge 0} (2n+3)(4n+12) (n+1) 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}\,. $$ Up to an explicit constant, the sum is bounded by $\sum n^3 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}$, which is at most some constant times $1/(q-1)^4$ by comparing to an integral. Since $a \ge 4$, this is overall bounded by $2^{a^3}/(q-1)^4$, which completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Tiles outside C_6 contribute nothing on G \ G'
nodes.statement:
We first fix $k,n, j$.
    By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{defineep}, we have that
    $\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)$ and hence $\mathbf{1}_{G \setminus G'} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)= 0$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j) \setminus {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Tiles outside C_6 contribute nothing on G \ G'
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Reduce to C_6(k,n,j)
nodes.statement: Thus it suffices to estimate the contribution of the sets ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to C_6(k,n,j)
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Split U_3 into 4n+12 layers of overlap 2^n
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{forest-stacking}, we can decompose ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ as a disjoint union of at most $4n + 12$ collections ${\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)$, $1 \le l \le 4n+12$, each satisfying
    $$
        \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le 2^n\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Split U_3 into 4n+12 layers of overlap 2^n
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Each layer gives an n-forest covering C_6
nodes.statement:
By Lemmas \ref{forest-geometry}, \ref{forest-convex}, \ref{forest-separation}, \ref{forest-inner} and \ref{C-dens1}, the pairs
    $$
        ({\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l), \mathfrak{T}_2|_{{\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)})
    $$
    are $n$-forests for each $k,n,j,l$, and by \Cref{C6-forest}, we have
    $$
        {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \bigcup_{l = 1}^{4n + 12} \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Each layer gives an n-forest covering C_6
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Density dens_2 bound
nodes.statement:
Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset G_1$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$, we have ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} = \emptyset$ and hence
    $$
        \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})) \le 2^{2a + 5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Density dens_2 bound
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Apply the Forest Operator Proposition to each term
nodes.statement:
Using the triangle inequality according to the splitting by $k,n,j$ and $l$ in \eqref{disclesssim1} and applying \Cref{forest-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate
    $$
        \sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k} (2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{440a^3}2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}(2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2 \|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2
    $$
    for the left hand side of \eqref{disclesssim1}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Forest Operator Proposition to each term
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Bound the L^2 norms
nodes.statement:
Since $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$.
    We get a bound
    $$
        2^{440a^3} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{1
        -\frac{1}{q}} 2^{2a+5}\sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k}(2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the L^2 norms
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Interchange summation
nodes.statement:
Interchanging the order of summation, the last factor equals
    $$
        2^{2a+5} \sum_{n \ge 0} (2n+3)(4n+12) (n+1) 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Interchange summation
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Sum the series by comparison with an integral
nodes.statement:
Up to an explicit constant, the sum is bounded by $\sum n^3 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}$, which is at most
    some constant times $1/(q-1)^4$ by comparing to an integral. Since $a \ge 4$, this is overall bounded by $2^{a^3}/(q-1)^4$,
    which completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the series by comparison with an integral
nodes.section: 5.4 Proof of the Forest Union Lemma

nodes.name: Tiles meeting G \ G'

nodes.name: antichain decomposition
conclusions: &\quad {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &= \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k} {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'} \\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)\cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\,.

nodes.statement: &\quad {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &= \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k} {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'} \\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)\cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\,.

nodes.name: Proof of antichain decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Locate each tile in some P(k), then some C(k,n), then in L_0(k,n) or C_1(k,n,j), and unwind definitions.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$. Clearly, for every cube $J = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$ there exists some $k \ge 0$ such that \eqref{muhj1} holds, and for no cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ and no $k < 0$ does \eqref{muhj2} hold. Thus ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ for some $k \ge 0$. Next, since $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\cap G$ for every $\lambda \ge 2$ and every tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ with $\lambda{\mathfrak p} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}'$, it follows from \eqref{muhj2} that $\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}')) \le 2^{-k} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))$ for every such ${\mathfrak p}'$, so $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{-k}$. Combining this with $a \ge 0$, it follows from \eqref{def-cnk} that there exists $n\ge k$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$, we have in particular ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset A(2n + 6, k, n)$, so there exist at most $1 + (4n + 12)2^n < 2^{2n+4}$ tiles $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le \mathfrak{m}$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ or ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for some $1 \le j \le 2n + 3$. In the former case we are done, in the latter case the equality to be shown follows from the definitions of the collections ${\mathfrak C}_i$ and ${\mathfrak L}_i$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: p lies in P(k) for some k ≥ 0
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$. Clearly, for every cube $J = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$ there exists some $k \ge 0$ such that \eqref{muhj1} holds, and for no cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ and no $k < 0$ does \eqref{muhj2} hold. Thus ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ for some $k \ge 0$.
nodes.statement_short: p lies in P(k) for some k ≥ 0
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: dens'_k bound puts p in some C(k,n)
nodes.statement: Next, since $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\cap G$ for every $\lambda \ge 2$ and every tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ with $\lambda{\mathfrak p} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}'$, it follows from \eqref{muhj2} that $\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}')) \le 2^{-k} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))$ for every such ${\mathfrak p}'$, so $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{-k}$. Combining this with $a \ge 0$, it follows from \eqref{def-cnk} that there exists $n\ge k$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.

nodes.name: Few maximal tiles above p: p in L_0 or C_1; conclude
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$, we have in particular ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset A(2n + 6, k, n)$, so there exist at most $1 + (4n + 12)2^n < 2^{2n+4}$ tiles $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le \mathfrak{m}$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ or ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for some $1 \le j \le 2n + 3$. In the former case we are done, in the latter case the equality to be shown follows from the definitions of the collections ${\mathfrak C}_i$ and ${\mathfrak L}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Few maximal tiles above p: p in L_0 or C_1; conclude
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: L0 antichain
nodes.statement_short: L_0(k,n) is a disjoint union of n antichains.
nodes.statement: We have that $$ {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) = \dot{\bigcup_{0 \le l < n}} {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n,l)\,, $$ where each ${\mathfrak L}_0(k,n,l)$ is an antichain.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.label: L0-antichain

nodes.name: Proof of L0 antichain
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to exclude chains of length n+1; a long chain plus the density bound yields a tile m in M(k,n) with 100p_0 ≲ m, contradicting p_0 not in C(k,n).
nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ contains no chain of length $n + 1$. Suppose that we had such a chain ${\mathfrak p}_0 \le {\mathfrak p}_1 \le \dotsb \le {\mathfrak p}_{n}$ with ${\mathfrak p}_i 
e {\mathfrak p}_{i+1}$ for $i =0, \dotsc, n-1$. By \eqref{def-cnk}, we have that $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}_n\}) > 2^{-n}$. Thus, by \eqref{eq-densdef}, there exists ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak p}_n \le \lambda {\mathfrak p}'$ and  egin{equation}  rac{\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}'))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))} > \lambda^{a} 2^{4a} 2^{-n}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathfrak{O}$ be the set of all ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ such that we have $ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}'') 
eq \emptyset$. We now show that  egin{equation} |\mathfrak{O}| \le 2^{4a}\lambda^a\,. \end{equation} The balls $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ are disjoint by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, and by the triangle inequality contained in $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda+1.2)$. By assumption \eqref{thirddb} on $\Theta$, this ball can be covered with $$ 2^{a\lceil \log_2(\lambda+1.2) + \log_2(5)ceil} \le 2^{a(\log_2(\lambda) + 4)} = 2^{4a}\lambda^a $$ many $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}$-balls of radius $0.2$. Here we have used that for $\lambda \ge 2$ $$ \lceil \log_2(\lambda + 1.2) + \log_2(5) ceil \le 1+ \log_2(1.6 \lambda) + \log_2(5) = 4 + \log_2(\lambda)\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, each such ball contains at most one ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is contained in one of the balls. Thus we get \eqref{eq-O-bound}. By \eqref{definee1} and \eqref{definee2} we have $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset  igcup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}} E_1({\mathfrak p}'')$, thus $$ 2^{4a}\lambda^a 2^{-n} < \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}}  rac{\mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}\,. $$ Hence there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ with  egin{equation*} \mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}'')) \ge 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))\,. \end{equation*} By the definition \eqref{mnkmax} of $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$, there exists a tile $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \leq \mathfrak{m}$. From \eqref{eq-p'}, the inclusion $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $a\ge 1$ we obtain $$ 2^n \geq 2^{4a} \lambda^{a} \geq \lambda\,. $$ From the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and $a \ge 1$, we now obtain for all ${\vartheta} \in B_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), 1)$ that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\vartheta})\ &\leq d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\ &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta})\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an} (d_{{\mathfrak p}_{n}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_n), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\ &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}''}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta}))\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an}(\lambda + (\lambda + 1) + 1 + 1) \leq 100\,. \end{align*} Thus, by \eqref{straightorder}, $100{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$, a contradiction to ${\mathfrak p}_0 
otin {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Reduce to excluding chains of length n+1
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ contains no chain of length $n + 1$.

nodes.name: Large E_2 density of p'
nodes.statement: \frac{\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}'))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))} > \lambda^{a} 2^{4a} 2^{-n}\,.

nodes.label: eq-p'

nodes.name: Define the set O and claim |O| ≤ 2^{4a}λ^a
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{O}$ be the set of all ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ such that we have $ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}'') \neq \emptyset$.
    We now show that
    \begin{equation} |\mathfrak{O}| \le 2^{4a}\lambda^a\,.
    \end{equation}
    The balls $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ are disjoint by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball},
    and by the triangle inequality contained in $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda+1.2)$.
    By assumption \eqref{thirddb} on $\Theta$, this ball can be covered with
    $$
        2^{a\lceil \log_2(\lambda+1.2) + \log_2(5)\rceil} \le 2^{a(\log_2(\lambda) + 4)} = 2^{4a}\lambda^a
    $$
    many $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}$-balls of radius $0.2$. Here we have used that for $\lambda \ge 2$
    $$
        \lceil \log_2(\lambda + 1.2)  + \log_2(5) \rceil \le 1+ \log_2(1.6  \lambda) + \log_2(5) = 4 + \log_2(\lambda)\,.
    $$
    By the triangle inequality, each such ball contains at most one ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is contained in one of the balls. Thus we get \eqref{eq-O-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Define the set O and claim |O| ≤ 2^{4a}λ^a
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Cardinality bound |O| ≤ 2^{4a}λ^a
nodes.statement: |\mathfrak{O}| \le 2^{4a}\lambda^a\,.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.label: eq-O-bound

nodes.name: Disjoint 0.2-balls inside a (λ+1.2)-ball
nodes.statement:
The balls $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ are disjoint by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball},
    and by the triangle inequality contained in $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda+1.2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint 0.2-balls inside a (λ+1.2)-ball
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Covering number bound
nodes.statement:
By assumption \eqref{thirddb} on $\Theta$, this ball can be covered with
    $$
        2^{a\lceil \log_2(\lambda+1.2) + \log_2(5)\rceil} \le 2^{a(\log_2(\lambda) + 4)} = 2^{4a}\lambda^a
    $$
    many $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}$-balls of radius $0.2$. Here we have used that for $\lambda \ge 2$
    $$
        \lceil \log_2(\lambda + 1.2)  + \log_2(5) \rceil \le 1+ \log_2(1.6  \lambda) + \log_2(5) = 4 + \log_2(\lambda)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Covering number bound
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Each covering ball contains one Q(p'')
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, each such ball contains at most one ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is contained in one of the balls. Thus we get \eqref{eq-O-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Each covering ball contains one Q(p'')
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Find p'' in O with large E_1
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{definee1} and \eqref{definee2} we have $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}} E_1({\mathfrak p}'')$, thus
    $$
        2^{4a}\lambda^a 2^{-n} < \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}} \frac{\mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}\,.
    $$
    Hence there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ with
    \begin{equation*}
        \mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}'')) \ge 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))\,.
    \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Find p'' in O with large E_1
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Find m in M(k,n) above p'
nodes.statement: By the definition \eqref{mnkmax} of $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$, there exists a tile $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \leq \mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Find m in M(k,n) above p'
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: 2^n ≥ λ
nodes.statement:
From \eqref{eq-p'}, the inclusion $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $a\ge 1$ we obtain
    $$
        2^n \geq 2^{4a} \lambda^{a} \geq \lambda\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: 2^n ≥ λ
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Bound d_{p_0}(Q(p_0), θ) ≤ 100
nodes.statement:
From the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and $a \ge 1$, we now obtain for all ${\vartheta} \in B_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), 1)$ that
    \begin{align*}
        &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\vartheta})\\
        &\leq d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\\
        &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) +
        d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta})\\
        &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an} (d_{{\mathfrak p}_{n}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_n), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\\
        &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}''}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) +
        d_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta}))\\
        &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an}(\lambda + (\lambda + 1) + 1 + 1) \leq 100\,.
    \end{align*}
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: 100p_0 ≲ m: contradiction
nodes.statement: Thus, by \eqref{straightorder}, $100{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$, a contradiction to ${\mathfrak p}_0 \notin {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.
nodes.statement_short: 100p_0 ≲ m: contradiction
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: L2 antichain
conclusions: Each of the sets ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is an antichain.
nodes.statement: Each of the sets ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is an antichain.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.label: L2-antichain

nodes.name: Proof of L2 antichain
nodes.statement_short: A comparable pair starts a maximal ≲-chain in C_1; its top is not in U_1, so the chain extends, contradicting maximality.
nodes.statement:
Suppose that there are ${\mathfrak p}_0, {\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}_0 
e {\mathfrak p}_1$ and ${\mathfrak p}_0 \le {\mathfrak p}_1$. By \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \Cref{wiggle-order-2}, it follows that $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_1$. Since ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is finite, there exists a maximal $l \ge 1$ such that there exists a chain $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_1 \lesssim \dotsb \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l$ with all ${\mathfrak p}_i$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ and ${\mathfrak p}_i 
e {\mathfrak p}_{i+1}$ for $i = 0, \dotsc, l-1$. If we have ${\mathfrak p}_l \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, then it follows from $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim {\mathfrak p}_l$ and \eqref{eq-L2-def} that ${\mathfrak p}_0 
ot\in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$, a contradiction. Thus, by the definition \eqref{defunkj} of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak p}_{l+1} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_l) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}) $ and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}_l}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_l), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}), 100)$. Using the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, one deduces that $200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}$. This contradicts maximality of $l$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Assume p_0 ≤ p_1 distinct in L_2
nodes.statement: Suppose that there are ${\mathfrak p}_0, {\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}_0 \ne {\mathfrak p}_1$ and ${\mathfrak p}_0 \le {\mathfrak p}_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume p_0 ≤ p_1 distinct in L_2

nodes.name: 2p_0 ≲ 200p_1
nodes.statement: By \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \Cref{wiggle-order-2}, it follows that $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_1$.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Take a maximal chain
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is finite, there exists a maximal $l \ge 1$ such that there exists a chain $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_1 \lesssim \dotsb \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l$ with all ${\mathfrak p}_i$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ and ${\mathfrak p}_i \ne {\mathfrak p}_{i+1}$ for $i = 0, \dotsc, l-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal chain

nodes.name: Top of chain is not in U_1
nodes.statement: If we have ${\mathfrak p}_l \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, then it follows from $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim {\mathfrak p}_l$ and \eqref{eq-L2-def} that ${\mathfrak p}_0 \not\in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Top of chain is not in U_1
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Find p_{l+1} with larger cube and overlapping balls
nodes.statement: Thus, by the definition \eqref{defunkj} of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak p}_{l+1} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_l) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}) $ and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}_l}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_l), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}), 100)$.
nodes.statement_short: Find p_{l+1} with larger cube and overlapping balls
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: Chain extends: contradiction with maximality
nodes.statement: Using the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, one deduces that $200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}$. This contradicts maximality of $l$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain extends: contradiction with maximality

nodes.name: Proof of L1 L3 antichain
nodes.statement_short: Sets of minimal (resp. maximal) elements are antichains.
nodes.statement: By its definition \eqref{eq-L1-def}, each set ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of minimal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak q}$, then ${\mathfrak q}$ would not be minimal. Hence such ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q}$ do not exist. Similarly, by \eqref{eq-L3-def}, each set ${\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of maximal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak q}$, then ${\mathfrak p}$ would not be maximal.

nodes.name: Proof of Forest Complement Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to tiles meeting G \ G', decompose into antichains with small densities, apply the Antichain Operator Proposition and sum the series.
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p} \not\in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$, then $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap (G \setminus G')) = 0$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{definee1}, it follows that $\mathbf{1}_{G \setminus G'} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = 0$ for almost every $x$. We thus have, almost everywhere, $$ \mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = \mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)\,. $$ Let ${\mathfrak L}(k,n)$ denote any of the terms ${\mathfrak L}_i(k,n,j,l) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{eq-fp'-decomposition}, where the indices $j, l$ may be void. Then ${\mathfrak L}(k,n)$ is an antichain, by Lemmas \ref{L0-antichain},\ref{L2-antichain}, \ref{L1-L3-antichain}. Further, we have \begin{equation*} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak L}(k,n)) \le 2^{4a+1 - n} \end{equation*} by \Cref{C-dens1}, and we have \begin{equation*} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak L}(k,n)) \le 2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}, \end{equation*} since \begin{equation*} {\mathfrak L}(k,n) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} \subset {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'} \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F, G} = \emptyset. \end{equation*} Applying now the triangle inequality according to the decomposition coming from \Cref{antichain-decomposition}, and then applying \Cref{antichain-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} (n + (2n+4) + 2(2n+4) (1+Z(n+1))) \\ \times 2^{117a^3}(q-1)^{-1} (2^{4a+1-n})^{\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} (2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2\,. \end{multline*} Because $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\mathbf{1}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. Using this and \eqref{defineZ}, we bound $$ \le 2^{118a^3} (q - 1)^{-1} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{\frac{1}{q'}} \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} n^2 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}}\,. $$ The last sum equals, by changing the order of summation, $$ \sum_{n \ge 0} n^2(n+1) 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} \le \frac{2^{2a^3}}{(q-1)^4}\,. $$ This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 5.5 Proof of the Forest Complement Lemma

nodes.name: tile disjointness
assumptions: there exists an $x\in X$ with $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\cap E({\mathfrak p}')$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}$. If there exists an $x\in X$ with $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\cap E({\mathfrak p}')$, then ${\mathfrak p}= {\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.label: tile-disjointness

nodes.name: Proof of tile disjointness
nodes.statement_short: A common point forces nested frequency sets, hence p ≤ p'; the antichain property gives p = p'.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'$ and $x$ be given. Assume without loss of generality that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. As we have $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and $x\in E({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ by Definition \eqref{defineep}, we conclude for $i=1,2$ that ${Q}(x)\in{\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${Q}(x)\in{\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. By \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$. By Definition \eqref{straightorder}, we conclude ${\mathfrak p}\le {\mathfrak p}'$. As $\mathfrak{A}$ is an antichain, we conclude ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$. This proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of maximal bound antichain
nodes.statement_short: By tile disjointness at most one T_p f(x) is nonzero; bound it via the kernel size and doubling by the average over B(c(p), 8D^{s(p)}).
nodes.statement: Fix $x\in X$. By \Cref{tile-disjointness}, there is at most one ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}$ such that $T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)$ is not zero. If there is no such ${\mathfrak p}$, the estimate \eqref{hlmbound} follows. Assume there is such a ${\mathfrak p}$. By definition of $T_{{\mathfrak p}}$ we have $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x, {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} Let $y\in X$ with $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)\neq 0$. By Definition \eqref{defks} of $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{1}{4} D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})-1} \leq \rho(x,y) \leq \frac{1}{2} D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} The triangle inequality with \eqref{eqtttt0} and \eqref{supp-Ks1} implies \begin{equation} \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),y) < 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} Using the kernel bound \eqref{eqkernel-size} and the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} we obtain \begin{equation} |K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)|\le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x,\frac 14 D^{{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}-1}))}\, . \end{equation} Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $5 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{5a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\, \end{equation} which, thanks to the closeness of the points $x$ and ${\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})$ shown in \eqref{eqtttt0}, is in turn bounded by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{6a+101a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\, . \end{equation} Using that {$|e({\vartheta})|$} is bounded by $1$ for every ${\vartheta}\in {\Theta}$, we estimate with the triangle inequality and the above information \begin{equation} | T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)| \le \frac{2^{6a+101 a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int _{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} |f(y)|\, dy \end{equation} This together with $a\ge 4$ proves the Lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of dens2 antichain
nodes.statement_short: Hölder on each ball extracts dens_2, then the Hardy–Littlewood bound and Cauchy–Schwarz with the pointwise maximal bound.
nodes.statement: We have $f=\mathbf{1}_Ff$. Using H\"older's inequality, we obtain for each $x\in B'$ and each $B'\in \mathcal{B}$ using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3\tilde{q}-2}}\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} \mathbf{1}_F(y)\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(M_{\mathcal{B}} (|f|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}})(x)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} Taking the maximum over all $B'$ containing $x$, we obtain \begin{equation} M_{\mathcal{B}}|f|\le M_{\mathcal{B},\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2} } |f| \operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} We have with \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} \begin{equation} \left\|M_{\mathcal{B}, \frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}} f\right\|_2\le 2^{2a}(3\tilde{q}-2)(2\tilde{q}-2)^{-1}\|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} Using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ estimates the last display by \begin{equation} 2^{2a+2} (\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} We obtain with Cauchy-Schwarz and then \Cref{maximal-bound-antichain} \begin{equation} |\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)\, d\mu(x)| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \|g\|_2 \Big\| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \Big\|_2 \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3}\|g\|_2 \| M_{\mathcal{B}}f \|_2 \end{equation} With \eqref{eqttt1} and \eqref{eqttt2} we can estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3+2a+2}(\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} Using $a\ge 4$ and $(\tilde q - 1)^{-1} = (q+1)/(q-1) \le 3(q-1)^{-1}$ proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of dens1 antichain
nodes.statement_short: TT* argument: expand the square of the adjoint sum, use the tile correlation estimate, Hölder and the antichain tile count, then Hardy–Littlewood. The key step is the tile counting bound via dens_1.
nodes.statement: We write for the expression inside the absolute values on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqttt3} \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}}\iint \overline{g(x)} \mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x) {K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)}e({Q}(x)(y) - {Q}(x)(x)) f(y)\, d\mu(y)\,d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} \overline{T_{{\mathfrak p}} ^*g(y)} f(y)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with the adjoint operator \begin{equation} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g(y)=\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)}e(-{Q}(x)(y)+ {Q}(x)(x))g(x)\, d\mu(x)\, . \end{equation} We have by expanding the square \begin{equation} \int \Big|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}}T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\Big|^2\, d\mu(y)= \int \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\right) \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}}\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\right)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}} \Big|\int T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} We split the sum into the terms with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Using the symmetry of each summand, we may switch ${\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathfrak p}'$ in the second sum. Using further positivity of each summand to replace the condition ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ by ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ in the second sum, we estimate \eqref{eqtts1} by \begin{equation} \le2 \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}: {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \Big|\int T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} Define for ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}$ \begin{equation} B({\mathfrak p}):=B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \end{equation} and define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p}):=\{{\mathfrak p}'\in\mathfrak{A}: {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\leq {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \land {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B({\mathfrak p})\}. \end{equation} Note that by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} applied $6$ times we have \begin{equation} \mu(B({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{6a} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))\, . \end{equation} Using \Cref{tile-correlation} and \eqref{eqttt4}, we estimate \eqref{eqtts2} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+6a+1} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g|(y) h({\mathfrak p})\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with $h({\mathfrak p})$ defined as \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))}\int \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p})} {(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}}(\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p}')}|g|)(y')\, d\mu(y')\,. \end{equation} Note that $p>4$ since $a\ge 4$. Let $p'$ be the dual exponent of $p$, satisfying $1/p+1/p'=1$. We estimate $h({\mathfrak p})$ as defined in \eqref{def-hp} with H\"older using $|g|\le \mathbf{1}_G$ and $E({\mathfrak p}')\subset B({\mathfrak p})$ by \begin{equation} \frac{\|g\mathbf{1}_{B({\mathfrak p})}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))} \Big\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p})}(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}\mathbf{1}_G\Big\|_{p}\, . \end{equation} Then we apply \Cref{antichain-tile-count} to estimate this by \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a} \frac{\|g\mathbf{1}_{B({\mathfrak p})}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))^{\frac 1p}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{B}'$ be the collection of all balls $B({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$. Then for each ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$ and $x\in B({\mathfrak p})$ we have by definition \eqref{def-hlm} of $M_{\mathcal{B}',p'}$ \begin{equation} \|g\mathbf{1}_{B({\mathfrak p})}\|_{p'}\le \mu(B({\mathfrak p}))^{\frac 1{p'}} M_{\mathcal{B}',p'}g(x) \, . \end{equation} Hence we can estimate \eqref{eqttt5} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a} (M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g(x)) \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\, . \end{equation} With this estimate of $h({\mathfrak p})$, using $E({\mathfrak p})\subset B({\mathfrak p})$ by construction of $B({\mathfrak p})$, we estimate \eqref{eqtts3} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} { \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}}\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g|(y)M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g(y) \, dy\,. \end{equation} Using \Cref{tile-disjointness}, the last display is observed to be \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} {\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}} \int |g|(y)(M_{\mathcal{B}', p'}g)(y) \, dy\,. \end{equation} Applying Cauchy-Schwarz and using \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and $1<p'<\frac 32$ estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+11a + 1} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p} \|g\|_2 \|M_{\mathcal{B}', p'} g\|_2 \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+12a+3} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\|g\|_2 ^2\,. \end{equation} Now \Cref{dens1-antichain} follows by applying Cauchy-Schwarz on the left-hand side and using $a\ge 4$.

nodes.statement_short: Geometric mean: multiply the (2-q)-th power of the dens_2 bound with the (q-1)-th power of the dens_1 bound.
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \left(\frac 1{\tilde{q}} -\frac 12\right) (2-q)= \frac 1q -\frac 12\,. \end{equation} Multiplying the $(2-q)$-th power of \eqref{eqttt9} and the $(q-1)$-th power of \eqref{eqttt3} and estimating gives after simplification of some factors \begin{equation} \Big|\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)\, d\mu(x)\Big| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{117a^3}(q-1)^{-1} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac {q-1}{2p}}\operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{q}-\frac 12} \|f\|_2\|g\|_2\, . \end{equation} With the definition of $p$, this implies \Cref{antichain-operator}.

nodes.statement_short: The product $\overline{K_{s_1}(x_1,\cdot)}K_{s_2}(x_2,\cdot)$ is supported in $B(x_1,D^{s_1})$ with $C^{1/a}$ norm $\lesssim 2^{231a^3}/(\mu(B_1)\mu(B_2))$.
nodes.statement: Let $-S\le s_1\le s_2\le S$ and let $x_1,x_2\in X$. Define \begin{equation} \varphi(y) := \overline{K_{s_1}(x_1, y)} K_{s_2}(x_2, y) \, . \end{equation} If $\varphi(y)\neq 0$, then \begin{equation} y\in B(x_1, D^{s_1})\, . \end{equation} Moreover, we have with $\tau = 1/a$ \begin{equation} \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(x_1, 2 D^{s_1}))}\le \frac{2^{231 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \, . \end{equation}

nodes.statement: If $\varphi(y)$ is not zero, then $K_{s_1}(x_1, y)$ is not zero and thus \eqref{supp-Ks} gives \eqref{eqt10}. We next have for $y$ with \eqref{eq-Ks-size} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)|\le \frac{2^{204 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \end{equation} and for $y'\neq y$ additionally with \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)-\varphi(y')| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le |K_{s_1}(x_1,y)-K_{s_1}(x_1,y'))|| K_{s_2}(x_2, y)| \end{equation} \begin{equation}+|K_{s_1}(x_1, y')| |K_{s_2}(x_2, y) - K_{s_2}(x_2, y'))| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{229 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}+ \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_2}}\right)^{1/a}\right) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{230 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}\,. \end{equation} Adding the estimates \eqref{suppart} and \eqref{holderpart} gives \eqref{eqt11}. This proves the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of tile uncertainty estimate
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality in the frequency metrics combined with the squeezing property, monotonicity and three applications of the doubling property of $d_B$.
nodes.statement: Let $i\in \{1,2\}$. By Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have ${Q}(x_i)\in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}_i)$ With \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we then conclude \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}_i}({Q}(x_i),{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_i)) < 1\, . \end{equation} We have by the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_2),14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_2)})$. Thus, using again \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({Q}(x_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2)) \le 2^{6a} d_{{\mathfrak p}_2}({Q}(x_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2)) \le 2^{6a}\,. \end{equation} By the triangle inequality, we obtain from \eqref{dponetwo} and \eqref{tgeo0.5} \begin{equation} 1+d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2))\le 2 + 2^{6a} +d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} As $x_1\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1)$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} d(x_1,{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_1))\le 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1)\subset B(x_1,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})\, . \end{equation} We thus estimate the right-hand side of \eqref{tgeo1} with monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of the metrics $d_B$ by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} + d_{B(x_1,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} This is further estimated by applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} three times by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} +2^{3a}d_{B_1(x_1, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} Now \eqref{tgeo} follows with $a\ge 4$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Tile Correlation Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to tiles with intersecting balls, expand $T^*T$ by Fubini, apply the Hölder van der Corput lemma with the correlation kernel bound and tile uncertainty; support part via tile range support.
nodes.statement: We begin with \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. By Lemma \ref{tile-range-support}, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} vanishes if $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) = \emptyset$. Thus we can assume for the remainder of the proof that \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \neq \emptyset\,. \end{equation} We expand the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} as \begin{equation} \left|\int \int_{E({\mathfrak p}')} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}(x_1,y)}e(-{Q}(x_1)(y)+ {Q}(x_1)(x_1))g(x_1)\, d\mu(x_1) \right. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \times \left.\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} {K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x_2,y)}e({Q}(x_2)(y) -{Q}(x_2)(x_2))\overline{g(x_2)}\, d\mu(x_2)\, d\mu(y)\right|\, . \end{equation} By Fubini and the triangle inequality and the fact $|e({Q}(x_i)(x_i))|=1$ for $i=1,2$, we can estimate \eqref{tstartstar} and \eqref{tstartstar'} from above by \begin{equation} \int_{E({\mathfrak p}')} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2)\, d\mu(x_1)d\mu(x_2)\,. \end{equation} with \begin{equation} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2):= \left|\int e(-{Q}(x_1)(y)+{Q}(x_2)(y))\varphi_{x_1,x_2}(y) d\mu(y) \, g(x_1)g(x_2)\right| \end{equation} We estimate for fixed $x_1\in E({\mathfrak p}')$ and $x_2\in E({\mathfrak p})$ the inner integral of \eqref{eqa1} with \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput}. The function $\varphi:=\varphi_{x_1,x_2}$ satisfies the assumptions of \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with $z = x_1$ and $R = D^{s_1}$ by \Cref{correlation-kernel-bound}. We obtain with $B':= B(x_1, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})$, \begin{equation*} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2) \le 2^{8a} \mu(B') \|{\varphi}\|_{C^\tau(B')} (1 + d_{B'}({Q}(x_1),{Q}(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)| \end{equation*} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3+8a}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} (1 + d_{B'}({Q}(x_1),{Q}(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,. \end{equation} Using \eqref{intersec5B}, \Cref{tile-uncertainty} and $a\ge 1$ estimates \eqref{eqa1.5} by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3 + 8a + 1}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} (1+d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p})))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)|\,. \end{equation} As $x_2\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x_2,{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) < 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset B(x_2,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation} Using three iterations of the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} give \begin{equation} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{3a}\mu(B(x_2,D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\, . \end{equation} With $a\ge 4$ and \eqref{eqa2} we conclude \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. Now assume the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} is not zero. There is a $y\in X$ with \begin{equation} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)}\neq 0 \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \Cref{tile-range-support}, we conclude \begin{equation} \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'))\le \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),y) +\rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),y) \le 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}+5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}\le 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} By the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, we conclude \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation} This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{tile-correlation}.

nodes.statement_short: Monotone cube metrics and triangle inequality, then doubling (five times, then $5a+2$ times) to show the ball inclusion $B_{\mathfrak p'}(\mathcal Q(\mathfrak p'),2^{N+2})\subset B_{\mathfrak p}(\mathcal Q(\mathfrak p),2^{N+2})$.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we have \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}) \le 2^{N} \, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{eqassumedismfa} and the triangle inequality, we obtain \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{N+1} \, . \end{equation} Now assume \begin{equation} {\vartheta}'\in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),2^{N+2}). \end{equation} By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, applied five times, we have \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} We have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})\in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})\, . \end{equation} Hence by the triangle inequality \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})\, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{ageo1} and monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of $d$ \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} Using the doubling property \eqref{seconddb} $5a+2$ times gives \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),2^{2-5a^2-2a}D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} Using ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ and $a\ge 4$ gives \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} With the triangle inequality and \eqref{eqdistqpqp}, \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N+2}\, . \end{equation} This shows \begin{equation} B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),2^{N+2})\subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),2^{N+2})\, . \end{equation} This implies \eqref{lp'lp''} and completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of stack density
nodes.statement_short: Bound each tile by $\mathrm{dens}_1$; count the tiles over $L$ by covering the $2^{N+1}$-ball with $2^{a(N+4)}$ balls of radius 0.2, each containing at most one $\mathcal Q(\mathfrak p')$ by disjointness of the $\Omega$.
nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta},N,L$ be given and set \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}':=\{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}:{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L\}\, . \end{equation} Let ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$. We have by Definition \eqref{definedens1} using $\lambda=2$ and the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} \begin{equation} \mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G)\le \mu(E_2(2, {\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{a}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}')\mu(L)\, . \end{equation} By the covering property \eqref{thirddb}, applied $N+4$ times, there is a collection ${\Theta}'$ of at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements such that \begin{equation} B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}, 2^{N+1})\subset \bigcup_{{\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'} B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)\, . \end{equation} As each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')$ with ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ is contained in the left-hand-side of \eqref{eqanti-4} by definition (because ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))$, it is in at least one $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)$ with ${\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'$. For two different ${\mathfrak p}',{\mathfrak p}''\in \mathfrak{A}'$, we have by \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} that ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}'')$ are disjoint and thus by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we have for every ${\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'$ \begin{equation} {\vartheta}'\not\in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)\cap B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)\, . \end{equation} Hence at most one of ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is in $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)$. It follows that there are at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements in $\mathfrak{A}'$. Adding \eqref{eqanti-3} over $\mathfrak{A}'$ proves \eqref{eqanti-1}.

By definition of $E$, the tile contributes zero to the sum on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqanti-0.5} unless ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}) \neq \emptyset$, which we may assume. With ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we conclude ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. We conclude from ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ that \begin{equation} {\vartheta} \in B_{\mathfrak p}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 2^{N+1})\, . \end{equation} With \Cref{tile-reach} and the assumption on ${\mathfrak p}_{\vartheta}$, we conclude \begin{equation} 2^{N+3}{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}} \lesssim 2^{N+3}{\mathfrak p} \, . \end{equation} By Definition \eqref{definee2} of $E_2$, we conclude \begin{equation} E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}) \subset E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})\, . \end{equation} Using disjointedness of the various $E({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness}, we obtain \eqref{eqanti-0.5}. This proves the lemma.

{Fix ${\vartheta}$ and $N$. Let $\mathfrak{A}'$ be the set of ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$ is not empty and $s({\mathfrak p}) > -S$. Let $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$ be the set of ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$ is not empty and $s({\mathfrak p}) = -S$ } Then we have  egin{equation*} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) = \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) + \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) \end{equation*} We start by estimating the contribution of $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. They all have scale $-S$, by definition of $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$, and hence they are pairwise disjoint by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}. We write \[ \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) = \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}, {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L} \mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G), \] and using \Cref{stack-density}, we estimate  egin{equation} \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \mu(L) \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}ight). \end{equation} We turn to $\mathfrak{A}'$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes $I\in\mathcal{D}$ such that $I \le {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ for some ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$ and such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})
ot \subset I$ for all ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, for each ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'$ and each $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$, there is $I\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I)=-S$ and $x\in I$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Since for all ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{A}'$ we have $s({\mathfrak p}') > -S$, we have $I \in \mathcal{L}$. Hence  egin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset  igcup\{I\in \mathcal{D}: s(I)=-S, I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\}\subset  igcup \mathcal{L}\, . \end{equation} As each $I\in \mathcal{L}$ satisfies $I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ for some ${\mathfrak p}$ in $\mathfrak{A'}$, we conclude  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}= igcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, . \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{L}^*$ be the set of maximal elements in $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to set inclusion. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the elements in $\mathcal{L}^*$ are pairwise disjoint and we have  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}^*= igcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, . \end{equation} Using the partition \eqref{eqdecAprime} into elements of $\mathcal{L}$ in \eqref{eqanti0}, it suffices to show for each $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$  egin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap L) \le 2^{101a^3+aN} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L)\,. \end{equation} Fix $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$. Pick such an element ${\mathfrak p}'$ in $\mathfrak{A}$ with minimal ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. As ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')
ot \subset L$ by definition of $L$, we have with \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $s(L)< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. In particular $s(L)<S$, thus $L 
e I_0$ and hence by \eqref{subsetmaxcube} there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subsetneq J$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there is an $L'\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $L \le L'$. eq L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L)\, , \end{equation} We first estimate \eqref{eqanti1} with \Cref{stack-density} by  egin{equation} \le \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L')\le 2^{a(N+5)}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\, . \end{equation} We turn to \eqref{eqanti2}. e L'$, then it follows that $s({\mathfrak p}'') < s(L')$. eq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $s(L)<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and thus $s(L')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} again, we have $L'\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. As $L'
eq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, we conclude $s(L)<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By \Cref{local-antichain-density}, we can thus estimate \eqref{eqanti2} by  egin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})
eq L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L') \le \mu (E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}))\, . \end{equation} With the decomposition in \eqref{eqanti1} and \eqref{eqanti2} and the estimates \eqref{equanti1.5}, \eqref{eqanti-0.5}, \eqref{pmfadens} we obtain the estimate  egin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap L) \le (2^{a(N+5)}+2^{Na+3a})\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\,. \end{equation} Using $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $100a^2+4$ times , we obtain  egin{equation} \mu(L')\le 2^{100a^3+4a}\mu(L)\, . \end{equation} Inserting in \eqref{eqanti3.14}, adding the estimate \eqref{eq_minus_S} and using $a\ge 4$ gives \eqref{eqanti0}. This completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 1
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathfrak A_{\vartheta,N}$ into $\mathfrak A'$ and $\mathfrak A_{-S}$ and decompose the sum
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 2
nodes.statement:
We start by estimating the contribution of $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$ be the
collection of dyadic cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. They all have scale $-S$,
by definition of $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$, and hence they are pairwise disjoint by the dyadic property
\eqref{dyadicproperty}.
nodes.statement_short: Bottom-scale cubes $\mathcal L_{-S}$ are disjoint
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 3
nodes.statement:
We write
\[
    \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G)
    = \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}, {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L} \mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G),
\]
and using \Cref{stack-density}, we estimate
\begin{equation} \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \mu(L)
    \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}\right).
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Stack density bounds the $\mathfrak A_{-S}$ part
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: Equation (eq_minus_S)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \mu(L) \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}\right).
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma
nodes.label: eq_minus_S

nodes.name: globanti step 4
nodes.statement:
We turn to $\mathfrak{A}'$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes $I\in\mathcal{D}$ such that $I \le {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$
for some ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$ and such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\not \subset I$ for all ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the collection $\mathcal L$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 5
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{coverdyadic}, for each ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'$
and each $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$, there is $I\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I)=-S$ and $x\in I$.
By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Since for all ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{A}'$ we
have $s({\mathfrak p}') > -S$, we have $I \in \mathcal{L}$. Hence
\begin{equation}
    {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset \bigcup\{I\in \mathcal{D}: s(I)=-S, I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\}\subset \bigcup \mathcal{L}\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cubes of $\mathfrak A'$ are covered by $\bigcup\mathcal L$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: Unlabelled display in F532 (line 4452)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset \bigcup\{I\in \mathcal{D}: s(I)=-S, I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\}\subset \bigcup \mathcal{L}\, .
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.statement_short: $\bigcup\mathcal L$ equals the union of the cubes

nodes.statement: \bigcup\mathcal{L}=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, .

nodes.name: globanti step 7
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}^*$ be the set of maximal elements in $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to set inclusion.
By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the elements in $\mathcal{L}^*$ are pairwise disjoint and we have
 \begin{equation} \bigcup\mathcal{L}^*=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, .
   \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Maximal elements $\mathcal L^*$ partition the union
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.statement: \bigcup\mathcal{L}^*=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, .
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.statement_short: Suffices to bound each $L\in\mathcal L^*$

nodes.name: globanti step 9
nodes.statement:
Fix $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$. By definition of $\mathcal{L}^*$, there exists an element ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}'$
such that $L\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Pick such an element ${\mathfrak p}'$ in $\mathfrak{A}$ with
minimal ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. As ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\not \subset L$ by definition of $L$,
we have with \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $s(L)< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $L$ and a minimal-scale $\mathfrak p'$ above it

nodes.name: globanti step 10
nodes.statement:
In particular $s(L)<S$, thus $L \ne I_0$ and hence by \eqref{subsetmaxcube}
there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subsetneq J$.
By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there is an $L'\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $L \le L'$.
By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $L\subset L'$.
nodes.statement_short: Find the parent cube $L'$ of $L$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.statement_short: Split by whether $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)=L'$

nodes.statement: \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L)

nodes.label: eqanti1

nodes.statement: + \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L)\, ,

nodes.statement_short: Stack density for the first part

nodes.name: Equation (equanti1.5)
nodes.statement: \le \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L')\le 2^{a(N+5)}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\, .
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 13
nodes.statement:
We turn to \eqref{eqanti2}.
Consider the element ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ as above
with $L\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $s(L)<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$.
As $L\subset L'$ and $s(L')=s(L)+1$, we conclude with the dyadic property that $L'\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$.
By maximality of $L$, we have
$L'\not\in \mathcal{L}$.
This together with the existence of the given ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}$
with $L'\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$
shows by definition of $\mathcal{L}$ that there exists ${\mathfrak p}''\in \mathfrak{A}'$ with
${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')\subset L'$.
nodes.statement_short: Find $\mathfrak p''$ with cube inside $L'$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 14
nodes.statement_short: Case $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p'')=L'$: take $\mathfrak p_\vartheta=\mathfrak p''$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.statement: {\vartheta} \in B({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 2^{N+1})\, .

nodes.statement_short: Otherwise choose $\mathfrak p_\vartheta$ over $L'$ and apply tile reach

nodes.statement_short: In both cases $\vartheta$ is in the ball of $\mathfrak p_\vartheta$

nodes.name: Unlabelled display in F532 (line 4527)
nodes.statement: {\vartheta}\in B_{{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}), 2^{N+1}).
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 17
nodes.statement:
As ${\mathfrak p}''\in \mathfrak{A}'$, we have by Definition
\eqref{definedens1} of $\operatorname{dens}_1$ that
\begin{equation} \mu(E_2(2^{N+3}, {\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}))\le 2^{Na+3a}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) {\mu(L')}\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{dens}_1$ bounds $\mu(E_2)$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: Equation (pmfadens)
nodes.statement: \mu(E_2(2^{N+3}, {\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}))\le 2^{Na+3a}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) {\mu(L')}\, .
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma
nodes.label: pmfadens

nodes.name: globanti step 18
nodes.statement:
Now let ${\mathfrak p}$ be any tile in the summation set in \eqref{eqanti2}, that is, ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq L'$.
Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap L\neq \emptyset$. It follows by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}
and the definition of $L$ that
$L\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and $L\neq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have
$s(L)<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and thus $s(L')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By the dyadic property
   \eqref{dyadicproperty} again, we have $L'\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$.
As $L'\neq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, we conclude $s(L)<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: Tiles of the second sum lie strictly above $L'$
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma

nodes.name: globanti step 19
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{local-antichain-density}, we can thus estimate \eqref{eqanti2} by
\begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L')
    \le \mu (E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}))\, .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Local antichain density for the second part

nodes.statement: \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}':{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\neq L'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G\cap L') \le \mu (E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}))\, .
nodes.section: 6.3 Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma
nodes.label: eqanti0.5

nodes.name: globanti step 20
nodes.statement:
With the decomposition in \eqref{eqanti1} and \eqref{eqanti2} and the
estimates \eqref{equanti1.5}, \eqref{eqanti-0.5}, \eqref{pmfadens} we obtain
the estimate
\begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap L)
    \le (2^{a(N+5)}+2^{Na+3a})\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L')\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two estimates

Inserting in \eqref{eqanti3.14}, adding the estimate \eqref{eq_minus_S} and using $a\ge 4$ gives \eqref{eqanti0}.

nodes.name: Proof of the Antichain Tile Count Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\mathfrak A$ into the layers $\mathfrak A_{\vartheta,N}$, use disjointness of the $E(\mathfrak p)$ to compute $p$-th powers, apply global antichain density and sum the geometric series in $N$.
nodes.statement: Using that $\mathfrak{A}$ is the disjoint union of the $\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ with $N\ge 0$, we estimate the left-hand side \eqref{eq-antichain-Lp} with the triangle inequality by \begin{equation} \le \sum_{N\ge 0} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})} \mathbf{1}_G\right\|_{p} \end{equation} We consider each individual term in this sum and estimate its $p$-th power. Using that for each $x\in X$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness} there is at most one ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$ with $x\in E({\mathfrak p})$, we have \begin{equation} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})} \mathbf{1}_G\right\|_{p}^p \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\Big(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})\cap G}(x)\Big)^p\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)}\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})\cap G}(x)\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} = 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) \end{equation} Using \Cref{global-antichain-density}, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)+101a^3+Na}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right) \end{equation} Using that $a\ge 4$ and since $p = 4a^4$, we have $$ pN/(2a^2+a^3)\ge 4a^4N/(3a^3) \ge Na+N\, . $$ Hence we have for \eqref{eqanti21} the upper bound $$ \le 2^{101a^3-N}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)\, . $$ Taking the $p$-th root and summing over $N\ge 0$ gives for \eqref{eqanti23} the upper bound $$ \le \left(\sum_{N\ge 0} 2^{-N/p}\right)2^{101a^3/p}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{{\frac{1}{p}}}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)^{{\frac{1}{p}}} $$ $$ = \left(1-2^{-1/p}\right)^{-1} 2^{101a^3/p} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)^{\frac 1p}\, . $$ Using that $p = 4a^4$ and $a \ge 4$, this proves the lemma.

$$
    = \left(1-2^{-1/p}\right)^{-1} 2^{101a^3/p} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)^{\frac 1p}\, .
$$
Using that $p = 4a^4$ and $a \ge 4$, this proves the lemma.
