nodes.name: Scale set $\sigma(\mathfrak u,x)$
nodes.statement:
For ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and $x\in X$, we define
$$
    \sigma ({\mathfrak u}, x):=\{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}):{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}), x\in E({\mathfrak p})\}\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: $\sigma(\mathfrak u,x)$ is the set of scales of tiles in $\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u)$ whose set $E(\mathfrak p)$ contains $x$.

nodes.name: Maximal and minimal scales $\overline\sigma$, $\underline\sigma$
nodes.statement:
We set
$$
    \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x) := \max \sigma({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}), x)
$$
$$
    \underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x) := \min\sigma({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}), x)\,.
$$

nodes.name: convex scales
nodes.statement_short: The scale set $\sigma(\mathfrak u,x)$ is an integer interval.
conclusions: \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x) = \mathbb{Z} \cap [\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x), \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)]\,.
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, we have $$ \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x) = \mathbb{Z} \cap [\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x), \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)]\,. $$
nodes.label: convex-scales

nodes.name: Proof of convex scales
nodes.statement_short: For an intermediate scale, pick a cube and tile between the extremal tiles; convexity of $\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u)$ puts it in the tree.
nodes.statement: Let $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x) \le s \le \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition of $\sigma$, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = \underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$, and there exists ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}'') = \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By property \eqref{coverdyadic} of the dyadic grid, there exists a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ with $x \in I$. By property \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ with ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$. Thus ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$, which gives with the convexity property \eqref{forest2} of ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, so $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$.

nodes.name: convscales step 1
nodes.statement: Let $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x) \le s \le \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition of $\sigma$, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = \underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$, and there exists ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}'') = \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$.
nodes.statement_short: Take extremal tiles at scales $\underline\sigma$, $\overline\sigma$

nodes.name: convscales step 2
nodes.statement: By property \eqref{coverdyadic} of the dyadic grid, there exists a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ with $x \in I$. By property \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ with ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct an intermediate tile $\mathfrak p'$ at scale $s$

nodes.name: convscales step 3
nodes.statement: By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: Nesting of cubes and frequency sets

nodes.name: convscales step 4
nodes.statement: Thus ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$, which gives with the convexity property \eqref{forest2} of ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, so $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of the tree gives $s\in\sigma$

nodes.name: Collection $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement:
For a nonempty collection of tiles $\mathfrak{S} \subset {\mathfrak P}$ we define
$$
    \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})
$$
to be the collection of all dyadic cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ such that $s(J) = -S$ or
$$
    {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})
$$
for all ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
differentia: $s(J) = -S$ or $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1}) $$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$
nodes.statement_short: Cubes of bottom scale or not containing any tile cube in their $100D^{s+1}$-ball.

nodes.name: Collection $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ to be the collection of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.name: Collection $\mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement:
We further define
$$
    \mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})
$$
to be the collection of dyadic cubes $L \in \mathcal{D}$ such that $s(L) = -S$, or there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and there exists no ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L$.
nodes.statement_short: Cubes of bottom scale, or inside some tile cube of $\mathfrak S$ but containing none.

nodes.name: Collection $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$
nodes.statement: We define $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$ to be the collection of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{L}_0(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.name: dyadic partitions
nodes.statement_short: Both $\mathcal J(\mathfrak S)$ and $\mathcal L(\mathfrak S)$ partition the union of all dyadic cubes.
nodes.statement: For each $\mathfrak{S} \subset {\mathfrak P}$, we have \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})}} J \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})}} L\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: dyadic-partitions

nodes.name: Equation (eq-J-partition)
nodes.statement: \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})}} J
nodes.label: eq-J-partition

nodes.name: Equation (eq-L-partition)
nodes.statement: \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})}} L\,.
nodes.label: eq-L-partition

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partitions
nodes.statement_short: Maximal cubes are disjoint by the dyadic property; every point lies in a bottom-scale cube, which lies in a maximal one.
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ is the set of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$, cubes in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{dyadicproperty}. The same applies to $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$. If $x \in \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, then there exists by \eqref{coverdyadic} a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in I$ and $s(I) = -S$. Then $I \in \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$. There exists an inclusion maximal cube in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$ containing $I$. This cube contains $x$ and is contained in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$. This shows one inclusion in \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the other one follows from $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \subset \mathcal{D}$. The proof of the two inclusions in \eqref{eq-L-partition} is similar.

nodes.name: dyadpart step 1
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ is the set of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$, cubes in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{dyadicproperty}. The same applies to $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximal cubes are pairwise disjoint

nodes.name: dyadpart step 2
nodes.statement: If $x \in \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, then there exists by \eqref{coverdyadic} a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in I$ and $s(I) = -S$. Then $I \in \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$. There exists an inclusion maximal cube in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$ containing $I$. This cube contains $x$ and is contained in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$. This shows one inclusion in \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the other one follows from $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \subset \mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: Covering: each point lies in a maximal cube of $\mathcal J_0$

nodes.name: dyadpart step 3
nodes.statement: The proof of the two inclusions in \eqref{eq-L-partition} is similar.
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathcal L$ case is analogous

nodes.name: Projection operator $P_{\mathcal{C}}$
nodes.statement:
For a finite collection of pairwise disjoint cubes $\mathcal{C}$, define the projection operator
$$
    P_{\mathcal{C}}f(x) :=\sum_{J\in\mathcal{C}}\mathbf{1}_J(x) \frac{1}{\mu(J)}\int_J f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: $P_{\mathcal C}f$ replaces $f$ on each cube $J\in\mathcal C$ by its average.

nodes.name: Dyadic cube $I_s(x)$ of scale $s$ containing $x$
nodes.statement: Given a scale $-S \le s\le S$ and a point $x \in \bigcup_{I\in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s} I$, there exists a unique cube in $\mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ containing $x$ by \eqref{coverdyadic}. We denote it by $I_s(x)$.

nodes.name: Nontangential maximal operator $T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\vartheta}$
nodes.statement_short: Supremum over $x'\in I_{s_1}(x)$ and admissible scale ranges $s_1\le s_2$ of the truncated kernel sums $|\sum_{s_1}^{s_2}\int K_s(x',y)f(y)|$.

nodes.name: Equation (eq-TN-def)
nodes.statement: T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\vartheta} f(x) := \sup_{-S \le s_1 < S} \sup_{x' \in I_{s_1}(x)} \sup_{\substack{s_1 \le s_2 \le S\\ D^{s_2-1} \le R_Q({\vartheta}, x')}} \left| \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \int K_s(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|\,.
nodes.label: eq-TN-def

nodes.name: Auxiliary operator $S_{1,\mathfrak u}$
nodes.statement:
Define for each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ the auxiliary operator
$$
    S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f(x)
$$
\begin{equation} :=\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \mathbf{1}_{I}(x) \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\
    J\subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} \frac{D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a}}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over cubes $I$ of averages of $|f|$ over smaller cubes $J\in\mathcal J(\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u))$ near $I$, weighted by $D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}$.

nodes.name: Equation (eq-def-S-op)
nodes.statement: :=\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \mathbf{1}_{I}(x) \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\ J\subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} \frac{D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a}}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
nodes.label: eq-def-S-op

nodes.name: Collection of balls $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement:
Define also the collection of balls
$$
    \mathcal{B} = \{B(c(I), 2^s D^{s(I)+t}) \ : \ I \in \mathcal{D}\,, 0 \le s \le S + 5\,, 0 \le t \le 2S+3\}\,.
$$

nodes.name: pointwise tree estimate
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bound of the tree operator on $L\in\mathcal L(\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u))$ by $M_{\mathcal B,1}$, $S_{1,\mathfrak u}$ and $T_{\mathcal N}$ applied to $P_{\mathcal J}f$ at any $x'\in L$.
conclusions: \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,{\mathfrak u}})P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}f(x')|,
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Let $x, x' \in L$. Then for all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support $$ \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x)\right| $$ \begin{equation} \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,{\mathfrak u}})P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}f(x')|, \end{equation}
nodes.label: pointwise-tree-estimate

nodes.name: Equation (eq-LJ-ptwise)
nodes.statement: \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,{\mathfrak u}})P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}f(x')|,
nodes.label: eq-LJ-ptwise

nodes.name: Proof of the pointwise tree estimate
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the tree sum over the scale set and split by the triangle inequality into three terms, bounded by the first, second and third tree pointwise lemmas.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp}, if $T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x) \ne 0$, then $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Combining this with $|e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x))| = 1$, we obtain $$ |\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x)| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{multline*} Using the triangle inequality, we bound this by the sum of three terms: \begin{multline} \le \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int (e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))-1)\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{multline} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{equation} The proof is completed using the bounds for these three terms proven respectively in \Cref{first-tree-pointwise}, \Cref{second-tree-pointwise} and \Cref{third-tree-pointwise}.

nodes.name: ptwtree step 1
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{definetp}, if $T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x) \ne 0$, then $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Combining this with $|e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x))| = 1$, we obtain
    $$
        |\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x)|
    $$
    \begin{multline*}
        = \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))\times\\
        K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,.
    \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the tree sum as a sum over $\sigma(\mathfrak u,x)$

nodes.name: ptwtree step 2
nodes.statement_short: Split into three terms

nodes.name: Equation (eq-term-A)
nodes.statement: \le \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int (e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))-1)\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|
nodes.label: eq-term-A

nodes.name: Equation (eq-term-B)
nodes.statement: + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|
nodes.label: eq-term-B

nodes.name: Equation (eq-term-C)
nodes.statement: + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,.
nodes.label: eq-term-C

nodes.name: ptwtree step 3
nodes.statement: The proof is completed using the bounds for these three terms proven respectively in \Cref{first-tree-pointwise}, \Cref{second-tree-pointwise} and \Cref{third-tree-pointwise}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the three tree pointwise lemmas

nodes.name: first tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: The phase-difference term (eq-term-A) is bounded by $10\cdot2^{104a^3}M_{\mathcal B,1}P_{\mathcal J}|f|(x')$.
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 10 \cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. $$
nodes.label: first-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of first tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: Bound the phase difference by the frequency metric, which decays geometrically below the top scale; then replace $|f|$ by its $\mathcal J$-projection and dominate by the maximal function $M_{\mathcal B,1}$. The key step shows every relevant $J$ has $s(J)\le s$ and lies in $B(c(\mathfrak p_s),16D^s)$.
nodes.statement:
Let $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u},x)$. If $x, y \in X$ are such that $K_s(x,y)
eq 0$, then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, we have $ho(x,y)\leq 1/2 D^s$. By $1$-Lipschitz continuity of the function $t \mapsto \exp(it) = e(t)$ and the property \eqref{osccontrol} of the metrics $d_B$, it follows that  egin{multline*} |e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y)+{Q}(x)(y)+{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x)-{Q}(x)(x))-1|\ \leq d_{B(x, 1/2 D^{s})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x))\,. \end{multline*} Let ${\mathfrak p}_s \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_s) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s)$, and let ${\mathfrak p}'$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$. Using the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb}, the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} repeatedly, the definition of $d_{{\mathfrak p}}$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we can bound the previous display by $$ d_{B(x, 4 D^{s})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \leq 2^{4a} d_{{\mathfrak p}_s}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x))\,. $$ Since ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}) \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 4)$ by \eqref{forest1} and ${Q}(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}') \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 1)$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, this is estimated by $$ \le 5 \cdot 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \,. $$ Using \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, it follows that $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B(x,0.5D^{s})}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $ igcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this is estimated by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\sum_{\substack{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J \cap B(x, 0.5D^s) 
e \emptyset} }\int_{J}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ This expression does not change if we replace $|f|$ by $P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|$. Let $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with $B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. By the triangle inequality and since $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4D^{s})$, it follows that $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. Thus we always have $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16 D^s)$. Thus we can continue our chain of estimates with $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16 D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ We have $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \subset B(x, 32D^s)$, by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, since $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$. Combining this with the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain $$ \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^s))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$, it follows that \eqref{eq-term-A} is bounded by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Since $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ and $x\in L \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$, we have $s(L) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$. It follows by \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$, in particular $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)$. Thus $$ \le 5\cdot 2^{104a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x') $$ $$ \le 10\cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. $$ This completes the estimate for term \eqref{eq-term-A}.

nodes.name: firsttree step 1
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz bound of the phase difference by $d_B$

nodes.name: firsttree step 2
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p}_s \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_s) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s)$, and let ${\mathfrak p}'$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$.
    Using the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb}, the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} repeatedly, the definition of $d_{{\mathfrak p}}$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we can bound the previous display by
    $$
        d_{B(x, 4 D^{s})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \leq 2^{4a} d_{{\mathfrak p}_s}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Geometric decay of the metric below the top scale

nodes.name: firsttree step 3
nodes.statement:
Since ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}) \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 4)$ by \eqref{forest1} and ${Q}(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}') \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 1)$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, this is estimated by
    $$
        \le 5 \cdot 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Forest property bounds the distance by 5

nodes.name: firsttree step 4
nodes.statement:
Using \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, it follows that
    $$
        \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B(x,0.5D^{s})}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Kernel size bound

nodes.name: firsttree step 5
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $\bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this is estimated by
    $$
         5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\sum_{\substack{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\J \cap B(x, 0.5D^s) \ne \emptyset} }\int_{J}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
    This expression does not change if we replace $|f|$ by $P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the $\mathcal J$-partition and pass to $P_{\mathcal J}|f|$

nodes.name: firsttree step 6
nodes.statement: Let $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with $B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J \ne \emptyset$. By the triangle inequality and since $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4D^{s})$, it follows that $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J \ne \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a relevant cube $J$

nodes.name: firsttree step 7
nodes.statement: If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. Thus we always have $s(J) \le s$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximality of $J$ forces $s(J)\le s$

nodes.name: firsttree step 8
nodes.statement: It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16 D^s)$.
nodes.statement_short: $J\subset B(c(\mathfrak p_s),16D^s)$

nodes.name: firsttree step 9
nodes.statement:
Thus we can continue our chain of estimates with
    $$
        5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16 D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Continue the chain of estimates

nodes.name: firsttree step 10
nodes.statement:
We have $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \subset B(x, 32D^s)$, by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, since $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$. Combining this with the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain
    $$
        \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^s))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling compares ball measures

nodes.name: firsttree step 11
nodes.statement:
Since $a \ge 4$, it follows that \eqref{eq-term-A} is bounded by
    $$
        5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \frac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite as averages over balls

nodes.name: firsttree step 12
nodes.statement:
Since $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ and $x\in L \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$, we have $s(L) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$. It follows by \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$, in particular $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)$. Thus
    $$
        \le 5\cdot 2^{104a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')
    $$
    $$
        \le 10\cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,.
    $$
    This completes the estimate for term \eqref{eq-term-A}.
nodes.statement_short: Dominate by $M_{\mathcal B,1}$ at $x'$ and sum the geometric series

nodes.name: second tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: The projected kernel sum over $\sigma(\mathfrak u,x)$ is bounded by $T_{\mathcal N}^{\mathcal Q(\mathfrak u)}P_{\mathcal J}f(x')$.
conclusions: \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \le T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(x')\,.
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \le T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(x')\,. $$
nodes.label: second-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of second tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: Check that the scale range $[\underline\sigma,\overline\sigma]$ and the point $x$ are admissible in the supremum defining $T_{\mathcal N}$, using the doubling properties of $d_B$.
nodes.statement: Let $s_1 = \underline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s_1$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap L$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, it follows that $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, in particular $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so $x \in I_{s_1}(x')$. Next, let $s_2 = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and let ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = s_2$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$. Since ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have $4{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$. Since ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$, it follows that $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5\,. $$ Applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} five times, we obtain $$ d_{B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have $B(x, D^{s_2}) \subset B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{s_2})$, so by \eqref{monotonedb} $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ Finally, by applying \eqref{seconddb} $100a$ times, we obtain $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2-1})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{-95a} < 1\,. $$ Consequently, $D^{s_2 - 1} < R_Q({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), x)$. The lemma now follows from the definition of $T_{\mathcal{N}}$.

nodes.name: secondtree step 1
nodes.statement: Let $s_1 = \underline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s_1$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap L$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, it follows that $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, in particular $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so $x \in I_{s_1}(x')$.
nodes.statement_short: Lowest scale: $x\in I_{s_1}(x')$

nodes.name: secondtree step 2
nodes.statement:
Next, let $s_2 = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and let ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = s_2$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$. Since ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have $4{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$. Since ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$, it follows that
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Top scale tile: $d_{\mathfrak p}(\mathcal Q(\mathfrak u),Q(x))\le5$

nodes.name: secondtree step 3
nodes.statement:
Applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} five times, we obtain
    $$
        d_{B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling five times

nodes.name: secondtree step 4
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality, we have $B(x, D^{s_2}) \subset B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{s_2})$, so by \eqref{monotonedb}
    $$
        d_{B(x, D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $d_B$

nodes.name: secondtree step 5
nodes.statement:
Finally, by applying \eqref{seconddb} $100a$ times, we obtain
    $$
        d_{B(x, D^{s_2-1})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{-95a} < 1\,.
    $$
    Consequently, $D^{s_2 - 1} < R_Q({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), x)$.

nodes.name: secondtree step 6
nodes.statement: The lemma now follows from the definition of $T_{\mathcal{N}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Definition of $T_{\mathcal N}$

nodes.name: third tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: The kernel sum applied to $f-P_{\mathcal J}f$ is bounded by $2^{128a^3}S_{1,\mathfrak u}P_{\mathcal J}|f|(x')$.
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have \begin{equation*} \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \le 2^{128a^3} S_{1,{\mathfrak u}} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: third-tree-pointwise

nodes.name: Proof of third tree pointwise
nodes.statement_short: Cancellation on each cube $J$ with the kernel smoothness bound; show relevant cubes are small and near $x$, then reorganize the sum by cubes $I$ to get $S_{1,\mathfrak u}$.
nodes.statement:
We have for $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$: $$ \int_J K_{s}(x,y)(1 - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))})f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$  egin{equation} = \int_J  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} By \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have for $y, z \in J$ $$ |K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z)| \le  rac{2^{127a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \left( rac{8 D^{s(J)}}{D^s}ight)^{1/a}\,. $$ Suppose that $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$. If $K_s(x,y) 
e 0$ for some $y \in J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, $y \in B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$ by the triangle inequality. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. So in both cases, $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B(x, 16 D^s)$. Thus, we can estimate \eqref{eq-term-C} by $$ 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}} rac{\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x,D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\ s(J) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}} D^{(s(J) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ $$ = 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}\ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I}} rac{\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} and \eqref{defineep}, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for tiles ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I$ are pairwise disjoint. It follows from the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ if and only if $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, thus we can estimate the sum over $\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)$ by $\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')$. If $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ then in particular $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} $B(c(I),16D^{s(I)}) \subset B(x, 32D^{s(I)})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ \mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$ we can continue our estimate with $$ \le 2^{128a^3}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}}  rac{\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f| $$ $$ = 2^{128a^3} S_{1,{\mathfrak u}} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. $$ This completes the proof.

nodes.name: thirdtree step 1
nodes.statement:
We have for $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$:
    $$
        \int_J K_{s}(x,y)(1 - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))})f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    \begin{equation} = \int_J \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite using the mean-zero property of $1-P_{\mathcal J}$ on $J$

nodes.name: Equation (eq-canc-comp)
nodes.statement: = \int_J \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
nodes.label: eq-canc-comp

nodes.name: thirdtree step 2
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have for $y, z \in J$
    $$
        |K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z)| \le \frac{2^{127a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \left(\frac{8 D^{s(J)}}{D^s}\right)^{1/a}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Kernel smoothness bound on $J$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 3
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$.
    If $K_s(x,y) 
e 0$ for some $y \in J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, $y \in B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$ by the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Take a relevant cube $J$ and tile $\mathfrak p$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 4
nodes.statement: If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. So in both cases, $s(J) \le s$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximality of $J$ forces $s(J)\le s$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 5
nodes.statement: It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B(x, 16 D^s)$.
nodes.statement_short: $J\subset B(x,16D^s)$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 6
nodes.statement:
Thus, we can estimate \eqref{eq-term-C} by
    $$
        2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}}\frac{\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x,D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\J\subset B(x, 16D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\\ s(J) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}} D^{(s(J) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}))/a} \int_J |f|\,.
    $$
    $$
        = 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}\\ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I}}\frac{\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f|\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound term C and regroup by cubes $I$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 7
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} and \eqref{defineep}, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for tiles ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I$ are pairwise disjoint. It follows from the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ if and only if $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, thus we can estimate the sum over $\mathbf{1}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)$ by $\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness replaces the indicator sum by $\mathbf 1_I(x')$

nodes.name: thirdtree step 8
nodes.statement:
If $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ then in particular $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} $B(c(I),16D^{s(I)}) \subset B(x, 32D^{s(I)})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}
    $$
        \mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling compares ball measures

nodes.name: thirdtree step 9
nodes.statement:
Since $a \ge 4$ we can continue our estimate with
    $$
        \le 2^{128a^3}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}} \frac{\mathbf{1}_{I}(x')}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f|
    $$
    $$
         = 2^{128a^3} S_{1,{\mathfrak u}} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,.
    $$
    This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $S_{1,\mathfrak u}P_{\mathcal J}|f|(x')$

nodes.name: tree projection estimate
nodes.statement_short: The tree operator pairing is bounded by $2^{130a^3}$ times the $L^2$ norms of the projections of $|f|$ onto $\mathcal{J}$ and of $|g|$ onto $\mathcal{L}$ of the tree.
assumptions: for all $f, g$ bounded with bounded support
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$. Then we have for all $f, g$ bounded with bounded support $$ \Bigg|\int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \bar g(y) T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_{2}\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: tree-projection-estimate

nodes.name: tree estimate inequality (eq-tree-est)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_{2}\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_{2}.
nodes.label: eq-tree-est

nodes.name: nontangential operator bound
nodes.statement_short: The nontangential maximal operator $T_{\mathcal{N}}^{\vartheta}$ is bounded on $L^2$ with constant $2^{102a^3}$.
assumptions: For all bounded $f$ with bounded support and all ${\vartheta} \in {\Theta}$
nodes.statement: For all bounded $f$ with bounded support and all ${\vartheta} \in {\Theta}$ $$ \|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\vartheta}} f\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3} \|f\|_2\,. $$
nodes.label: nontangential-operator-bound

nodes.name: boundary operator bound
nodes.statement_short: The auxiliary boundary operator $S_{1,\mathfrak u}$ is bounded on $L^2$ with constant $2^{12a}$.
assumptions: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \|S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f\|_2 \le 2^{12a} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: boundary-operator-bound

nodes.name: Proof of the tree projection estimate
nodes.statement_short: Apply the pointwise tree estimate on each $L\in\mathcal{L}$, integrate, then Cauchy-Schwarz and the $L^2$ bounds for the maximal, nontangential and boundary operators.
nodes.statement: Let $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Let $b(x')$ denote the right-hand side of \Cref{pointwise-tree-estimate}. Apply this lemma to $e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) f$, to obtain for all $y, x' \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le b(x'). $$ Hence, by taking an infimum, we have for $y \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le \inf_{x' \in L} b(x'). $$ Integrating this estimate yields $$ \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L |g(y)| \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ By \eqref{definetp}, we have $T_{{\mathfrak p}} f = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, so $$ \Bigg| \int \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| = \Bigg| \int_{\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. $$ Since $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ partitions $\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, we get from the triangle inequality $$ \le \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ which by the above computation is bounded by $$ \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_X P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ Applying Cauchy-Schwarz, this is bounded by $\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_2 \times \|b\|_2$. By Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, \Cref{nontangential-operator-bound} and \Cref{boundary-operator-bound}, $\|b\|_2$ is at most $$ 2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a})\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 + 2^{103a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]\|_2\,. $$ By the triangle inequality we have for all $x \in X$ that $|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]|(x) \le P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x)$, thus we can further estimate the above by $$ (2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a}) + 2^{103a^3}) \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2\,. $$ This completes the proof since $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: Fix $L$ and apply the pointwise tree estimate: the tree sum is at most
nodes.statement:
Let $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$.
    Let $b(x')$ denote the right-hand side of \Cref{pointwise-tree-estimate}. Apply this lemma to $e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) f$, to obtain for all $y, x' \in L$
    $$
        \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le b(x').
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Fix $L$ and apply the pointwise tree estimate: the tree sum is at most $b(x')$

nodes.name: Take the infimum over $x' \in L$
nodes.statement:
Hence, by taking an infimum, we have for $y \in L$
    $$
        \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le \inf_{x' \in L} b(x').
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Take the infimum over $x' \in L$

nodes.name: Integrate against $|g|$ over $L$ and pass to $P_{\mathcal{L}}|g|$
nodes.statement:
Integrating this estimate yields
    $$
        \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    $$
        \le \int_L |g(y)| \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    $$
        =   \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    $$
        \le \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times  b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate against $|g|$ over $L$ and pass to $P_{\mathcal{L}}|g|$

nodes.name: Restrict the integral to the union of the tile cubes
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{definetp}, we have $T_{{\mathfrak p}} f = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, so
    $$
        \Bigg| \int \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| = \Bigg| \int_{\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the integral to the union of the tile cubes

nodes.name: Split over the partition $\mathcal{L}$, triangle inequality, use the c
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ partitions $\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ by \Cref{dyadic-partitions},
    we get from the triangle inequality
    $$
        \le \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    which by the above computation is bounded by
    $$
        \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times  b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    $$
        = \int_X P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times  b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Split over the partition $\mathcal{L}$, triangle inequality, use the computation above

nodes.name: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Applying Cauchy-Schwarz, this is bounded by $\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_2 \times \|b\|_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz

nodes.name: Bound $\|b\|_2$ by Minkowski and the operator bounds
nodes.statement:
By Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, \Cref{nontangential-operator-bound} and \Cref{boundary-operator-bound}, $\|b\|_2$ is at most
    $$
        2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a})\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 + 2^{103a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]\|_2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|b\|_2$ by Minkowski and the operator bounds

nodes.name: Remove the modulation by the triangle inequality and conclude using $a
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality we have for all $x \in X$ that $|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]|(x) \le P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x)$, thus we can further estimate the above by
    $$
        (2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a}) + 2^{103a^3}) \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2\,.
    $$
    This completes the proof since $a \ge 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Remove the modulation by the triangle inequality and conclude using $a\ge4$

nodes.name: Proof of the nontangential operator bound
nodes.statement_short: Write the truncated sum via the partition of unity $\psi$, split into a sharp truncation term and two boundary annuli; bound the first by $T_Q^\vartheta$ and the others by the finitary maximal function.
nodes.statement: Fix $s_1, s_2$. By \eqref{eq-psisum} we have for all $x \in (0, \infty)$ $$ \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1 - \sum_{s < s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x) - \sum_{s > s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x)\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, the two sums on the right hand side are zero for all $x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2 - 1}]$, hence $$ x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, we further have $$ x \notin [\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}, \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 0\,. $$ Finally, since $\psi \ge 0$ and $\sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1$, we have for all $x$ $$ 0 \le \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) \le 1\,. $$ Let $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and suppose that $D^{s_2 - 1} \le R_Q({\vartheta}, x')$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, it holds that $\rho(x,x') \le 8D^{s_1}$. We have $$ \Bigg|\sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \int K_s(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ $$ = \Bigg|\int \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}\rho(x',y)) K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le \Bigg| \int_{8D^{s_1} < \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le 8D^{s_1}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} The first term \eqref{eq-sharp-trunc-term} is at most $2T_{{Q}}^{\vartheta} f(x)$, using with $R_1 := 8D^{s_1}$, $R_2 := \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ and $R_1 < R_2 < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')$ the triangle inequality in the form \begin{equation} \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) \le R_2} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \left|\int_{R_2 < \rho(x',y) < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|. \end{equation} The other two terms will be estimated by the finitary maximal function from \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}. For the second term \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} we use \eqref{eqkernel-size} which implies that for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}$, we have $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}))}\,. $$ Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32D^{s_1}))}\, . \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_1}) \subset B(c(I_{s_1}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_1}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_1})\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{pf-nontangential-operator-bound-imeq}, we conclude that \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a + 101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ For \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} we argue similarly. We have for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}))}\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 + 100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a + 101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32 D^{s_2}))}\, . \end{equation} Note that by \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have $I_{s_1}(x) \subset I_{s_2}(x)$, in particular $x' \in I_{s_2}(x)$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_2}) \subset B(c(I_{s_2}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_2}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_2})\,. $$ Combining this, \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a+101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ Using $a \ge 4$, taking a supremum over all $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and then a supremum over all $-S \le s_1 < s_2 \le S$, we obtain $$ T_{\mathcal{N}} f(x) \le 2T_{{Q}}^{\vartheta} f(x) + 2^{102a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ The lemma now follows from assumption \eqref{linnontanbound}, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: Proof of the boundary overlap lemma
nodes.statement_short: Volume counting: the small balls around same-scale cube centres are disjoint and each carries a $2^{-9a}$ fraction of a common large ball, by doubling.
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e \emptyset$ and $s(I) = s(J)$. Then $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)})$. Hence by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ 2^{9a}\mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})) \ge \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,, $$ and by the triangle inequality, $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})$ is contained in $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is any finite collection of cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ satisfying $s(J) = s(I)$ and  egin{equation*} B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e\emptyset\ , \end{equation*} then it follows from \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and pairwise disjointedness of cubes of the same scale \eqref{dyadicproperty} that the balls $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J)})$ are pairwise disjoint. Hence  egin{align*} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})) &\ge \sum_{J \in \mathcal{C}} \mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}))\ &\ge |\mathcal{C}| 2^{-9a} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,. \end{align*} Since $\mu$ is doubling and $\mu 
e 0$, we have $\mu(B(c(I), 33D^{s(I)})) > 0$. The lemma follows after dividing by $2^{-9a}\mu(B(c(I), 33D^{s(I)}))$.

nodes.name: Proof of the boundary operator bound
nodes.statement_short: Duality: pair with $g$, swap sums, bound averages by $M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|$, sum the geometric series using the boundary overlap lemma, then Cauchy-Schwarz and Hardy-Littlewood.
nodes.statement: Note that by definition, $S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ is a finite sum of indicator functions of cubes $I \in \mathcal{D}$ for each locally integrable $f$, and hence is bounded, has bounded support and is integrable. Let $g$ be another function with the same three properties. Then $\bar g S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ is integrable, and we have $$ \Bigg|\int \bar g(y) S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg|\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}))} \int_I \bar g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\s(J)\le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| \end{multline*} \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))} \int_{B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})} | g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{multline*} Changing the order of summation and using $J \subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})$ to bound the first average integral by $M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y)$ for any $y \in J$, we obtain \begin{align} \le \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D} \, : \, J\subset B(c(I),16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(I) \ge s(J)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}. \end{align} By \Cref{boundary-overlap}, there are at most $2^{9a}$ cubes $I$ at each scale satisfying the inclusion $J \subset B(c(I),16D^{s(I)})$. Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, $(1 - D^{-1/a})^{-1} \le 2$. Using this estimate for the sum of the geometric series, we conclude that \eqref{eq-boundary-operator-bound-1} is at most $$ 2^{9a+1} \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ The collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $\bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this equals $$ 2^{9a+1} \int_X|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Using Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, we conclude $$ \left|\int \bar g S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| \le 2^{12a} \|g\|_2\|f\|_2\,. $$ The lemma now follows by choosing $g = S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ and dividing on both sides by the finite $\|S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f\|_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of the densities tree bound
nodes.statement_short: Localise $g$ to $\mathcal{E}(\mathfrak u)$ and $f$ to $\mathcal{I}(\mathfrak u)$, apply the tree projection estimate, and bound each projection factor by Cauchy-Schwarz and the local density bounds.
nodes.statement: Denote $$ \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u}) = \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak p})\,. $$ Then we have $$ \left| \int_X \bar g \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{ g\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}f) \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|\,. $$ By \Cref{tree-projection-estimate}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} |\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}g|\|_2\,. \end{equation} We bound the two factors separately. We have $$ \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} |\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}g|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(L)} \left(\int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})} |g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{local-dens1-tree-bound} this is at most $$ \le \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} 2^{101a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})} |g(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is \begin{equation} \le 2^{51 a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation} Similarly, we have \begin{equation} \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} By Cauchy-Schwarz, this is $$ \le \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_J |f(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes in $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is at most \begin{equation} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree}, \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-J-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est}. If $f \le \mathbf{1}_F$ then $f = f\mathbf{1}_F$, so $$ \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2} $$ $$ =\left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_{J \cap F} |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ We estimate as before, using now \Cref{local-dens2-tree-bound} and Cauchy-Schwarz, and obtain that this is $$ \le 2^{101a^3} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|f\|_2\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est-F}.

nodes.name: Proof of the local dens1 tree bound
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the scale of tiles meeting $L$: either $L=\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$ and the set lies in $E_2(9,\mathfrak p)$, or one passes to the parent cube $L'$ and a tile $\mathfrak p'$ on it. Both cases conclude via the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_1$.
nodes.statement:
If the set on the right hand side is empty, then \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} holds. If not, then there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) 
e \emptyset$. Suppose first that there exists such ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le s(L)$. Then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L$, which gives by the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $s(L) = -S$ and hence $L = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Let ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $E({\mathfrak q}) \cap L 
e \emptyset$. Since $s(L) = -S \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})$ it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$. We have then by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}  egin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) &\le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\ &\le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\,. \end{align*} Using that ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and \eqref{forest1}, this is at most $8$. Using again the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we obtain that for each $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$ $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,. $$ Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p})$. We obtain $$ \mu(L \cap G \cap  igcup_{{\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak q})) \le \mu(E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}))\,. $$ By the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_1$, this is bounded by $$ 9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) =9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L)\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$, \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} follows in this case. Now suppose that for each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap E({\mathfrak p}) 
e \emptyset$, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(L)$. Since there exists at least one such ${\mathfrak p}$, there exists in particular at least one cube $L'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L''$ and $s(L'') > s(L)$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there exists $L' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L'$ and $s(L') = s(L) + 1$. By the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset L'$. It now suffices to show that there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = L'$, $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) < 4$ and $9{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim 9{\mathfrak p}'$. For then, let ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap E({\mathfrak q}) 
e \emptyset$. As shown above, this implies ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) \ge s(L')$, so by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $L' \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$. If $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$, then by a similar calculation as above, using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{forest1}, we obtain $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,. $$ Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}')$. We deduce using the definition \eqref{definedens1} of $\operatorname{dens}_1$ $$ \mu(L \cap G \cap  igcup_{{\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak q})) \le \mu(E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}')) \le 9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L')\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, and $a \ge 4$ this is estimated by $$ 9^a 2^{100a^3 + 5a}\operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L) \le 2^{101 a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\mu(L)\,. $$ To show existence of ${\mathfrak p}'$ with the given properties, if ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') = L'$ we can take ${\mathfrak p}' = {\mathfrak p}''$, which satisfies the distance property by \eqref{forest1} and the other properties trivially. Otherwise, let ${\mathfrak p}'$ be the unique tile such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = L'$ and such that $\Omega({\mathfrak u}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}') 
e \emptyset$. Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Since by \eqref{forest1} ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = s(L') \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$, we have by \eqref{dyadicproperty} and \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} that $\Omega({\mathfrak u}) \subset \Omega({\mathfrak p}')$, and hence the distance property. $9{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim 9{\mathfrak p}'$ follows by the triangle inequality, \eqref{forest1}, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: The empty case is trivial; otherwise some tile cube meets $L$
nodes.statement: If the set on the right hand side is empty, then \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} holds. If not, then there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: The empty case is trivial; otherwise some tile cube meets $L$

nodes.name: Case $s(\mathfrak p)\le s(L)$: $L=\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$ and the set
nodes.statement:
Suppose first that there exists such ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le s(L)$. Then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L$, which gives by the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $s(L) = -S$ and hence $L = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Let ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $E({\mathfrak q}) \cap L \ne \emptyset$. Since $s(L) = -S \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})$ it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$. We have then by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}
    \begin{align*}
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) &\le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\\
        &\le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\,.
    \end{align*}
    Using that ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and \eqref{forest1}, this is at most $8$. Using again the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we obtain that for each $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,.
    $$
    Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p})$. We obtain
    $$
        \mu(L \cap G \cap \bigcup_{{\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak q})) \le \mu(E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}))\,.
    $$
    By the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_1$, this is bounded by
    $$
        9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) =9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L)\,.
    $$
    Since $a \ge 4$, \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} follows in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Case $s(\mathfrak p)\le s(L)$: $L=\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$ and the set lies in $E_2(9,\mathfrak p)$

nodes.name: Then $s(L)=-S$ and $L=\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$
nodes.statement: Suppose first that there exists such ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le s(L)$. Then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset L$, which gives by the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $s(L) = -S$ and hence $L = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: Then $s(L)=-S$ and $L=\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$

nodes.name: Any $\mathfrak q$ meeting $L$ has $L\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak q)$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $E({\mathfrak q}) \cap L \ne \emptyset$. Since $s(L) = -S \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q})$ it follows from \eqref{dyadicproperty} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$.
nodes.statement_short: Any $\mathfrak q$ meeting $L$ has $L\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak q)$

nodes.name: Triangle inequality and monotone cube metrics give distance at most 8
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality and monotone cube metrics give distance at most 8

nodes.name: Hence $L\cap G\cap E(\mathfrak q)\subset E_2(9,\mathfrak p)$
nodes.statement:
Using again the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we obtain that for each $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,.
    $$
    Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p})$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $L\cap G\cap E(\mathfrak q)\subset E_2(9,\mathfrak p)$

nodes.name: Bound by $9^a\operatorname{dens}_1\mu(L)$ by the definition of $\opera
nodes.statement:
We obtain
    $$
        \mu(L \cap G \cap \bigcup_{{\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak q})) \le \mu(E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}))\,.
    $$
    By the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_1$, this is bounded by
    $$
        9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) =9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L)\,.
    $$
    Since $a \ge 4$, \eqref{eq-1density-estimate-tree} follows in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Bound by $9^a\operatorname{dens}_1\mu(L)$ by the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_1$

nodes.name: Case all tiles meeting $L$ have larger scale: use the parent cube $L'$
nodes.statement:
Now suppose that for each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap E({\mathfrak p}) \ne \emptyset$, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(L)$.
    Since there exists at least one such ${\mathfrak p}$, there exists in particular at least one cube $L'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L''$ and $s(L'') > s(L)$.
    By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there exists $L' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subset L'$ and $s(L') = s(L) + 1$.
    By the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset L'$.

    It now suffices to show that there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = L'$, $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) < 4$ and $9{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim 9{\mathfrak p}'$.
    For then, let ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with $L \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \ne \emptyset$. As shown above, this implies ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) \ge s(L')$, so by \eqref{dyadicproperty} $L' \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q})$.
    If $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$, then by a similar calculation as above, using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{forest1}, we obtain
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,.
    $$
    Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}')$. We deduce using the definition \eqref{definedens1} of $\operatorname{dens}_1$
    $$
        \mu(L \cap G \cap \bigcup_{{\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak q})) \le \mu(E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}')) \le 9^a \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L')\,.
    $$
    Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, and $a \ge 4$ this is estimated by
    $$
        9^a 2^{100a^3 + 5a}\operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(L) \le 2^{101 a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\mu(L)\,.
    $$
    To show existence of ${\mathfrak p}'$ with the given properties, if ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') = L'$ we can take ${\mathfrak p}' = {\mathfrak p}''$, which satisfies the distance property by \eqref{forest1} and the other properties trivially.
    Otherwise, let ${\mathfrak p}'$ be the unique tile such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = L'$ and such that $\Omega({\mathfrak u}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}') \ne \emptyset$.
    Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$.
    Since by \eqref{forest1} ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = s(L') \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$, we have by \eqref{dyadicproperty} and \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} that $\Omega({\mathfrak u}) \subset \Omega({\mathfrak p}')$, and hence the distance property.
    $9{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim 9{\mathfrak p}'$ follows by the triangle inequality, \eqref{forest1}, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}.
    This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Case all tiles meeting $L$ have larger scale: use the parent cube $L'$
