nodes.name: Proof of the local dens2 tree bound
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finding a tile $\mathfrak p$ and radius $r$ with $J\subset B(c(\mathfrak p),r)$ of comparable measure; handle $s(J)=S$ directly and otherwise use the parent cube $J'$ and a tile near it.
nodes.statement: We prove the inequality with the constant $2^{201a^3}$ replaced by $2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a}$; this is stronger because $a \geq 4$. It suffices to show the existence of a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and an $r \geq 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ such that $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)$ and $\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) \le 2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)$, because then it follows from the definition \eqref{definedens2} of $\operatorname{dens}_2$ that $$ \mu(F \cap J) \le \mu(F \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) $$ $$ \le \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) \le 2^{200a^3 + 14a} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\mu(J)\,. $$ In particular, these criteria are satisfied, with $r = 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$, by any ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ such that $J \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}, 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))$ and $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$, because then by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $$ \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} / 4)) $$ $$ \le 2^{4a} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)\,. $$ Suppose first that $s(J) = S$. Then $J = I_0$, so \eqref{subsetmaxcube} and the fact that $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \subseteq \mathcal{J}_0({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ imply that $s(J) = -S$. Thus $S = 0$. It follows that $J$ is the only dyadic cube, so any ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ has ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = J$, and therefore satisfies $J \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}, 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))$ and $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. It remains to consider the case $s(J) < S$. Then, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists some cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $J \subset J'$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ there exists some ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$. Since $c(J) \in J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')})$, the triangle inequality, $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ imply $$ B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B(c(J), 204D^{s(J') + 1} + 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B(c(J), 2^8 D^{s(J) + 2})\,. $$ From the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $D=2^{100a^2}$ and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we obtain \begin{equation} \mu(B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J') + 1})) \leq 2 ^ {200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,. \end{equation} If $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, then we need only check that $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. This follows immediately from ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$ and \eqref{measure-comparison}. From now on we assume $J \not \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$. Since \begin{equation*} {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}) \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\, , \end{equation*} we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality $$ J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})\,. $$ In particular this implies $104 D^{s(J') + 1} > 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$. By the triangle inequality we also have $$ B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 204 D^{s(J') + 1})\,, $$ so from \eqref{measure-comparison}, $$ \mu( B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,, $$ which proves ${\mathfrak p}$ satisfies the needed criteria with $r=104 D^{s(J') + 1}$.

    \eqref{definedens2} of $\operatorname{dens}_2$ that
    $$

    $$
    $$
        \le \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) \le 2^{200a^3 + 14a} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\mu(J)\,.

    $$

nodes.name: Case $s(J)=S$: $J$ is the only cube and any tile works
nodes.statement:
Suppose first that $s(J) = S$. Then $J = I_0$, so \eqref{subsetmaxcube} and the fact that
    $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \subseteq \mathcal{J}_0({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ imply that $s(J) = -S$. Thus
    $S = 0$. It follows that $J$ is the only dyadic cube, so any ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ has
    ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = J$, and therefore satisfies $J \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}, 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))$ and
    $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $s(J)=S$: $J$ is the only cube and any tile works

nodes.name: Case $s(J)<S$: use the parent cube $J'$
nodes.statement:
It remains to consider the case $s(J) < S$. Then, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and
    \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists some cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and
    $J \subset J'$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ there exists some ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$
    such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$.

    Since $c(J) \in J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')})$, the triangle inequality,
    $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ imply
    $$
        B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B(c(J), 204D^{s(J') + 1} + 4D^{s(J')})
                                 \subset B(c(J), 2^8 D^{s(J) + 2})\,.
    $$
    From the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $D=2^{100a^2}$ and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we
    obtain
    \begin{equation} \mu(B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J') + 1})) \leq 2 ^ {200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,.
    \end{equation}

    If $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, then we need only check that
    $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. This follows immediately from
    ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$ and \eqref{measure-comparison}.

    From now on we assume $J \not \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$. Since
    \begin{equation*}
        {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}) \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\, ,
    \end{equation*}
    we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality
    $$
        J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})\,.
    $$
    In particular this implies $104 D^{s(J') + 1} > 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$. By the triangle inequality
    we also have
    $$
        B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 204 D^{s(J') + 1})\,,
    $$
    so from \eqref{measure-comparison},
    $$
        \mu( B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,,
    $$
    which proves ${\mathfrak p}$ satisfies the needed criteria with $r=104 D^{s(J') + 1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $s(J)<S$: use the parent cube $J'$

    ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$ and \eqref{measure-comparison}.
nodes.statement_short: Subcase $J\subset B(c(\mathfrak p),4D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$

nodes.name: Subcase $J\not\subset B(c(\mathfrak p),4D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$: $J$ lies
nodes.statement:
From now on we assume $J \not \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$. Since
    \begin{equation*}
        {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}) \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\, ,
    \end{equation*}
    we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality
    $$
        J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})\,.
    $$
    In particular this implies $104 D^{s(J') + 1} > 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$.
nodes.statement_short: Subcase $J\not\subset B(c(\mathfrak p),4D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$: $J$ lies in a larger ball around $c(\mathfrak p)$

nodes.name: The larger ball has measure comparable to $\mu(J)$, giving $r=104D^{s(
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality
    we also have
    $$
        B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 204 D^{s(J') + 1})\,,
    $$
    so from \eqref{measure-comparison},
    $$
        \mu( B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,,
    $$
    which proves ${\mathfrak p}$ satisfies the needed criteria with $r=104 D^{s(J') + 1}$.
nodes.statement_short: The larger ball has measure comparable to $\mu(J)$, giving $r=104D^{s(J')+1}$

nodes.name: adjoint tile operator $T_{\mathfrak p}^*$
nodes.statement_short: Formula for the adjoint $T_{\mathfrak p}^*$ of the tile operator $T_{\mathfrak p}$.

nodes.name: adjoint tile operator formula (definetp*)
nodes.statement: T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x)} e(-{Q}(y)(x)+ {Q}(y)(y)) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.

nodes.name: adjoint tile support
nodes.statement_short: $T_{\mathfrak p}^*g$ only sees $g$ on $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$ and is supported in $B(c(\mathfrak p),5D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$; for tree tiles both localise to $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u)$.
assumptions: For each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$
conclusions: T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g\,.
T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\,.
T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g\,.

conclusions: T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\,.

nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, we have $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g\,. $$ For each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\,. $$
nodes.label: adjoint-tile-support

nodes.name: Proof of the adjoint tile support lemma
nodes.statement_short: Insert the indicator of $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$ using $E(\mathfrak p)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$, then use the kernel support to localise $x$.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{forest1}, $E({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. Thus by \eqref{definetp*} $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x) $$ $$ = \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x)} e(-{Q}(y)(x) + {Q}(y)(y)) \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(y) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ If this integral is not $0$, then there exists $y \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ such that $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x) \ne 0$. By \eqref{supp-Ks}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, it follows that \begin{equation*} x \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation*} Thus $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(x) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x)\,. $$ The second claimed equation follows now since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and by \eqref{forest6} we have $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.

nodes.name: Insert $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)}$ into the adjoint
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{forest1}, $E({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. Thus by \eqref{definetp*}
    $$
         T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x)
    $$
    $$
        = \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x)} e(-{Q}(y)(x) + {Q}(y)(y)) \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(y) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Insert $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)}$ into the adjoint

nodes.name: Kernel support forces $x\in B(c(\mathfrak p),5D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$
nodes.statement:
If this integral is not $0$, then there exists $y \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ such that $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x) \ne 0$. By \eqref{supp-Ks}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, it follows that
    \begin{equation*}
        x \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, .
    \end{equation*}
    Thus
    $$
        T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(x) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Kernel support forces $x\in B(c(\mathfrak p),5D^{s(\mathfrak p)})$

nodes.name: The tree case follows from \eqref{forest6}

nodes.statement_short: The tree case follows from \eqref{forest6}

nodes.name: adjoint tree estimate
nodes.statement_short: The adjoint tree operator applied to $g$ supported in $G$ is bounded on $L^2$ with gain $\operatorname{dens}_1^{1/2}$.
conclusions: \left\| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,.
nodes.statement: For all $g$ with $\text{support}(g) \subseteq G$, we have that $$ \left\| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. $$
nodes.label: adjoint-tree-estimate

nodes.name: Proof of the adjoint tree estimate
nodes.statement_short: Duality from the densities tree bound, testing against $f$ equal to the adjoint tree sum.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{densities-tree-bound}, we have for all bounded $f$ and $g$ with $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$ that $$ \left| \int_X \overline{\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{g} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Let $f = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$. Since $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$, $f$ is bounded and has bounded support. In particular $\|f\|_2 < \infty$. Dividing \eqref{eq-adjoint-bound} by $\|f\|_2$ completes the proof.

nodes.name: Dualise the densities tree bound
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{densities-tree-bound}, we have for all bounded $f$ and $g$ with $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$ that
    $$
        \left| \int_X \overline{\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{g} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right|
    $$
    \begin{equation} \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Dualise the densities tree bound

nodes.name: adjoint duality bound (eq-adjoint-bound)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\,.
nodes.label: eq-adjoint-bound

nodes.name: Test with $f$ equal to the adjoint sum and divide by $\|f\|_2$
nodes.statement: Let $f = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$. Since $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$, $f$ is bounded and has bounded support. In particular $\|f\|_2 < \infty$. Dividing \eqref{eq-adjoint-bound} by $\|f\|_2$ completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Test with $f$ equal to the adjoint sum and divide by $\|f\|_2$

nodes.name: auxiliary operator $S_{2,\mathfrak u}$
nodes.statement:
We define
$$
    S_{2,{\mathfrak u}}g := \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g \right| + M_{\mathcal{B},1}g + |g|\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: $S_{2,\mathfrak u}g$ is the modulus of the adjoint tree sum plus the maximal function plus $|g|$.

nodes.name: adjoint tree control
nodes.statement_short: $S_{2,\mathfrak u}$ is bounded on $L^2$ for $g$ supported in $G$, with constant $2^{182a^3}$.
assumptions: for all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and for all $g$ with $\text{support}(g) \subseteq G$
nodes.statement: We have for all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and for all $g$ with $\text{support}(g) \subseteq G$ $$ \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}} g\|_2 \le 2^{182a^3} \|g\|_2\,. $$
nodes.label: adjoint-tree-control

nodes.name: Proof of the adjoint tree control lemma
nodes.statement_short: Minkowski's inequality with Hardy-Littlewood and the adjoint tree estimate.
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} and \Cref{adjoint-tree-estimate}, using that $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: correlation separated trees
nodes.statement_short: Almost orthogonality: the correlation of adjoint operators of two distinct trees decays like $2^{-4n}$, relative to $S_{2}$ norms on the overlap of their top cubes.
assumptions: For any ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support
nodes.statement: For any ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support, we have \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{512a^3-4n} \prod_{j =1}^2 \| S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2))}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: correlation-separated-trees

nodes.name: separated trees correlation (eq-lhs-sep-tree)
nodes.statement: \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right|
nodes.label: eq-lhs-sep-tree

nodes.name: separated trees correlation bound (eq-rhs-sep-tree)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{512a^3-4n} \prod_{j =1}^2 \| S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2))}\,.
nodes.label: eq-rhs-sep-tree

nodes.name: Proof of the correlation separated trees lemma
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to nested top cubes, split tiles by the separated set $\mathfrak S$, and combine the distant- and near-tree-part lemmas with $Z=2^{12a}$.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the left hand side \eqref{eq-lhs-sep-tree} is $0$ unless ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Without loss of generality we assume that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. Define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{S} := \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \ : \ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn/2}\,\}. \end{equation} \Cref{correlation-separated-trees} follows by combining the definition \eqref{defineZ} of $Z$ with the following two lemmas.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_2)$
nodes.statement: By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the left hand side \eqref{eq-lhs-sep-tree} is $0$ unless ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Without loss of generality we assume that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_2)$ without loss of generality

nodes.name: Define the set $\mathfrak S$ of tiles where the two tree frequencies a
nodes.statement_short: Define the set $\mathfrak S$ of tiles where the two tree frequencies are far apart

nodes.name: separated tile set $\mathfrak S$ (def-Tree-S-set)
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{S} := \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \ : \ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn/2}\,\}.
nodes.label: def-Tree-S-set

nodes.name: Combine the two following lemmas
nodes.statement: \Cref{correlation-separated-trees} follows by combining the definition \eqref{defineZ} of $Z$ with the following two lemmas.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two following lemmas

nodes.name: correlation distant tree parts
nodes.statement_short: Correlation bound for the part of the second tree inside $\mathfrak S$, with decay $2^{-Zn/(4a^2+2a^3)}$.
assumptions: for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support
nodes.statement: We have for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{511a^3} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \prod_{j =1}^2 \| S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1))}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: correlation-distant-tree-parts

nodes.name: distant tree parts correlation (eq-lhs-big-sep-tree)
nodes.statement: \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right|
nodes.label: eq-lhs-big-sep-tree

nodes.name: correlation near tree parts
nodes.statement_short: Correlation bound for the part of the second tree outside $\mathfrak S$, with decay $2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa}$.
assumptions: for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support
nodes.statement: We have for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \prod_{j=1}^2 \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1))}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: correlation-near-tree-parts

nodes.name: near tree parts correlation (eq-lhs-small-sep-tree)
nodes.statement: \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right|
nodes.label: eq-lhs-small-sep-tree

nodes.name: near tree parts bound (eq-rhs-small-sep-tree)
nodes.statement: \le 2^{232a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \prod_{j=1}^2 \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1))}\,.
nodes.label: eq-rhs-small-sep-tree

nodes.name: overlap implies distance
nodes.statement_short: Tiles of either tree whose cube meets $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$ lie in $\mathfrak S$; in particular $\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u_1)\subset\mathfrak S$.
assumptions: Let ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$.
${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$
conclusions: In particular, we have ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$, then ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. In particular, we have ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.label: overlap-implies-distance

nodes.name: Proof of the overlap implies distance lemma
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on which tree contains $\mathfrak p$, using the forest separation condition and monotonicity of cube metrics.
nodes.statement: Suppose first that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$, by \eqref{forest1}. Thus we have by the separation condition \eqref{forest5}, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, \eqref{forest1} and the triangle inequality \begin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) &\ge d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) - d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1))\\ &\ge 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4\\ &\ge 2^{Zn/2}\,, \end{align*} using that $Z= 2^{12a}\ge 4$. Hence ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. Suppose now that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then the same argument as above with ${\mathfrak u}_1$ and ${\mathfrak u}_2$ swapped shows ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then, by \eqref{dyadicproperty}, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Pick ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Hence, by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the first paragraph $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn}\,, $$ so ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.

nodes.name: Case $\mathfrak p\in\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u_1)$: separation condition
nodes.statement:
Suppose first that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$, by \eqref{forest1}. Thus we have by the separation condition \eqref{forest5}, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, \eqref{forest1} and the triangle inequality
    \begin{align*}
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) &\ge d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) - d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1))\\
        &\ge 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4\\
        &\ge 2^{Zn/2}\,,
    \end{align*}
    using that $Z= 2^{12a}\ge 4$. Hence ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\mathfrak p\in\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u_1)$: separation condition gives distance $\ge 2^{Zn/2}$

nodes.name: Case $\mathfrak p\in\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u_2)$
nodes.statement:
Suppose now that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then the same argument as above with ${\mathfrak u}_1$ and ${\mathfrak u}_2$ swapped shows ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then, by \eqref{dyadicproperty}, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Pick ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Hence, by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the first paragraph
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn}\,,
    $$
    so ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\mathfrak p\in\mathfrak T(\mathfrak u_2)$

nodes.name: Subcase $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$: sam
nodes.statement: Suppose now that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then the same argument as above with ${\mathfrak u}_1$ and ${\mathfrak u}_2$ swapped shows ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Subcase $\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$: same argument

nodes.name: Subcase $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$: com
nodes.statement:
If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then, by \eqref{dyadicproperty}, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Pick ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Hence, by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the first paragraph
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn}\,,
    $$
    so ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Subcase $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)\subset\mathcal I(\mathfrak p)$: compare with a tile of the first tree via monotone cube metrics

nodes.name: tile-set operators $T_{\mathfrak C}$, $T_{\mathfrak C}^*$
nodes.statement:
To simplify the notation, we will write at various places throughout the proof of Lemmas \ref{correlation-distant-tree-parts} and \ref{correlation-near-tree-parts} for a subset ${\mathfrak C} \subset {\mathfrak P}$
$$
    T_{{\mathfrak C}} f := \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\,, \quad\quad T_{{\mathfrak C}}^* g := \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in{\mathfrak C}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\,.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Notation $T_{\mathfrak C}$ and $T_{\mathfrak C}^*$ for sums of tile operators and their adjoints over a tile set $\mathfrak C$.

nodes.name: cube collection $\mathcal{J}'$
nodes.statement:
Define
    $$
        \mathcal{J}' = \{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \ : \ J \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)\}\,.
    $$

nodes.name: dyadic partition 1
nodes.statement_short: The cubes of $\mathcal J'$ partition $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$.
nodes.statement: We have that $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}} J\,. $$
nodes.label: dyadic-partition-1

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partition 1
nodes.statement_short: By the dyadic partition lemma it suffices to rule out cubes of $\mathcal J(\mathfrak S)$ containing $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$, which contradicts the definition of $\mathcal J(\mathfrak S)$.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ with $J \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$. But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset J$. Pick ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset J$. This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$.

nodes.statement_short: There is a partition of unity $\chi_J$, $J\in\mathcal J'$, of $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$ with $0\le\chi_J\le\mathbf 1_{B(J)}$ and Lipschitz constant $2^{227a^3}D^{-s(J)}$.
conclusions: There exists a family of functions $\chi_J$, $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ such that
nodes.statement: There exists a family of functions $\chi_J$, $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ such that \begin{equation} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \chi_J\,, \end{equation} and for all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $y,y' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ \begin{equation} 0 \leq \chi_J(y) \leq \mathbf{1}_{B(J)}(y)\,, \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le 2^{227a^3} \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\,. \end{equation}

nodes.name: moderate scale change

nodes.name: Proof of the Lipschitz partition unity lemma
nodes.statement_short: Normalise tent functions $\tilde\chi_J$ by their sum $a(y)\ge4$; bound the Lipschitz constant by counting neighbouring cubes via moderate scale change and doubling.
nodes.statement:
For each cube $J \in \mathcal{J}$ let $$ 	ilde\chi_J(y) = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}(y)\max\{0, 8 - D^{-s(J)} ho(y, c(J))\}\,, $$ and set $$ a(y) = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} 	ilde \chi_J(y)\,. $$ We define \[ \chi_J(y) :=  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y)}{a(y)}\,. \] Then, due to \eqref{forest6} and \eqref{def-BJ}, the properties \eqref{eq-pao-1} and \eqref{eq-pao-2} are clearly true. Estimate \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows from \eqref{eq-pao-2} if $y, y' 
otin B(J)$. Thus we can assume that $y \in B(J)$. We have by the triangle inequality $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le  rac{|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')|}{a(y)} +  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|}{a(y)a(y')} $$ Since $	ilde \chi_J(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in B(c(J),4D^{s(J)}) \supset J$ and by \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, we have that $a(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. So we can estimate the above further by $$ \le 2^{-2}(|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|)\,. $$ If $y' 
otin B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$ then the second summand vanishes. Else, we can estimate the above, using also that $|	ilde \chi_J(y')| \le 8$, by $$ \le 2^{-2} |	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}}|	ilde \chi_{J'}(y) - 	ilde \chi_{J'} (y')|\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have for all dyadic cubes $I$ $$ |	ilde \chi_I(y) - 	ilde \chi_I(y')| \le ho(y, y') D^{-s(I)}\,. $$ Using this above, we obtain $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le ho(y,y') \Big(  rac{1}{4} D^{-s(J)} + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}} D^{-s(J')}\Big)\,. $$ By \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, this is at most $$  rac{ho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} \left(  rac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}|ight)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, the balls $B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J')})$ are pairwise disjoint. By the triangle inequality and \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, each such ball for $J'$ in the set of the last display is contained in $$ B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})\,. $$ By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we further have $$ \mu(B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a} \mu\Big(B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J')})\Big) $$ for each such ball. Thus $$ |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}| \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a}\,. $$ Recalling that $D=2^{100a^2}$, we obtain $$ rac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}|\leq 2^{200a^3 + 100a^2 + 7a + 2}.$$ Since $a\ge 4$, \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows.

nodes.statement:
For each cube $J \in \mathcal{J}$ let
        $$
            \tilde\chi_J(y) = \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}(y)\max\{0, 8 - D^{-s(J)} \rho(y, c(J))\}\,,
        $$
        and set
        $$
            a(y) = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \tilde \chi_J(y)\,.
        $$
        We define
        \[
            \chi_J(y) := \frac{\tilde \chi_J(y)}{a(y)}\,.
        \]

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for the quotient
nodes.statement:
We have by the triangle inequality
        $$
            |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le \frac{|\tilde \chi_J(y) - \tilde \chi_J(y')|}{a(y)} + \frac{\tilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|}{a(y)a(y')}
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality for the quotient

nodes.name: Use $a\ge4$ on $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$
nodes.statement:
Since $\tilde \chi_J(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in B(c(J),4D^{s(J)}) \supset J$ and by \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, we have that $a(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. So we can estimate the above further by
        $$
            \le 2^{-2}(|\tilde \chi_J(y) - \tilde \chi_J(y')| + \tilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|)\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Use $a\ge4$ on $\mathcal I(\mathfrak u_1)$

nodes.name: Bound $|a(y)-a(y')|$ by neighbouring tent differences
nodes.statement:
If $y' \notin B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$ then the second summand vanishes. Else, we can estimate the above, using also that $|\tilde \chi_J(y')| \le 8$, by
        $$
            \le 2^{-2} |\tilde \chi_J(y) - \tilde \chi_J(y')| + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\\ B(J') \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset}}|\tilde \chi_{J'}(y) - \tilde \chi_{J'} (y')|\,.
        $$

nodes.name: Each tent function is $D^{-s(I)}$-Lipschitz
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality, we have for all dyadic cubes $I$
        $$
            |\tilde \chi_I(y) - \tilde \chi_I(y')| \le \rho(y, y') D^{-s(I)}\,.
        $$
        Using this above, we obtain
        $$
            |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le \rho(y,y') \Big( \frac{1}{4} D^{-s(J)} + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\\ B(J') \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset}} D^{-s(J')}\Big)\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Each tent function is $D^{-s(I)}$-Lipschitz

nodes.statement:
By \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, this is at most
        $$
             \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} \left( \frac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset\}|\right)\,.
        $$

nodes.name: Neighbouring small balls are disjoint and lie in $B(c(J),9D^{s(J)+1})$
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, the balls $B(c(J'), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(J')})$ are pairwise disjoint. By the triangle inequality and \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, each such ball for $J'$ in the set of the last display is contained in
        $$
            B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Neighbouring small balls are disjoint and lie in $B(c(J),9D^{s(J)+1})$

nodes.name: Doubling bounds the number of neighbours by $2^{200a^3+7a}$
nodes.statement:
By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we further have
        $$
            \mu(B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a} \mu\Big(B(c(J'), \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J')})\Big)
        $$
        for each such ball.
        Thus
        $$
            |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset\}| \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a}\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling bounds the number of neighbours by $2^{200a^3+7a}$

nodes.name: Collect constants to get \eqref{eq-pao-3}
nodes.statement:
Recalling that $D=2^{100a^2}$, we obtain
        $$\frac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset\}|\leq 2^{200a^3 + 100a^2 + 7a + 2}.$$
        Since $a\ge 4$, \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Collect constants to get \eqref{eq-pao-3}

nodes.name: Proof of the moderate scale change lemma
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a scale gap of at least two gives a tile of $\mathfrak S$ inside the large ball around $c(J)$, which the definition of $\mathcal J'$ excludes.
nodes.statement: Suppose that $s(J') < s(J) - 1$. Then $s(J) > -S$. Thus, by the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$ there exists no ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,. \end{equation} Since $s(J') < s(J)$, there exists a cube $J'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J''$ and $s(J'') = s(J') + 1$. By the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2})\,. \end{equation} But by the triangle inequality and \eqref{defineD}, we have $$ B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2}) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,, $$ which contradicts \eqref{eq-tile-incl-1} and \eqref{tile-incl-2}.

nodes.statement_short: Split the difference into a phase and a kernel term, bound each via oscillation control and kernel smoothness, treating separately the cases where y, y' lie inside/outside B(c(p),5D^{s(p)}).
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp*}, we have $$ |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y)) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y')| $$ \begin{multline*} =\bigg| \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} e({Q}(x)(x) - {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y)) \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y)} g(x) \\ - e({Q}(x)(x) - {Q}(x)(y') + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')) \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y')} g(x) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\bigg| \end{multline*} \begin{multline*} \leq\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g(x)| |e({Q}(x)(y) - {Q}(x)(y') - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y'))\overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y)}\\ - \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y')}| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \end{multline*} \begin{multline} \leq\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g(x)| |e(-{Q}(x)(y) + {Q}(x)(y') + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')) - 1| \\ \times |\overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y)}|\, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \end{multline} \begin{equation} + \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g(x)| |\overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y)} - \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x, y')} |\, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. \end{equation} By the oscillation estimate \eqref{osccontrol}, we have $$ |-{Q}(x)(y) + {Q}(x)(y') + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')| $$ \begin{equation} \le d_{B(y, 1.6\rho(y,y'))}({Q}(x), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\,. \end{equation} Suppose that $y, y' \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, so that $\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$. Let $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $2^{ak}\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ but $2^{a(k+1)} \rho(y,y') > 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$. In particular, $k \ge 0$. Then, using \eqref{seconddb} followed by \eqref{firstdb}, we can bound \eqref{eq-lem-tile-Holder-comp} from above by $$ 2^{-k} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 16 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}({Q}(x), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) \le 2^{6a - k} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({Q}(x), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\,. $$ Since $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ we have ${Q}(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 1)$, and since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ we have ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}) \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 4)$, so this is estimated by $$ \le 5 \cdot 2^{6a - k}\,. $$ By definition of $k$, we have $$ -k < 1 - \frac{1}{a} \log_2\left(\frac{10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}{\rho(y,y')}\right)\,, $$ which gives \begin{equation} |-{Q}(x)(y) + {Q}(x)(y') + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')| \le 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a}\,. \end{equation} For all $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, we have by \eqref{doublingx} that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \ge 2^{-3a} \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,. $$ Combining the above with \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-lem-Tile-holder-im1}, we obtain $$ \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{3a}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \times $$ $$ (2^{102a^3} \cdot 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{ D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a} + 2^{127a^3} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a}) $$ Since $\rho(y,y') \le 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$, we conclude $$ \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{128a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Next, if $y,y' \notin B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, then $T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g(y) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g(y') = 0$, by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}. Then \eqref{T*Holder2} holds. Finally, if $y \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$ and $y' \notin B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, then $$ |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y)) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y')| = |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y)| $$ $$ \le \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)| |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ By the same argument used to prove \eqref{eq-Ks-aux}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \psi(D^{-s} \rho(x,y)) |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. \end{equation} It follows from the definition of $\psi$ that $$ \psi(x) \le \max\{0, (2 - 4x)^{1/a}\}\,. $$ Now for all $x\in E({\mathfrak p})$, it follows by the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that \begin{multline*} 2 - 4D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(x,y)\leq 2 - 4D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(y, {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) + 4 D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(x, {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}))\\\leq 18 - 4 D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \rho(y, {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \leq 4 D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(y,y') - 2 . \end{multline*} Combining the above with the previous estimate on $\psi$, we get $$ \psi(D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(x,y)) \le 4 (D^{-{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\rho(y,y'))^{1/a}. $$ Further, we obtain from the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \ge 2^{-3a} \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,. $$ Plugging this into \eqref{eq-lem-Tile-holder-im2} and using $a \ge 4$, we get $$ |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y)| \le \frac{2^{103a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,, $$ which completes the proof of the lemma.

Suppose that $y, y' \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, so that $\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$.
        Let $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $2^{ak}\rho(y,y') \le 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ but $2^{a(k+1)} \rho(y,y') > 10D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$.
        In particular, $k \ge 0$. Then, using \eqref{seconddb} followed by \eqref{firstdb}, we can bound \eqref{eq-lem-tile-Holder-comp} from above by
        $$
            2^{-k} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 16 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}({Q}(x), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) \le 2^{6a - k} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({Q}(x), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))\,.
        $$
        Since $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ we have ${Q}(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 1)$, and since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ we have ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}) \in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 4)$, so this is estimated by
        $$
            \le 5 \cdot 2^{6a - k}\,.
        $$
        By definition of $k$, we have
        $$
            -k < 1 - \frac{1}{a} \log_2\left(\frac{10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}{\rho(y,y')}\right)\,,
        $$
        which gives
      \begin{equation} |-{Q}(x)(y) + {Q}(x)(y') + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y')| \le 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a}\,.
        \end{equation}
        For all $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, we have by \eqref{doublingx} that
        $$
            \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \ge 2^{-3a} \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,.
        $$
        Combining the above with \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-lem-Tile-holder-im1},
        we obtain
        $$
            \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{3a}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \times
        $$
        $$
            (2^{102a^3} \cdot 10 \cdot 2^{6a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{ D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a} + 2^{127a^3} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a})
        $$
        Since $\rho(y,y') \le 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$, we conclude
        $$
            \eqref{T*Holder1b}+\eqref{T*Holder1} \le \frac{2^{128a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}}\right)^{1/a} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.
        $$

        $$
        $$
            \le \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)| |g(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.

        By the same argument used to prove \eqref{eq-Ks-aux}, this is bounded by

        It follows from the definition of $\psi$ that

nodes.name: limited scale impact

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$, $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and suppose that $$ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) \ne \emptyset\,. $$ Then $$ s(J) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le s(J) +3\,. $$

nodes.label: limited-scale-impact

nodes.name: Proof of limited scale impact
nodes.statement_short: Both estimates by contradiction: a too-small scale contradicts disjointness from I(u_1); a too-large scale contradicts the separation defining S via metric doubling.
nodes.statement: For the first estimate, assume that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) < s(J)$, then in particular ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \notin \mathfrak{S}$, we have by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset$. Since $B\Big(c(J), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(J)}\Big) \subset {\mathcal{I}}(J) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, this implies $$ \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}\,. $$ On the other hand $$ \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \le \frac{1}{8} D^{s(J)} + 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\,, $$ by our assumption. Thus $D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \ge 64^{-1} D^{s(J)}$, which contradicts \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$. For the second estimate, assume that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(J) + 3$. Since $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus there exists $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}. By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists some ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})$. On the other hand, since $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) \ne \emptyset$, by the triangle inequality it holds that $$ B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\,. $$ Using the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$, we have $$ 2^{Zn/2} \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,. $$ By \eqref{seconddb}, this is $$ \le 2^{-100a} d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) $$ $$ \le 2^{-100a} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,, $$ and by \eqref{firstdb} and the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$ $$ \le 2^{-94a} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le 2^{-94a} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$ This is a contradiction, the second estimate follows.

nodes.name: lower bound on s(p)
nodes.statement:
For the first estimate, assume that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) < s(J)$, then in particular ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \notin \mathfrak{S}$, we have by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset$.
        Since $B\Big(c(J), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(J)}\Big) \subset {\mathcal{I}}(J) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, this implies
        $$
            \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}\,.
        $$
        On the other hand
        $$
            \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \le \frac{1}{8} D^{s(J)} + 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\,,
        $$
        by our assumption. Thus $D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \ge 64^{-1} D^{s(J)}$, which contradicts \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: assume s(p) < s(J)

nodes.name: distance bounds
nodes.statement:
Since $B\Big(c(J), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(J)}\Big) \subset {\mathcal{I}}(J) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, this implies
        $$
            \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}\,.
        $$
        On the other hand
        $$
            \rho(c(J), {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) \le \frac{1}{8} D^{s(J)} + 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\,,
        $$
        by our assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Get lower and upper bounds on rho(c(J), c(p)).

nodes.name: contradiction with D

nodes.statement:
For the second estimate, assume that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(J) + 3$. Since $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus there exists $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}. By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists some ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})$. On the other hand, since $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) \ne \emptyset$, by the triangle inequality it holds that
        $$
            B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\,.
        $$
        Using the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$, we have
        $$
            2^{Zn/2} \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,.
        $$
        By \eqref{seconddb}, this is
        $$
            \le 2^{-100a} d_{B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J) + 3})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))
        $$
        $$
            \le 2^{-100a} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,,
        $$
        and by \eqref{firstdb} and the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$
        $$
            \le 2^{-94a} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le 2^{-94a} 2^{Zn/2}\,.
        $$
        This is a contradiction, the second estimate follows.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound: assuming s(p) > s(J)+3 contradicts the separation defining S.

On the other hand, since $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) \ne \emptyset$, by the triangle inequality it holds that

        and by \eqref{firstdb} and the definition of $\mathfrak{S}$

            \le 2^{-94a} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le 2^{-94a} 2^{Zn/2}\,.

nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality plus limited scale impact restrict to four scales; kernel size and doubling bound each scale by a ball average of |g|, hence by the maximal function.
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality and since $T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$, we have $$ \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus\mathfrak{S}}^* g| \leq \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g|\,. $$ By \Cref{limited-scale-impact}, this is at most  egin{equation} \sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}, {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}} \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g|\,. \end{equation} If $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ and $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset$, then $$ B(c(J), 16D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset B(x, 32 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\,, $$ by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality. Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, it follows that $$ \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \ge 2^{-5a} \mu(B(c(J), 16D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,. $$ Using \eqref{definetp*}, \eqref{eq-Ks-size} and that $a \ge 4$, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-aux-3} by $$ 2^{103a^3}\sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}, {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s\B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset}}  rac{1}{\mu(B(c(J), 16 D^s)} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}. Further, if $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B^\circ(J) 
e \emptyset$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \ge s(J)$, then $E({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 16 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$. Thus the last display is bounded by $$ 2^{103a^3}\sum_{s = s(J)}^{s(J) + 3}  rac{1}{\mu(B(c(J), 16 D^s))} \int_{B(c(J), 16 D^s)} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ $$ \le \inf_{x' \in J} 2^{103a^3 +2} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g|\,. $$ The lemma follows since $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: triangle inequality

By the triangle inequality and since $T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$, we have
        $$
            \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus\mathfrak{S}}^* g|

Using \eqref{definetp*}, \eqref{eq-Ks-size} and that $a \ge 4$, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-aux-3} by

For each $I \in \mathcal{D}$, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}.

        $$

nodes.name: Proof of global tree control 1
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the sup bound to the Hölder bound; sum the tile Hölder estimates over tiles of scale >= s(J), using disjointness and doubling to bound by the maximal function.
nodes.statement: Note that \eqref{TreeUB} follows from \eqref{TreeHolder}, since for $y'\in B^\circ{}(J)$, by the triangle inequality, $$\left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a}\le \Big(16 + \frac{1}8\Big)^{1/a}\le 2^2.$$ By the triangle inequality, \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \Cref{Holder-correlation-tile}, we have for all $y, y' \in B'(J)$ \begin{equation} |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y')| \end{equation} $$ \le \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_i\\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y')| $$ $$ \le 2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_i\\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} \frac{D^{- {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})/a}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ By \Cref{scales-impacting-interval}, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \ge s(J)$ for all ${\mathfrak p}$ occurring in the sum. Further, for each $s \ge s(J)$, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, and contained in $B(c(J), 32D^{s})$ by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality. Using also the doubling estimate \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain that the expression in the last display can be estimated by $$ 2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{-s/a} \frac{2^{4a}}{\mu(B(c(J), 32D^{s}))} \int_{B(c(J), 32D^{s})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu $$ $$ \le 2^{128a^3+4a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g|\,. $$ Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, we have $$ \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \le 2. $$ Estimate \eqref{TreeHolder}, and therefore the lemma, follow.

nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality, \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \Cref{Holder-correlation-tile}, we have for all $y, y' \in B'(J)$
        \begin{equation} |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y')|
        \end{equation}
        $$
            \le \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_i\\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y')|
        $$
        $$
            \le 2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_i\\ B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B'(J) \neq \emptyset}} \frac{D^{- {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})/a}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum the Hölder estimates of the individual tiles.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: Lipschitz difference of tree operator
nodes.statement: |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_i)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak C}_i}^* g(y')|
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators
nodes.label: eq-C-Lip

nodes.name: scales at least s(J)
nodes.statement: By \Cref{scales-impacting-interval}, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \ge s(J)$ for all ${\mathfrak p}$ occurring in the sum.
nodes.statement_short: Only tiles of scale >= s(J) occur.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: disjointness and doubling
nodes.statement:
Further, for each $s \ge s(J)$, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{defineep} and \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, and contained in $B(c(J), 32D^{s})$ by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality. Using also the doubling estimate \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain that the expression in the last display can be estimated by
        $$
            2^{128a^3}\rho(y,y')^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{-s/a} \frac{2^{4a}}{\mu(B(c(J), 32D^{s}))} \int_{B(c(J), 32D^{s})} |g| \, \mathrm{d}\mu
        $$
        $$
            \le 2^{128a^3+4a} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g|\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness of E(p) and doubling bound the sum by maximal-function terms.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: geometric sum
nodes.statement:
Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, we have
        $$
            \sum_{S \ge s \ge s(J)} D^{(s(J) - s)/a} \le 2.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum the geometric series.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Estimate \eqref{TreeHolder}, and therefore the lemma, follow.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: global tree control 2
nodes.statement_short: Sup over B'(J) of the adjoint of T(u_2)∩S is at most the inf over B°(J) of the adjoint of T(u_2) plus the maximal function.
assumptions: for all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all bounded $g$ with bounded support $$ \sup_{B'(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} g| \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)} g| + 2^{129a^3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|\,. $$
conclusions: $$ \sup_{B'(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} g| \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)} g| + 2^{129a^3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|\,. $$
nodes.statement: We have for all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all bounded $g$ with bounded support $$ \sup_{B'(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} g| \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)} g| + 2^{129a^3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators
nodes.label: global-tree-control-2

nodes.name: Proof of global tree control 2
nodes.statement_short: Apply global tree control 1, the triangle inequality to split T(u_2)∩S = T(u_2) minus the rest, and local tree control.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{global-tree-control-1} $$ \sup_{B'(J)} |T^*_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} g| \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g| + 2^{128a^3+4a+3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g| $$ $$ \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)}^* g| + \sup_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g| + 2^{128a^3+4a+3} \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g|\,, $$ and by \Cref{local-tree-control} $$ \le \inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)}^* g| + (2^{104a^3} + 2^{128a^3+4a+3}) \inf_{J} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1} |g|\,. $$ This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: Proof of Holder correlation tree
nodes.statement_short: Bound h_J pointwise and split its difference into three terms, each bounded by the partition-of-unity properties and global tree control 1 and 2.
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}, and $h_J$ be as defined in \eqref{def-hj}. By \eqref{eq-pao-2} and \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the function $h_J$ is supported in $B'(J) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have for all $y \in B'(J)$: $$ |h_J(y)| \le 2^{257a^3+4a+3} P\,. $$ We have by the triangle inequality \begin{align} &|h_J(y) - h_J(y')|\nonumber\\ &\le |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y)| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y')| |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y')|\,. \end{align} As $h_J$ is supported in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we can assume without loss of generality that $y' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. If $y \notin {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} vanishes. If $y \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then we have by \eqref{eq-pao-3}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2} $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} \le 2^{484a^3+4a+3} \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} P\,, $$ where $P$ denotes the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}. By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-2} \le 2^{257a^3+4a+1} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, and twice \Cref{global-tree-control-1}, we have $$ \eqref{eq-h-Lip-3} \le 2^{256a^3+8a+5} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,. $$ Using that $\rho(y,y') \le 32D^{s(J)}$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: introduce P
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}, and $h_J$ be as defined in \eqref{def-hj}.
nodes.statement_short: Name the product P.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: support of h_J
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq-pao-2} and \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the function $h_J$ is supported in $B'(J) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: h_J is supported in B'(J)∩I(u_1).
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: pointwise bound
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have for all $y \in B'(J)$:
        $$
            |h_J(y)| \le 2^{257a^3+4a+3} P\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bound |h_J| <= C P.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: three-term split
nodes.statement_short: Split the difference into three terms.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: three-term splitting of h_J difference
nodes.statement: &|h_J(y) - h_J(y')|\nonumber\\ &\le |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y)| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y)|\\ & + |\chi_J(y')| |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1(y')| |e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y)) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y) - e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y')) T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2(y')|\,.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators
nodes.label: eq-h-Lip-1

nodes.name: WLOG y' in I(u_1)
nodes.statement: As $h_J$ is supported in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we can assume without loss of generality that $y' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Without loss of generality y' in I(u_1).
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: first term
nodes.statement:
If $y \notin {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} vanishes. If $y \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then we have by \eqref{eq-pao-3}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}
        
        
        
        $$
            \eqref{eq-h-Lip-1} \le 2^{484a^3+4a+3} \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} P\,,
        $$
        where $P$ denotes the product on the right hand side of \eqref{hHolder}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the chi_J difference term.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: second term
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, \Cref{global-tree-control-1} and \Cref{global-tree-control-2}, we have
        
        
        
        $$
            \eqref{eq-h-Lip-2} \le 2^{257a^3+4a+1} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the u_1 Hölder difference term.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: third term
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{eq-pao-2}, and twice \Cref{global-tree-control-1}, we have
        
        
        
        $$
            \eqref{eq-h-Lip-3} \le 2^{256a^3+8a+5} \left(\frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\right)^{1/a} P\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the u_2 Hölder difference term.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Using that $\rho(y,y') \le 32D^{s(J)}$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Collect the three bounds.
nodes.section: 7.5.2 H\"older estimates for adjoint tree operators

nodes.name: lower oscillation bound
nodes.statement_short: On B(J), Q(u_1) and Q(u_2) are separated by at least 2^{-201a^3} 2^{Zn/2}.
assumptions: For all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have that $$ d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{-201a^3} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$
nodes.statement: For all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we have that $$ d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{-201a^3} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$
nodes.label: lower-oscillation-bound

nodes.name: Proof of lower oscillation bound
nodes.statement_short: Find a tile of S near the parent of J, use the separation defining S, and transfer to B(J) by the metric doubling property.
nodes.statement: Since $\emptyset \ne {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$ by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, there exists at least one tile ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathcal{S}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$, so $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}. By definition of $\mathcal{J'}$ and the triangle inequality, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)+2})\,. $$ Thus, by definition of $\mathfrak{S}$: \begin{align*} 2^{Zn/2} \le d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le d_{B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)+2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,. \end{align*} By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, this is $$ \le 2^{200a^3 + 4a} d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,, $$ which gives the lemma using $a \ge 4$.

nodes.name: J strictly inside I(u_1)
nodes.statement: Since $\emptyset \ne {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$ by \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, there exists at least one tile ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathcal{S}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: A tile of S inside I(u_1) shows J is a strict subcube.

nodes.name: parent cube J'
nodes.statement: Thus ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$, so $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}.
nodes.statement_short: Take the parent cube J'.

nodes.name: tile p in S near J
nodes.statement:
By definition of $\mathcal{J'}$ and the triangle inequality, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ such that
    $$
        {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)+2})\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Definition of J' gives a nearby tile p in S.

nodes.name: separation at p
nodes.statement_short: Separation at p.

nodes.name: transfer to B(J)
nodes.statement:
By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, this is
    $$
        \le 2^{200a^3 + 4a} d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,,
    $$
    which gives the lemma using $a \ge 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Doubling transfers the bound to B(J).

nodes.name: Proof of correlation distant tree parts
nodes.statement_short: Localise via the partition of unity to the h_J, apply the Hölder van der Corput lemma on each B(J), and bound using Holder correlation tree and the lower oscillation bound. Finish with Cauchy-Schwarz.
nodes.statement: We have $$ \eqref{eq-lhs-big-sep-tree} = \left| \int_{X} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1 \overline{T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2 }\right|\,. $$ By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the right hand side is supported in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Using \eqref{eq-pao-1} of \Cref{Lipschitz-partition-unity} and the definition \eqref{def-hj} of $h_J$, we thus have $$ \le \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \left|\int_{X} e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y)) h_J(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|\,. $$ Using \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with the ball $B(J)$, we bound this by $$ \le 2^{7a} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \|h_J\|_{C^{\tau}(B'(J))} (1 + d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,. $$ Using \Cref{Holder-correlation-tree}, \Cref{lower-oscillation-bound} and $a \ge 4$, we bound the above by \begin{multline} \le 2^{485a^3+7a+3a^3+3a} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \\ \times \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)\,. \end{multline} By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ \mu(B(J)) \le 2^{6a} \mu(B^\circ{}(J))\,, $$ thus $$ \mu(B(J)) \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j) $$ $$ \le 2^{6a} \int_{B^\circ{}(J)} \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) $$ $$ \le 2^{6a} \int_J \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Summing over $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we obtain $$ \eqref{eq-big-sep-1} \le 2^{499a^3} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \int_X \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \Cref{correlation-distant-tree-parts} follows.

nodes.name: rewrite as integral
nodes.statement:
We have
    $$
