        \eqref{eq-lhs-big-sep-tree} = \left| \int_{X} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)}^* g_1 \overline{T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2 }\right|\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the left side as an integral.

nodes.name: localise with partition of unity
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the right hand side is supported in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Using \eqref{eq-pao-1} of \Cref{Lipschitz-partition-unity} and the definition \eqref{def-hj} of $h_J$, we thus have
    $$
        \le \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \left|\int_{X} e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)(y) - {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)(y)) h_J(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Support and the partition of unity reduce to a sum of oscillatory integrals of h_J.

nodes.name: van der Corput
nodes.statement:
Using \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with the ball $B(J)$, we bound this by
    $$
        \le 2^{7a} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \|h_J\|_{C^{\tau}(B'(J))} (1 + d_{B(J)}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Hölder van der Corput lemma on each B(J).

nodes.name: insert Hölder and separation bounds
nodes.statement:
Using \Cref{Holder-correlation-tree}, \Cref{lower-oscillation-bound} and $a \ge 4$, we bound the above by
    \begin{multline} \le 2^{485a^3+7a+3a^3+3a} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \\
        \times \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)\,.
    \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the Hölder bound for h_J and the lower oscillation bound.

nodes.name: bound after van der Corput
nodes.statement: \le 2^{485a^3+7a+3a^3+3a} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \mu(B(J)) \\ \times \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)\,.
nodes.label: eq-big-sep-1

nodes.name: average over B°(J)
nodes.statement:
By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}
    $$
        \mu(B(J)) \le 2^{6a} \mu(B^\circ{}(J))\,,
    $$
    thus
    $$
        \mu(B(J)) \prod_{j=1}^2 (\inf_{B^\circ{}(J)} |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j| + \inf_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j)
    $$
    $$
        \le 2^{6a} \int_{B^\circ{}(J)} \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)
    $$
    $$
        \le 2^{6a} \int_J \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling replaces products of infima by integrals over J.

nodes.name: sum over J
nodes.statement:
Summing over $J \in \mathcal{J}'$, we obtain
    $$
        \eqref{eq-big-sep-1} \le 2^{499a^3} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \int_X \prod_{j=1}^2 ( |T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_j)}^* g_j|(x) + M_{\mathcal{B},1} g_j(x)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum over J.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, \Cref{correlation-distant-tree-parts} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: cube collection J' (Remaining Tiles)
nodes.statement:
We define
    $$
        \mathcal{J}' = \{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)) \, : \, J \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)\}\,,
    $$
    note that this is different from the $\mathcal{J}'$ defined in the previous subsection.
nodes.statement_short: J' is the set of cubes of J(T(u_1)) contained in I(u_1); it differs from the J' of Sec. 7.5.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: dyadic partition 2
nodes.statement_short: The cubes of J' partition I(u_1).
nodes.statement: We have $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}} J\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: dyadic-partition-2

nodes.name: Proof of dyadic partition 2
nodes.statement_short: By dyadic partitions, it suffices that every cube of J(T(u_1)) meeting I(u_1) lies in J'; otherwise it would strictly contain a tile's cube, contradicting the definition.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$ with $J \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$. But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subsetneq J$. Pick ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subsetneq J$. This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: reduction
nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$ with $J \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via dyadic partitions.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: J strictly contains I(u_1)
nodes.statement: But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subsetneq J$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise J strictly contains I(u_1).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: pick a tile
nodes.statement: Pick ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subsetneq J$.
nodes.statement_short: A tile of T(u_1) then has cube strictly inside J.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: contradiction
nodes.statement: This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with the definition of J(T(u_1)).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: bound for tree projection
nodes.statement_short: The projection onto J' of the adjoint of T(u_2) minus S has small L^2 norm, with exponential decay in Zn kappa.
assumptions: for all bounded $f$ with bounded support $$ \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$
nodes.statement: We have for all bounded $f$ with bounded support $$ \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: bound-for-tree-projection

nodes.name: Proof of correlation near tree parts
nodes.statement_short: Apply the tree projection estimate, Jensen for the g_1 factor, identify the projection via dyadic partition 2, and conclude by the bound for tree projection.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{tree-projection-estimate} and \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, we have \begin{align*} \eqref{eq-lhs-small-sep-tree} \le 2^{130a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))} |\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}g_1| \|_2 \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) )}|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2\,. \end{align*} It follows from the definition of the projection operator $P$ and Jensen's inequality that $$ \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))} |g_1\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}| \|_2 \le \|g_1 \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}\|_2\,. $$ By \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, a cube $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$ intersects ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ if and only if $J \in \mathcal{J}'$. Thus $$ P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) )}|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2| = P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\,. $$ Combining this with \Cref{bound-for-tree-projection}, the definition \eqref{definekappa} and $a \ge 4$ proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: tree projection estimate
nodes.statement_short: Apply the tree projection estimate.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: Jensen
nodes.statement:
It follows from the definition of the projection operator $P$ and Jensen's inequality that
        $$
            \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))} |g_1\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}| \|_2 \le \|g_1 \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}\|_2\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Jensen bounds the g_1 factor.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: identify projection
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, a cube $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1))$ intersects ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ if and only if $J \in \mathcal{J}'$. Thus
        $$
            P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) )}|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2| = P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: The projection reduces to P_{J'}.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Combining this with \Cref{bound-for-tree-projection}, the definition \eqref{definekappa} and $a \ge 4$ proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude with the bound for tree projection.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: thin scale impact
nodes.statement_short: Tiles of T(u_2) outside S whose ball meets B(J) have scale far below s(J), by about Zn/(202a^3).
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$ and $J \in \mathcal{J'}$ with $B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \cap B(J) \ne \emptyset$, then $$ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le s(J) + 2 - \frac{Zn}{202a^3}\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: thin-scale-impact

nodes.name: Proof of thin scale impact
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a tile p' of T(u_1) near the parent of J is far from u_2 by forest5, but comparing metrics via doubling bounds the separation by that at p, which is small since p is not in S.
nodes.statement: Suppose that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(J) + 2 -\frac{Zn}{202a^3} =: s(J) - s_1$. Then, we have $s_1 + 2 \ge 0$ so $$ \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), c(J)) \le 8D^{s(J)}+8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \le 16 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1 + 2}\,. $$ There exists a tile ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. By \eqref{forest1}, it satisfies ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q}) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$. It follows that $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. By \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ with $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, the definition \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, we have $$ B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 128 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1 + 2})\,. $$ Since ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$, we have by \eqref{forest5} $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. $$ Hence, by \eqref{forest1}, the triangle inequality and using that by \eqref{defineZ} $Z(n+1) = 2^{12a}(n+1) \ge 3$ $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4 \ge 2^{Z(n+1) - 1}\,. $$ It follows that $$ 2^{Z(n+1)-1} \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 128 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1+ 2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,. $$ Using \eqref{firstdb}, we obtain $$ \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,. $$ Since ${\mathfrak p}' \notin \mathfrak{S}$ this is bounded by $$ \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} 2^{Zn/2}\,. $$ Thus $$ Z n/2 + Z - 1 \le 9a + 100a^3(s_1 + 3)\,, $$ contradicting the definition of $s_1$.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: assume large scale
nodes.statement:
Suppose that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) > s(J) + 2 -\frac{Zn}{202a^3} =: s(J) - s_1$. Then, we have $s_1 + 2 \ge 0$ so
        $$
            \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), c(J)) \le 8D^{s(J)}+8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \le 16 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1 + 2}\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume the contrary; define s_1 and bound the distance of centres.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: J strictly inside I(u_1)
nodes.statement: There exists a tile ${\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. By \eqref{forest1}, it satisfies ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak q}) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \notin \mathcal{J}'$. It follows that $J \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: J is a strict subcube of I(u_1).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: parent cube J'
nodes.statement: By \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists a cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J'$ and $s(J') = s(J) + 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the parent cube J'.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: tile p' near J'
nodes.statement:
By definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ with
        $$
            {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Definition of J' gives p' near J'.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: ball inclusion
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality, the definition \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, we have
        $$
            B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 128 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1 + 2})\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Ball inclusion around c(p).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: forest separation
nodes.statement:
Since ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$, we have by \eqref{forest5}
        $$
            d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: forest5 separates Q(p') and Q(u_2).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: separation of u_1 and u_2 at p'
nodes.statement:
Hence, by \eqref{forest1}, the triangle inequality and using that by \eqref{defineZ} $Z(n+1) = 2^{12a}(n+1) \ge 3$
        $$
            d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) > 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4 \ge 2^{Z(n+1) - 1}\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Separation of Q(u_1), Q(u_2) at p'.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: compare metrics
nodes.statement:
It follows that
        $$
            2^{Z(n+1)-1} \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \le d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 128 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) + s_1+ 2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of the ball metrics.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: doubling
nodes.statement:
Using \eqref{firstdb}, we obtain
        $$
            \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2))\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling bound.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: not in S
nodes.statement:
Since ${\mathfrak p}' \notin \mathfrak{S}$ this is bounded by
        $$
            \le 2^{9a + 100a^3 (s_1+3)} 2^{Zn/2}\,.
        $$
nodes.statement_short: Small separation since outside S.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: contradiction
nodes.statement:
Thus
        $$
            Z n/2 + Z - 1 \le 9a + 100a^3(s_1 + 3)\,,
        $$
        contradicting the definition of $s_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with the definition of s_1.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: square function count
nodes.statement_short: The average over J of the squared count of nearby smaller cubes outside I(u_1) decays like (8D^{-s})^kappa.
assumptions: For each $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $s$, we have $$ \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\bigg)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le 2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa\,. $$
nodes.statement: For each $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $s$, we have $$ \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\bigg)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le 2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa\,. $$
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: square-function-count

nodes.name: Proof of square function count
nodes.statement_short: The relevant balls lie in a thin boundary layer of J and have bounded overlap; combine with the small boundary property.
nodes.statement: Since $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ we have $J \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Thus, if $B(I) \cap J \ne \emptyset$ then \begin{equation} B(I) \cap J \subset \{x \in J \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus J) \le 8D^{s(I)}\}\,. \end{equation} Furthermore, for each $s$ the balls $B(I)$ with $s(I) = s$ have bounded overlap: Consider the collection $\mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ of all $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in B(I)$ and $s(I) = s$. By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the balls $B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})$, $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ are disjoint, and by the triangle inequality, they are contained in $B(x, 9 D^{s})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we have $$ \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \le 2^{7a} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) $$ for each $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$. Thus $$ \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \ge \sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) \ge 2^{-7a} |\mathcal{D}_{s,x}| \mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))\,. $$ Dividing by the positive $\mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))$, we obtain that for each $x$ \begin{equation} \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq-sep-small-incl}, \eqref{eq-sep-small-bound} and the small boundary property \eqref{eq-small-boundary}, noting that $8D^{s(I)}=8D^{-s}D^{s(J)}$, the lemma follows.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: boundary layer
nodes.statement_short: The balls meet J only near its boundary.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: boundary layer inclusion
nodes.statement: B(I) \cap J \subset \{x \in J \ : \ \rho(x, X \setminus J) \le 8D^{s(I)}\}\,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-small-incl

nodes.name: bounded overlap
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, for each $s$ the balls $B(I)$ with $s(I) = s$ have bounded overlap: Consider the collection $\mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ of all $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in B(I)$ and $s(I) = s$. By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the balls $B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})$, $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ are disjoint, and by the triangle inequality, they are contained in $B(x, 9 D^{s})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we have
    $$
        \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \le 2^{7a} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)}))
    $$
    for each $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$.
    Thus
    $$
        \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \ge \sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) \ge 2^{-7a} |\mathcal{D}_{s,x}| \mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))\,.
    $$
    Dividing by the positive $\mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))$, we obtain that for each $x$
    \begin{equation} \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\
        J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Balls B(I) at a fixed scale have bounded overlap.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: claim bounded overlap
nodes.statement: Furthermore, for each $s$ the balls $B(I)$ with $s(I) = s$ have bounded overlap:
nodes.statement_short: Claim: bounded overlap.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: collection D_{s,x} and disjoint small balls
nodes.statement: Consider the collection $\mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ of all $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in B(I)$ and $s(I) = s$. By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the balls $B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})$, $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$ are disjoint, and by the triangle inequality, they are contained in $B(x, 9 D^{s})$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce D_{s,x}; the small balls are disjoint and contained in B(x,9D^s).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: doubling
nodes.statement:
By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we have
    $$
        \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \le 2^{7a} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)}))
    $$
    for each $I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}$.
nodes.statement_short: Doubling compares volumes.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: count
nodes.statement:
Thus
    $$
        \mu(B(x, 9D^{s})) \ge \sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}_{s,x}} \mu(B(c(I), \frac{1}{4} D^{s(I)})) \ge 2^{-7a} |\mathcal{D}_{s,x}| \mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum volumes to bound |D_{s,x}|.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: overlap bound
nodes.statement:
Dividing by the positive $\mu(B(x, 9D^{s}))$, we obtain that for each $x$
    \begin{equation} \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\
        J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Overlap bounded by 2^{14a}.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: bounded overlap count
nodes.statement: \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(x) \bigg)^2 \le |\mathcal{D}_{s(J) - s,x}|^2 \le 2^{14a} \,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-small-bound

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq-sep-small-incl}, \eqref{eq-sep-small-bound} and the small boundary property \eqref{eq-small-boundary}, noting that $8D^{s(I)}=8D^{-s}D^{s(J)}$, the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the small boundary property.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of bound for tree projection
nodes.statement_short: Split by relative scale (thin scale impact), apply Minkowski, bound each T_p^* by maximal-function averages, then Cauchy-Schwarz and square function count; sum the geometric series in s.
nodes.statement:
Expanding the definition of $P_{\mathcal{J}'}$, we have $$ \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y) ight| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2 ight)^{1/2}\,. $$ By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the innermost sum in the last display is $0$ if $J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) = \emptyset$. Then we split that sum according to the scale of ${\mathfrak p}$ relative to the scale of $J$. By \Cref{thin-scale-impact}, $s_1 \le s(J) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le 2S$ with $s_1 := \lfloor rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2floor$: $$ = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s(J) - s\ J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) 
e \emptyset}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y) ight| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2 ight)^{1/2}\,. $$ Then we apply the triangle inequality and Minkowski's inequality to get  egin{equation} \le \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s(J) - s\ J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) ight)^2ight)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} We have by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{eq-Ks-size} $$ |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3} \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(y) \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, it follows that $$ \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,. $$ Thus, using also $a \ge 4$ $$ |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(y)  rac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,. $$ Since for each $I \in \mathcal{D}$ the sets $E({\mathfrak p}), {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ are disjoint, it follows that $$ \int_J \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I\ J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) 
e \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}  rac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|(y) \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ By \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$. Thus we can estimate \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-1} by $$ 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\ J \cap B(I) 
e \emptyset}} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2| \mathbf{1}_{B(I)} \, \mathrm{d}\mu ight)^2ight)^{1/2}\,, $$ which is by Cauchy-Schwarz at most  egin{equation} 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J ( M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu 	imes  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \left(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\ J \cap B(I) 
e \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}ight)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu ight)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} Using \Cref{square-function-count}, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-2} by $$ 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left(2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J (M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2ight)^{1/2}\,, $$ and since dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{J}'$ form a partition of ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ by \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, $\kappa \le 1$ by \eqref{definekappa}, and $a \ge 4$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} D^{-s\kappa/2} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} D^{-s_1 \kappa /2}  rac{1}{1 - D^{-\kappa/2}} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,. $$ By convexity of $t \mapsto D^{-t}$ and since $D \ge 2$, we have for all $0 \le t \le 1$ $$ D^{-t} \le 1 - t(1 - 1/D) \le 1 -  rac{1}{2}t\,. $$ Using this for $t = \kappa/2$ and using that $s_1 =  rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2$ and the definitions \eqref{defineD} and \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $D$ $$ \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} 2^{-100a^2( rac{Zn}{202a^3} - 3)  rac{\kappa}{2}}  rac{2}{\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2 $$ $$ = 2^{102a^3+21a+4} 2^{150a^2\kappa} 2^{- rac{100}{404a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,. $$ Using the definition \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: expand projection
nodes.statement:
Expanding the definition of $P_{\mathcal{J}'}$, we have
    $$
        \|P_{\mathcal{J}'}|T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}}^* g_2|\|_2
    $$
    $$
        = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y) \right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Expand the projection norm.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: support
nodes.statement: By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}, the innermost sum in the last display is $0$ if $J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Only tiles whose ball meets J contribute.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: split by scale
nodes.statement:
Then we split that sum according to the scale of ${\mathfrak p}$ relative to the scale of $J$.
    By \Cref{thin-scale-impact}, $s_1 \le s(J) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le 2S$ with $s_1 := \lfloor\frac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2\rfloor$:
    $$
        = \left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \left| \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\\ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s(J) - s\\
        J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \ne \emptyset}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y) \right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Thin scale impact restricts relative scales to [s_1, 2S].
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: Minkowski
nodes.statement:
Then we apply the triangle inequality and Minkowski's inequality to get
    \begin{equation} \le \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\\ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s(J) - s\\
        J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \ne \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^2\right)^{1/2}\,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle and Minkowski inequalities.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: Minkowski split by scale
nodes.statement: \le \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\\ {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s(J) - s\\ J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \ne \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^2\right)^{1/2}\,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-tree-small-1

nodes.name: pointwise bound on T_p^*
nodes.statement:
We have by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{eq-Ks-size}
    $$
        |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3} \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(y) \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \frac{1}{\mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bound for T_p^* g_2.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: doubling
nodes.statement:
Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, it follows that
    $$
        \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B(x, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Doubling.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: normalised bound
nodes.statement:
Thus, using also $a \ge 4$
    $$
        |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \mathbf{1}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(y) \frac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound by a ball average.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: maximal function bound
nodes.statement:
Since for each $I \in \mathcal{D}$ the sets $E({\mathfrak p}), {\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ are disjoint, it follows that
    $$
        \int_J \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}\\ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I\\
        J \cap B({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \ne \emptyset}} |T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g_2(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu
    $$
    $$
        \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J \mathbf{1}_{B(I)} \frac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} |g_2(x)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)
    $$
    $$
        \le 2^{102a^3+4a} \int_J M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|(y) \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness gives a bound by M g_2 on B(I).
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{overlap-implies-distance}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}$.
    Thus we can estimate \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-1} by
    $$
        2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\
        J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2| \mathbf{1}_{B(I)} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^2\right)^{1/2}\,,
    $$
    which is by Cauchy-Schwarz at most
    \begin{equation} 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J ( M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \times
        \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \left(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\
        J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\right)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2}\,.
    \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cubes are disjoint from I(u_1); apply Cauchy-Schwarz.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: after Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: 2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J ( M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \times \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J \left(\sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D}, s(I) = s(J) - s\\ I \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \emptyset\\ J \cap B(I) \ne \emptyset}} \mathbf{1}_{B(I)}\right)^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right)^{1/2}\,.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma
nodes.label: eq-sep-tree-small-2

nodes.name: square function count
nodes.statement:
Using \Cref{square-function-count}, we bound \eqref{eq-sep-tree-small-2} by
    $$
        2^{102a^3+4a} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} \left(2^{14a+1} (8 D^{-s})^\kappa \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \int_J (M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|)^2\right)^{1/2}\,,
    $$
    and since dyadic cubes in $\mathcal{J}'$ form a partition of ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ by \Cref{dyadic-partition-2}, $\kappa \le 1$ by \eqref{definekappa}, and $a \ge 4$
    $$
        \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} \sum_{s=s_1}^{2S} D^{-s\kappa/2} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2
    $$
    $$
        \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} D^{-s_1 \kappa /2} \frac{1}{1 - D^{-\kappa/2}} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply square function count and partition.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: convexity bound
nodes.statement:
By convexity of $t \mapsto D^{-t}$ and since $D \ge 2$, we have for all $0 \le t \le 1$
    $$
        D^{-t} \le 1 - t(1 - 1/D) \le 1 - \frac{1}{2}t\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Convexity bound for D^{-t}.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: insert constants
nodes.statement:
Using this for $t = \kappa/2$ and using that $s_1 = \frac{Zn}{202a^3} - 2$ and the definitions \eqref{defineD} and \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $D$
    $$
        \le 2^{102a^3+11a+2} 2^{-100a^2(\frac{Zn}{202a^3} - 3) \frac{\kappa}{2}} \frac{2}{\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2
    $$
    $$
        = 2^{102a^3+21a+4} 2^{150a^2\kappa} 2^{-\frac{100}{404a}Zn\kappa} \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} M_{\mathcal{B},1} |g_2|\|_2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Insert s_1, D, kappa.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Using the definition \eqref{definekappa} of $\kappa$ and $a \ge 4$, the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude.
nodes.section: 7.6 Proof of The Remaining Tiles Lemma

nodes.name: n-row
nodes.statement: Define an $n$-row to be an $n$-forest $({\mathfrak U}, {\mathfrak T})$, i.e. satisfying conditions \eqref{forest1} - \eqref{forest6}, such that in addition the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}), {\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ are pairwise disjoint.
differentia: the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}), {\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ are pairwise disjoint

nodes.name: forest row decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Every n-forest decomposes into 2^n n-rows.
assumptions: Let $({\mathfrak U}, {\mathfrak T})$ be an $n$-forest. Then there exists a decomposition $$ {\mathfrak U} = \dot{\bigcup_{1 \le j \le 2^n}} {\mathfrak U}_j $$ such that for all $j = 1, \dotsc, 2^n$ the pair $({\mathfrak U}_j, {\mathfrak T}|_{{\mathfrak U}_j})$ is an $n$-row.
conclusions: there exists a decomposition $$ {\mathfrak U} = \dot{\bigcup_{1 \le j \le 2^n}} {\mathfrak U}_j $$ such that for all $j = 1, \dotsc, 2^n$ the pair $({\mathfrak U}_j, {\mathfrak T}|_{{\mathfrak U}_j})$ is an $n$-row.
nodes.statement: Let $({\mathfrak U}, {\mathfrak T})$ be an $n$-forest. Then there exists a decomposition $$ {\mathfrak U} = \dot{\bigcup_{1 \le j \le 2^n}} {\mathfrak U}_j $$ such that for all $j = 1, \dotsc, 2^n$ the pair $({\mathfrak U}_j, {\mathfrak T}|_{{\mathfrak U}_j})$ is an $n$-row.
nodes.label: forest-row-decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of forest row decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Greedily pick maximal disjoint families of top cubes; by induction on j each point lies in at most 2^n - j remaining cubes, so 2^n rounds suffice.
nodes.statement: Define recursively ${\mathfrak U}_j$ to be a maximal disjoint set of tiles ${\mathfrak u}$ in $$ {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' < j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'} $$ with inclusion maximal ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. Properties \eqref{forest1}, -\eqref{forest6} for $({\mathfrak U}_j, {\mathfrak T}|_{{\mathfrak U}_k})$ follow immediately from the corresponding properties for $({\mathfrak U}, {\mathfrak T})$, and the cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}), {\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ are disjoint by definition. The collections ${\mathfrak U}_j$ are also disjoint by definition. Now we show by induction on $j$ that each point is contained in at most $2^n - j$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$. This implies that $\bigcup_{j = 1}^{2^n} {\mathfrak U}_j = {\mathfrak U}$, which completes the proof of the Lemma. For $j = 0$ each point is contained in at most $2^n$ cubes by \eqref{forest3}. For larger $j$, if $x$ is contained in any cube ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' < j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$, then it is contained in a maximal such cube. Thus it is contained in a cube in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$. Thus the number ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ is zero, or is less than the number of ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j-1} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ by at least one.

nodes.name: greedy construction
nodes.statement:
Define recursively ${\mathfrak U}_j$ to be a maximal disjoint set of tiles ${\mathfrak u}$ in
    $$
        {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' < j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}
    $$
    with inclusion maximal ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.
nodes.statement_short: Define U_j recursively as maximal disjoint families.

nodes.name: rows are n-rows
nodes.statement: Properties \eqref{forest1}, -\eqref{forest6} for $({\mathfrak U}_j, {\mathfrak T}|_{{\mathfrak U}_k})$ follow immediately from the corresponding properties for $({\mathfrak U}, {\mathfrak T})$, and the cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}), {\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ are disjoint by definition. The collections ${\mathfrak U}_j$ are also disjoint by definition.
nodes.statement_short: Each (U_j, T|U_j) is an n-row and the U_j are disjoint.

nodes.name: induction on j
nodes.statement: Now we show by induction on $j$ that each point is contained in at most $2^n - j$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$. This implies that $\bigcup_{j = 1}^{2^n} {\mathfrak U}_j = {\mathfrak U}$, which completes the proof of the Lemma. For $j = 0$ each point is contained in at most $2^n$ cubes by \eqref{forest3}. For larger $j$, if $x$ is contained in any cube ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' < j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$, then it is contained in a maximal such cube. Thus it is contained in a cube in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$. Thus the number ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ is zero, or is less than the number of ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j-1} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ by at least one.
nodes.statement_short: Induction: after j rounds each point lies in at most 2^n - j remaining cubes.

nodes.name: covering follows
nodes.statement: This implies that $\bigcup_{j = 1}^{2^n} {\mathfrak U}_j = {\mathfrak U}$, which completes the proof of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Hence the U_j exhaust U.

nodes.name: base case
nodes.statement: For $j = 0$ each point is contained in at most $2^n$ cubes by \eqref{forest3}.
nodes.statement_short: Base case by forest3.

nodes.name: inductive step
nodes.statement: For larger $j$, if $x$ is contained in any cube ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' < j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$, then it is contained in a maximal such cube. Thus it is contained in a cube in ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$. Thus the number ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ is zero, or is less than the number of ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U} \setminus \bigcup_{j' \le j-1} {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ by at least one.
nodes.statement_short: Each round removes a maximal cube containing x.

nodes.name: rows (U_j, T_j)
tree and row operators T_C, T_{R_j}
nodes.statement:
To save some space in the proofs of the remaining lemmas in this section we will write
    $$
        T_{{\mathfrak C}} = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}} T_{{\mathfrak p}},\qquad T_{{\mathfrak C}}^* = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*,
    $$
    $$
        T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})},\qquad T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} T_{{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})}^*.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: T_C and T_C^* sum the tile operators over a collection C; T_{R_j} sums the tree operators over the j-th row.

nodes.name: row bound
nodes.statement_short: The adjoint row operator has L^2 norm at most 2^{182a^3}2^{-n/2}, improved by the square root of the density when restricted to F.
assumptions: For each $1 \le j \le 2^n$ and each bounded $g$ with bounded support with $\text{support}(g) \subseteq G$, we have \begin{equation} \left\| T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g \right\|_2 \le 2^{182a^3} 2^{-n/2} \|g\|_2 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left\| \mathbf{1}_F T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g \right\|_2 \le 2^{283a^3} 2^{-n/2} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement: For each $1 \le j \le 2^n$ and each bounded $g$ with bounded support with $\text{support}(g) \subseteq G$, we have \begin{equation} \left\| T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g \right\|_2 \le 2^{182a^3} 2^{-n/2} \|g\|_2 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left\| \mathbf{1}_F T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g \right\|_2 \le 2^{283a^3} 2^{-n/2} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.label: row-bound

nodes.name: row bound with density
nodes.statement: \left\| \mathbf{1}_F T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g \right\|_2 \le 2^{283a^3} 2^{-n/2} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,.
nodes.label: eq-row-bound-2

nodes.name: Proof of row bound
nodes.statement_short: Use the densities tree bound for each tree and the disjointness of the top cubes in a row to sum the tree estimates orthogonally.
nodes.statement: By \Cref{densities-tree-bound} and the density assumption \eqref{forest4}, we have for each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded $f$ of bounded support that \begin{equation} \left\|\mathbf{1}_G\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \right\|_{2} \le 2^{181a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \|f\|_2\, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \left\|\mathbf{1}_G \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} \mathbf{1}_F f \right\|_{2} \le 2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a + 1-n)/2} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Since for each $j$ the top cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ are disjoint, we further have for all bounded $g$ of bounded support and $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$ by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} $$ \left\|\mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right\|_2^2 $$ $$ = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \int_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \left| \mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \mathbf{1}_F T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_G \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right\|_2^2\,. $$ Applying the estimate for the adjoint operator following from equation \eqref{eq-explicit-tree-bound-2}, we obtain $$ \le 2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \max_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \left\| \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right\|_2^2\,. $$ Again by disjointedness of the cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, this is estimated by $$ 2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \max_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2^2\,. $$ Thus, \eqref{eq-row-bound-2} follows, since $a \ge 4$. The proof of \eqref{eq-row-bound-1} from \eqref{eq-explicit-tree-bound-1} is the same up to replacing $F$ by $X$.

nodes.name: tree bounds
nodes.statement_short: Densities tree bound for each tree.

nodes.name: explicit tree bound
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathbf{1}_G\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \right\|_{2} \le 2^{181a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \|f\|_2\,
nodes.label: eq-explicit-tree-bound-1

nodes.name: explicit tree bound with density
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathbf{1}_G \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} \mathbf{1}_F f \right\|_{2} \le 2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a + 1-n)/2} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|f\|_2\,.
nodes.label: eq-explicit-tree-bound-2

nodes.name: disjoint top cubes
nodes.statement:
Since for each $j$ the top cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ are disjoint, we further have for all bounded $g$ of bounded support and $|g| \le \mathbf{1}_G$ by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support}
    $$
        \left\|\mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right\|_2^2
    $$
    $$
        = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \int_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \left| \mathbf{1}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu
        \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \mathbf{1}_F T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_G \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}  g\right\|_2^2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness of top cubes splits the row into trees.

nodes.name: apply tree bound
nodes.statement:
Applying the estimate for the adjoint operator following from equation \eqref{eq-explicit-tree-bound-2}, we obtain
    $$
        \le 2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \max_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \left\| \mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\right\|_2^2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the adjoint tree estimate.

nodes.name: sum over row
nodes.statement:
Again by disjointedness of the cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, this is estimated by
    $$
        2^{282a^3} 2^{(4a+1-n)/2} \max_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2^2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum using disjointness.

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement:
Thus, \eqref{eq-row-bound-2} follows, since $a \ge 4$.
    The proof of \eqref{eq-row-bound-1} from \eqref{eq-explicit-tree-bound-1} is the same up to replacing $F$ by $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Both estimates follow.

nodes.name: row bound for bounded functions supported on G
nodes.statement:
Because all involved operators are linear, the inequality
\eqref{eq-row-bound-2} is also true for uniformly bounded functions $g$
supported on $G$.
nodes.statement_short: By linearity, the row bound with density holds for uniformly bounded g supported on G.
conclusions:
the inequality
\eqref{eq-row-bound-2} is also true for uniformly bounded functions $g$
supported on $G$

nodes.name: row correlation
nodes.statement_short: Adjoint operators of distinct rows are almost orthogonal, with correlation at most 2^{876a^3-4n}.
assumptions: For all $1 \le j,j' \le 2^n$ with $j\ne j'$ and for all $g_1, g_2$ with $\text{support}(g_i) \subseteq G$, it holds that $$ \left| \int T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g_1 \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^*g_2} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| \le 2^{876a^3-4n}\|g_1\|_2 \|g_2\|_2\,. $$
nodes.statement: For all $1 \le j,j' \le 2^n$ with $j\ne j'$ and for all $g_1, g_2$ with $\text{support}(g_i) \subseteq G$, it holds that $$ \left| \int T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g_1 \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^*g_2} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| \le 2^{876a^3-4n}\|g_1\|_2 \|g_2\|_2\,. $$
nodes.label: row-correlation

nodes.name: Proof of row correlation
nodes.statement_short: Expand over pairs of trees, apply the separated-trees correlation bound, then Cauchy-Schwarz and disjointness with the adjoint tree control.
nodes.statement: We have by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and the triangle inequality that $$ \left| \int T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g_1 \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^*g_2} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| $$ $$ \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \left| \int T^*_{{\mathfrak T}_j({\mathfrak u})} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g_1) \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak T}_{j'}({\mathfrak u}')} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')} g_2)} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|\,. $$ By \Cref{correlation-separated-trees}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} 2^{512a^3-4n} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}'} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')}g_2)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}))}\,. \end{equation} We apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the form \begin{equation*} \sum_{i \in M} a_i b_i \le (\sum_{i \in M} a_i^2 )^{1/2}(\sum_{i \in M} b_i^2 )^{1/2} \end{equation*} to the outer two sums: $$ \le 2^{512a^3-4n} \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}))}^2 \right)^{1/2} $$ $$ \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}'} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')}g_2)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}))}^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ We can now estimate the factor involving $g_1$ as follows: \begin{multline*} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}))}^2 \\ = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \int_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')} |S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y)g_1(y))|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \end{multline*} By pairwise disjointedness of the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ for ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$, we have $$ \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\int_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} |S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y)g_1(y))|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\int_{X} |S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y)g_1(y))|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_2^2 $$ By \Cref{adjoint-tree-control} we now estimate: $$ \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}(2^{182a^3})^2 \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1\|_2^2 $$ By pairwise disjointedness of the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ for ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ (and writing out the definition of $L^2$-norms), we have $$ \le (2^{182a^3})^2 \|g_1\|_2^2 $$ Arguing similarly for $g_2$, we obtain the desired inequality.

nodes.name: expand over tree pairs
nodes.statement:
We have by \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and the triangle inequality that
    $$
        \left| \int T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g_1 \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^*g_2} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|
    $$
    $$
        \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \left| \int T^*_{{\mathfrak T}_j({\mathfrak u})} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g_1) \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak T}_{j'}({\mathfrak u}')} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')} g_2)} \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Expand over pairs of trees.

nodes.name: separated trees
nodes.statement_short: Apply correlation of separated trees.

nodes.name: bound via S_2 square functions
nodes.statement: 2^{512a^3-4n} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}} \|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}'} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')}g_2)\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')\cap{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}))}\,.
nodes.label: eq-S2uu'

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz in the two sums.

nodes.name: write g_1 factor
nodes.statement_short: Write out the g_1 factor.

nodes.name: disjointness in u'
nodes.statement:
By pairwise disjointedness of the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ for ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_{j'}$, we have
    $$
        \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\int_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} |S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y)g_1(y))|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
        \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\int_{X} |S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y)g_1(y))|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)
    $$
    $$
       = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}\|S_{2,{\mathfrak u}} (\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1)\|_2^2
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness over u'.

nodes.name: adjoint tree control
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{adjoint-tree-control} we now estimate:
    $$
        \le \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j}(2^{182a^3})^2 \|\mathbf{1}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}g_1\|_2^2
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply adjoint tree control.

nodes.name: disjointness in u
nodes.statement:
By pairwise disjointedness of the sets ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ for ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j$ (and writing out the definition of $L^2$-norms), we have
    $$
        \le (2^{182a^3})^2 \|g_1\|_2^2
    $$
    Arguing similarly for $g_2$, we obtain the desired inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness over u; same for g_2.

nodes.name: row support E_j
nodes.statement:
Define for $1 \le j \le 2^n$
$$
    E_j := \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak p})\,.
$$

nodes.name: disjoint row support
nodes.statement_short: The sets E_j of distinct rows are pairwise disjoint.
conclusions: The sets $E_j$, $1 \le j \le 2^n$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.statement: The sets $E_j$, $1 \le j \le 2^n$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.label: disjoint-row-support

nodes.name: Proof of disjoint row support
nodes.statement_short: If x lies in E(p)∩E(p') for tiles of different trees, forest5 separates their frequencies, so Omega(p) and Omega(p') are disjoint, a contradiction.
nodes.statement:
Suppose that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}')$ with ${\mathfrak u} 
e {\mathfrak u}'$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}) \cap E({\mathfrak p}')$. Suppose without loss of generality that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Then $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{forest5}, it follows that $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. $$ By the triangle inequality. \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{forest1} it follows that  egin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) &\ge d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) - d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &> 2^{Z(n+1)} - d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &\ge 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4\,. \end{align*} Since $Z \ge 3$ by \eqref{defineZ}, it follows that ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}') 
otin B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 1)$, so $\Omega({\mathfrak p}') 
ot\subset \Omega({\mathfrak p})$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. Hence, by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, $\Omega({\mathfrak p}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}') = \emptyset$. But if $x \in E({\mathfrak p}) \cap E({\mathfrak p}')$ then $Q(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}')$. This is a contradiction, and the lemma follows.

nodes.name: assume common point
nodes.statement: Suppose that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}')$ with ${\mathfrak u} \ne {\mathfrak u}'$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}) \cap E({\mathfrak p}')$. Suppose without loss of generality that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a common point of E(p), E(p') for different trees; WLOG s(p) <= s(p').

nodes.name: cube inclusion
nodes.statement: Then $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.statement_short: I(p) lies in I(u').

nodes.name: forest5 separation
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{forest5}, it follows that
    $$
        d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: forest5 gives separation from Q(u').

nodes.name: separation of p and p'
nodes.statement_short: Q(p) and Q(p') are far apart.

nodes.name: disjoint frequency cubes
nodes.statement: Since $Z \ge 3$ by \eqref{defineZ}, it follows that ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}') \notin B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 1)$, so $\Omega({\mathfrak p}') \not\subset \Omega({\mathfrak p})$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. Hence, by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, $\Omega({\mathfrak p}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}') = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence Omega(p), Omega(p') are disjoint.

nodes.name: contradiction
nodes.statement: But if $x \in E({\mathfrak p}) \cap E({\mathfrak p}')$ then $Q(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}')$. This is a contradiction, and the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with x in both E's.

nodes.name: Proof of forest operator
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the forest into rows; bound the diagonal by the row bound and off-diagonal by row correlation for the L^2 estimate; use disjoint row supports for the density estimate; interpolate.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp*}, we have for each $j$ $$ T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g = T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\,. $$ Hence, by \Cref{forest-row-decomposition} and the triangle inequality, $$ \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}} g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\right\|_2^2 $$ $$ = \int_X \left|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu $$ $$ \le \sum_{j=1}^{2^n} \|T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2 + \sum_{j =1}^{2^n} \sum_{\substack{j' = 1\\j' \ne j}}^{2^n} \left| \int_X \overline{ T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g} T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_{j'}} g \right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,. $$ We use \Cref{row-bound} to estimate each term in the first sum, and \Cref{row-correlation} to bound each term in the second sum: $$ \le 2^{566a^3-n} \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2 + 2^{876a^3-4n}\sum_{j=1}^{2^n}\sum_{j' = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2 \|\mathbf{1}_{E_{j'}}g\|_2\,. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz in the second two sums, this is at most $$ 2^{876a^3} (2^{-n} + 2^{n}2^{-4n}) \sum_{j = 1}^n \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2\,, $$ and by disjointedness of the sets $E_j$, this is at most $$ 2^{877a^3 - n} \|g\|_2^2\,. $$ Taking square roots, it follows that for all $g$ \begin{equation} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{439a^3-\frac{n}{2}} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation} On the other hand, we have by disjointedness of the sets $E_j$ from \Cref{disjoint-row-support} and the triangle inequality $$ \left\|\mathbf{1}_G \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\right\|_2^2 \le \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\|_2^2 \le \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\|_2^2\,. $$ Now with $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$ and \Cref{row-bound} we obtain $$ \| \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2^2 = \left| \int_X \overline{\mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f} T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f} \mathbf{1}_F f \right| $$ $$ \le \|f\|_2 \| \mathbf{1}_F T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2 \le 2^{283a^3-n/2} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \| \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2 \|f\|_2. $$ Dividing this last inequality by the finite $\| \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2$, substituting back and taking square roots we get $$ \left\|\mathbf{1}_G \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right\|_2 \le 2^{283a^3} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{\frac{1}{2}} 2^{-\frac{n}{2}} (\sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|f\|_2^2)^{\frac{1}{2}} $$ \begin{equation} = 2^{283a^3} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{\frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} \Cref{forest-operator} follows by taking the product of the $(2 - \frac{2}{q})$-th power of \eqref{eq-forest-bound-1} and the $(\frac{2}{q} - 1)$-st power of \eqref{eq-forest-bound-2}.

nodes.name: localise to E_j
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{definetp*}, we have for each $j$
    $$
        T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^*g = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_j} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g = T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Each row operator only sees g on E_j.

nodes.name: expand square
nodes.statement:
Hence, by \Cref{forest-row-decomposition} and the triangle inequality,
    $$
        \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}} g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} g\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\right\|_2^2
    $$
    $$
        = \int_X \left|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} T^*_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\right|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu
    $$
    $$
        \le \sum_{j=1}^{2^n} \|T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2 + \sum_{j =1}^{2^n} \sum_{\substack{j' = 1\\j' \ne j}}^{2^n} \left| \int_X \overline{ T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_j} g} T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j'}}^* \mathbf{1}_{E_{j'}} g \right| \, \mathrm{d}\mu\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Expand the square into diagonal and off-diagonal terms.

nodes.name: row bound and correlation
nodes.statement:
We use \Cref{row-bound} to estimate each term in the first sum, and \Cref{row-correlation} to bound each term in the second sum:
    $$
        \le 2^{566a^3-n} \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2 + 2^{876a^3-4n}\sum_{j=1}^{2^n}\sum_{j' = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2 \|\mathbf{1}_{E_{j'}}g\|_2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound terms by row bound and row correlation.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and disjointness
nodes.statement:
By Cauchy-Schwarz in the second two sums, this is at most
    $$
        2^{876a^3} (2^{-n} + 2^{n}2^{-4n}) \sum_{j = 1}^n \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} g\|_2^2\,,
    $$
    and by disjointedness of the sets $E_j$, this is at most
    $$
        2^{877a^3 - n} \|g\|_2^2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz and disjoint E_j.

nodes.name: first estimate
nodes.statement_short: Get the L^2 forest bound.

nodes.name: forest L^2 bound
nodes.statement: \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{439a^3-\frac{n}{2}} \|g\|_2\,.
nodes.label: eq-forest-bound-1

nodes.name: disjoint supports
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, we have by disjointedness of the sets $E_j$ from \Cref{disjoint-row-support} and the triangle inequality
    $$
        \left\|\mathbf{1}_G \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f\right\|_2^2 = \left\|\sum_{j=1}^{2^n} \mathbf{1}_{E_j} \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\right\|_2^2 \le \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_{E_j} \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\|_2^2 \le \sum_{j = 1}^{2^n} \|\mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_{j}} f\|_2^2\,.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint row supports split the G-restricted operator.

nodes.name: TT* argument
nodes.statement:
Now with $|f| \le \mathbf{1}_F$ and \Cref{row-bound} we obtain
    $$
        \| \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2^2 = \left| \int_X \overline{\mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f} T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f} \mathbf{1}_F f \right|
    $$
    $$
        \le \|f\|_2 \| \mathbf{1}_F T_{\mathfrak{R}_j}^* \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2 \le 2^{283a^3-n/2} \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}}{\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \| \mathbf{1}_G T_{\mathfrak{R}_j} f \|_2 \|f\|_2.
    $$
nodes.statement_short: TT* argument with the row density bound.

nodes.statement_short: Get the density forest bound.

nodes.name: Lipschitz Holder approximation
nodes.statement_short: A $C^\tau$ function supported in a ball is approximated within $(t/2)^\tau$ by a Lipschitz function with Lipschitz norm $\lesssim t^{-1-a}$.
assumptions: Let $\varphi: X \to \mathbb{C}$ be a function supported in the ball
conclusions: There exists a function $\tilde \varphi : X \to \mathbb{C}$, supported in $B(z,2R)$, such that for every $x\in X$
nodes.statement: Let $z\in X$ and $R>0$. Let $\varphi: X \to \mathbb{C}$ be a function supported in the ball $B:=B(z,R)$ with finite norm $\|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}$. Let $0<t \leq 1$. There exists a function $\tilde \varphi : X \to \mathbb{C}$, supported in $B(z,2R)$, such that for every $x\in X$ \begin{equation} |\varphi(x) - \tilde \varphi(x)| \leq (t/2)^{\tau} \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z,2R))} \end{equation}and \begin{equation} \|\tilde \varphi\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(B(z,2R))} \leq 2^{4a}t^{-1-a} \|\varphi\|_{C^{\tau}(B(z,2R))}\, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of the Lipschitz Holder approximation lemma
nodes.statement_short: Mollify $\varphi$ by averaging against the Lipschitz tent kernel $L(x,y)$ of radius $tR$; the doubling condition bounds the normalization from below.
nodes.statement: Define for $x,y\in X$ the Lipschitz and thus measurable function \begin{equation} L(x,y) := \max\{0, 1 - \frac{\rho(x,y)}{tR}\}\, . \end{equation} We have that $L(x,y)\neq 0$ implies \begin{equation} y\in B(x, tR)\, . \end{equation} We have for $y\in B(x, 2^{-1}tR)$ that \begin{equation} |L(x,y)|\ge 2^{-1} \ . \end{equation} Hence \begin{equation} \int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\ge 2^{-1}\mu(B(x, 2^{-1}tR))\, . \end{equation} Let $n$ be the smallest integer so that \begin{equation} 2^n t\ge 1\, . \end{equation} Iterating $n+2$ times the doubling condition \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain \begin{equation} \int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\ge 2^{-1-a(n+2)}\mu(B(x, 2R))\, . \end{equation} Now define $$ \tilde \varphi(x) := \left(\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^{-1}\int L(x,y) \varphi(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\, . $$ Using that $\varphi$ is supported in $B(z,R)$ and \eqref{eql01}, we have that $\tilde{\varphi}$ is supported in $B(z,2R)$. We prove \eqref{eq-firstt}. For any $x\in X$, using that $L$ is nonnegative, \begin{equation} \left(\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right) |\varphi(x) - \tilde \varphi(x)| \end{equation} \begin{equation} = \left| \int L(x,y)(\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right|\, . \end{equation} Using \eqref{eql01}, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le \int_{B(x, tR)} L(x,y)|\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\, .\end{equation} We claim that in this integral, $|\varphi(x) - \varphi(y)|\le \rho(x,y)^\tau \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}(2R)^{-\tau}$. Indeed, if $x$ or $y$ does not belong to $B(z, 2R)$, then the other point is not in $B(z,R)$ as $\rho(x,y)\le tR \le R$. Therefore, $\varphi(x)=\varphi(y)=0$ since $\varphi$ is supported in $B (z, R)$. Otherwise, both points are in $B(z, 2R)$, and the inequality follows from the definition of $\|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}$. Therefore, we can estimate the last display further by \begin{equation} \le \left(\int_{B(x, tR)} L(x,y) \rho(x,y)^\tau \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)\|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}(2R)^{-\tau}\, . \end{equation} Using the condition on the domain of integration to estimate $\rho(x,y)$ by $tR$ and then expanding the domain by positivity of the integrand, we estimate this further by \begin{equation} \le \left(\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right) \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))} (t/2)^{\tau} \, . \end{equation} Dividing the string of inequalities from \eqref{eql1} to \eqref{eql5} by the positive integral of $L$ proves \eqref{eq-firstt}. We turn to \eqref{eq-secondt}. For every $x\in X$, we have \begin{equation} \left|\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right||\tilde{\varphi}(x)| =\left|\int L(x,y) {\varphi}(y)\, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left|\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right| \sup_{x'\in X} |{\varphi}(x')|\ . \end{equation} As $\varphi$ is supported on $B$, dividing by the integral of $L$, we obtain \begin{equation} |\tilde{\varphi}(x)|\le \sup_{x'\in B} |{\varphi}(x')|\le \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\ . \end{equation} If $\rho(x,x')\ge R$, then we have by the triangle inequality \begin{equation} R\frac{|\tilde{\varphi}(x') - \tilde \varphi(x)|}{\rho(x,x')} \le 2\sup_{x''\in X} |\tilde{\varphi}(x'')|\le 2\|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\, . \end{equation} Now assume $\rho(x,x')< R$. For $y\in X$ we have by the triangle inequality and a two fold case distinction for the maximum in the definition of $L$, \begin{equation} |L(x,y) - L(x',y)| \le \frac{\rho(x,x')}{tR}. \end{equation} We compute with \eqref{eql10}, first adding and subtracting a term in the integral, \begin{equation} \left(\int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right) |\tilde{\varphi}(x') - \tilde \varphi(x)|= \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left|\int L(x,y) \tilde{\varphi}(x') -L(x,y) \tilde{\varphi}(x) +L(x',y) \tilde{\varphi}(x')- L(x',y) \tilde{\varphi}(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right|\,. \end{equation} Grouping the second and third and the first and fourth term, we obtain using the definition of $\tilde \varphi$ and Fubini, \begin{equation} \le \left| \int (L(x',y)-L(x,y)) \varphi(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \left| \int L(x,y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)-\int L(x',y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right||\tilde{\varphi}(x')| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2 \int |L(x,y) -L(x',y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\, , \end{equation} where in the last inequality we have used \eqref{eql42}. Using further \eqref{eql10} and the support of $L$, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation}\le 2 \frac{\rho(x,x')} {tR}\mu(B(x,tR)\cup B(x',tR)) \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\, . \end{equation} Using $\rho(x,x')<R$ and the triangle inequality, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation}\le 2 \frac{\rho(x,x')} {tR} \mu(B(x,2R)) \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\, . \end{equation} Dividing by the integral over $L$ and using \eqref{eql32} and \eqref{2nt1}, we obtain \begin{equation} \frac {R |\tilde{\varphi}(x') - \tilde \varphi(x)|}{\rho(x,x')} \le 2^{2+a(n+2)}t^{-1}\|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))} \le 2^{2+3a} t^{-1-a} \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(z, 2R))}\, . \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eql52} and \eqref{eql226} using $a\ge 4$ and $t\le 1$ and adding \eqref{eql42} proves \eqref{eq-secondt} and completes the proof of \Cref{Lipschitz-Holder-approximation}.

We prove \eqref{eq-firstt}.
